EXTREMELY DECEPTIVE & DISAPPOINTING SERVICE!

When we were seated, our waitress, Veronica, aggressively pushed us to order excessive amounts of crab, repeatedly insisting on at least 4kg, dangling “2 flavours” as an incentive. When we clearly stated we only wanted 1kg because we were ordering multiple other dishes, she flatly refused several times and said the smallest portion was 2kg. After continued pressure, we reluctantly agreed to 2kg only after explicitly pointing to and requesting the Sri Lankan crab on the menu and specifically NOT the other option, Alaskan crab. This was what we agreed to when we asked her to repeat the order back to us.

When the bill arrived, we were shocked to see we were charged for Alaskan crab instead, at double the price, totaling $536 for crab alone and $757 overall. At no point was this change explained or confirmed, despite us being very explicit about what we wanted.

When we calmly raised the issue, Veronica became dismissive and defensive, refused to acknowledge any mistake, and claimed we “should have known” what crab we were served when it arrived at the table. That argument is completely unreasonable. Please see photo attached, how is a customer, especially tourists, supposed to visually identify the species of a cooked crab? If even restaurant staff don’t clearly explain it, why would a customer assume or accuse the restaurant that they are being served something different from what they ordered? When we said this to her in person she had no response except repeating that we should have known when we saw the crab.

Veronica claimed to speak multiple languages and spoke to us in both English and Cantonese, yet somehow failed to clarify this crucial detail in either language. That does not feel accidental, it feels intentional. No solution was offered, no accountability taken. We ultimately paid under pressure, simply to avoid causing a scene in front of other diners while she and another staff member went in circles with us getting nowhere in understanding the principal of lack of service and clear intentional upsell, we were trying to get across to them.

Prices are already high, but misleading customers and refusing responsibility is unacceptable. After reading other low reviews, it’s clear this is not an isolated incident and that management will not offer support.

Avoid this restaurant. And if you do dine here, do not let Veronica pressure or manipulate your order.

I intend to report this incident to CASE and the Singapore Tourism Board.

author: Yemima Giovany
review_text:
“Perfect Riverside Dining Experience”
I had an incredible dinner here! The ambiance is unbeatable – dining right next to the river with the city skyline glowing in the background was just magical. The chili crab was hands down the best I’ve ever had, and the black pepper prawns were juicy and flavorful. Service was attentive but not overbearing. Highly recommend this place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Singaporean seafood in a beautiful setting. Thank you to Auntie Veronica for the best service 😇🙏

author: Y KN
review_text:
Lunch menu's easy on the wallet with a gorgeous Singapore River view. Expect crowds at lunch hour - reserve ahead.

Bonus: outdoor seating's pet-friendly 🐶🌟

author: Raylz
review_text: Absolutely yummy and beautiful. Great service  great location

author: JhaySeph Dela Cruz
review_text: This place is a must-visit. From the friendly service to the delicious chili crab, everything was spot on—plus a great view at a great price! ♥️

author: KC
review_text: Lovely dining location right by the river. The food was very delicious - we had the black pepper crab and it was great. Attentive staff with helping us keep our tables clean. The lady who assisted us with ordering was a little bit much (recommending expensive dishes) and the cocktails were quite sweet. Other than that it was a good experience.

author: ng vivian
review_text: This place knows how to do King Crab right! The chilli sauce had the perfect balance of heat and sweetness, and the crab was incredibly fresh and juicy. We loved the generous portion size and the rich, savory flavor of the sauce. Don’t forget to order the mantou — it’s the best way to enjoy every bit of that amazing sauce. Highly recommended for seafood lovers.

author: Edmar Monteroso
review_text: The Alaskan King Crab "Emperor's Treasure" is always the top favorite of our family! we have tried this several times already. 🥰 always so worth it 👍 The crab meat is fresh, delicious, and firm-- no trace of fishiness, just pure flavor. The seasoning and sauce enhanced the natural taste without overpowering it. This is always the highlight of our dinner. The serving is always generous and beautifully presented. a must try by all locals and tourists! we will definitely still come back and order the same! 👍👍

author: Phai Dip
review_text:
Had excellent service here from
Veronica. The food was great and the atmosphere was top notch.

author: Kian
review_text: Went there for drinks last night and every single drink was amazing!! Especially recommend the ecstasy stunner!! My friend also lost his necklace at the restraunt and they found it and kept it safe till we were able to come back. Highly recommend!!

author: Jing Xuan Ong
review_text: Food is cheap (can have a set meal below $10 even with GST) and the set meal comes with drink, soup, salad, desert which is very generous. Place is quiet and cozy and there are usually empty tables so it is easy to talk. Highly recommend.

author: Halle Warne
review_text: This place was incredible! The service and drinks was something i very much enjoyed and would go back again 100%. Definitely recommend, the cocktails were to die for!!

author: Liz Gorman
review_text: Seafood so fresh it moved before we ate it. Lovely mama cooked the best lobster Thermidor and spider crab

author: Austin Seck
review_text: Great lunch deals here, I thought the food was cooked really well as well. Very value for money.

author: Jo
review_text: Recently dined at Segar and tried several dishes including the Hong Kong noodles, hor fun, cockles fried kway teow, three eggs royal spinach, fu rong egg, lemon chicken, and Thai-style chicken. The food doesn’t taste as good as before. Flavours were lacking, and the overall experience felt disappointing. Staff didn’t come across as very friendly either. The place was surprisingly quiet for a weekend, which felt a bit unusual.

author: Mark Lim
review_text:
Segar@Chinatown – A Second Date with Zi-Char Comfort

Second round at Segar@Chinatown Point and it didn’t disappoint. Nestled on Basement 2, this Halal zi-char spot remains a go-to for good portions, wallet-friendly prices, and consistently hearty flavours.

For this visit, we polished off a couple of comfort classics:
• Seafood E-Mee: Springy e-meng noodles enveloped in a savoury, umami-packed seafood broth—perfectly slurpable and deeply satisfying.
• Beef Fried Rice, plus an extra egg: generous, golden-fried rice with tender beef slices and that extra egg yolk melding through each grain with a rich, glossy finish. A heaping portion for just about S$6.70 especially good bang for your buck￼.
• A shared A&W Root Beer to wash it all down—a fizzy hit of nostalgia that caps the meal perfectly  .

First-time takeaway? The dark seafood Hokkien mee made it back for our “first lamppost at home” dinner later—rich in wok hei, peppery, saucy, and just begging for an extra squirt of chili.

#SegarAtChinatown #ChinatownPoint #SingaporeEats #ZiCharLove #TzeChar #FoodieSG #SgFoodie #EatbookSG #SgFood #FoodieAdventures #HalalEatsSG #SingaporeFoodies #WokHei #FoodstagramSG #SgFoodDiary #LocalEatsSG #BeefFriedRice #SeafoodEMee #HokkienMeeLove #FoodieLifeSG

author: boub bou
review_text: Great portion for the price, and the food came really fast. Really love the claypot golden chicken from here, one of the best chicken menu i ever had! Will come back for the curry fish head next time.

author: Patrick Yu
review_text: Again patronised Segar for my Elder Sis her 60th Birthday on Sat 6 Sep. This year She requested something more local cuisine, reasonable price and Cozy ambience especially. Nevertheless, Segar has never disappointed my family and myself. The dishes maintained the usual standard and some were even better than usual time. The service rendered by the Service Crew was warmed and homely. That's one of reasons why we always have Segar as our first choice. Thank you Segar for "being" our family's "private" kitchen in past years. 😜😜😜 Well Done 👏👏👏👏👏

author: taeyeon
review_text: Food is usually good however today was terrible, stingray smelled so bad we couldn't even eat it. I hope you guys do a thorough check on the food that you serve as this was a really huge disappointment for me today.

author: Jon Wan
review_text: Wide variety of menu. They have set combinations too. Halal. Digital order and payment. Polite staff. Spacious and comfortable seating

author: N. Gan
review_text:
We dined at Segar Restaurant today, a Halal-certified eatery we frequently visit. This restaurant offers great value with its $33.80 set meals for 2. We selected cereal prawns as our main dish, accompanied by minced chicken tofu, chye sim with garlics, two glasses of refreshing lemon juice, and two plates of white rice. Their assam fish is a must-have for us, so we added it to our meal as always.

What stood out once again was the exceptional service provided by an elderly server, Guek Hua who greets everyone with a warm, familiar smile. Her passion for serving diners is evident in the way she attentively observes their needs and spontaneously offers assistance. I was particularly impressed by her agility and skill in carrying 4 to 5 plates at a time, effortlessly serving each table with grace. Her dedication truly enhances the dining experience, making every visit enjoyable.

author: Jaslyn Lau
review_text:
I was with my family for dinner. The staff informed us that this place is halal. I was informed that there is 5% discount for self ordering through QR and joining as a member, hence I did. I initially preferred to order through the staff directly to save the hassle.

One thing that upset me was that when I asked the staff for help us take a group photo, 2 of them rejected me as they said their hands are dirty. They didn't even come back to assist. A third staff came and help but grumbled when we informed that we prefer the photo to be taken from outside as it looks better. I feel most of the servers are not that service oriented.

Food wise, it was ok but tastes different compared to non halal Chinese food so the elders didn't enjoy as much but still quite tasty.

author: JY
review_text: One of my family’s go-to places for casual family dinners in a comfortable environment. The fish head curry & prawn paste chicken are our favourite dishes from this place. So far everything that we’ve ordered over the years have been good, and the prices are affordable as well. Highly recommended!

author: Bunny Sammm
review_text: Having dinner here at Chinatown outlet. Been here for few times. The food is average sometimes salty. Usually the staff are quite friendly. However, today one of the staff is kinda rude when asking for cutlery she give my an annoyed expression.  After a meal I was request a refill hot water for my tea. As I came here before I know  can refill once. She sounds so much rude and confrontational said only can refill once. Just wanna to ask are u ok seriously??? If you’re not happy can take leave or rest at home please don’t ruin customer mood like this. We are paying money not to suffer by ur attitude tho.

author: Javier Tan
review_text: Legitimately surprised by this shop! Felt that it may not be as delicious but after eating, the price point and the dishes did not disappoint! We came here with a large group and everyone was satisfied with the food!

author: Ame
review_text:
Ordered the value set:
- Oyster with egg was good
- Sambal kang kong was good
- Cereal prawn was ok, cereal was good
- Extra ordered hotplate tofu which was not bad too.
- Finally curry fish head, abit disappointed as the taste wasn't as good as our last few visits. The curry gravy was more bland than before.

Overall, it was still good for us. Value for money too.

author: Bylur Xu
review_text:
Homely spot. Nice halal place to hangout with my Malay pal in the midst of nots when we happen to be in the area.

Service was from a crew of senior ladies who were pretty friendly and gladly shared their views from questions we asked. And perhaps appetites have shrunken, the spread of two mains and two sides had us filled to the brim.

Food wasn’t the most flavourful that you know they scream msg and artificial flavourings in it, but was nice. Just nice. Wouldn’t mind to be here again if I happen to be area the area.

author: Pei Leng Tho
review_text: Nice dishes. We are in a group of 10 and we ordered 2 set meals. Dishes are yummy not salty or oily.

author: KWRER
review_text:
Went to Segar chinatown outlet for lunch, around 12 noon on 7 October, an older waitress serve my dish (kway tiao cockles) to wrong table 2 times + 1 time wrong dish with chilli (belonged to the table next to me) *Total 3 times error in a row.

I had to repeatedly ask where's my dish because i waited 30 minutes for my dish.

At last , my dish came. Quality was so-so because it was rushed out by the cook. All because the waitress messed up. Server had a black face with no apologies given.

We overheard the aunty waitress replying to the manager ' serve wrong so what..' in chinese when confronted on the mistake.

Not sure whether the older aunty waitress has dementia or simply lack of EQ and training. I need to feedback this because it can affect the reputation of the company if this kind of attitude is continued without consequences.

author: khrhms
review_text: Good set meal for 4-5 persons worth $118+ after GST. Comes with curry fish head. Dishes are average but for the price, good for sharing. Fuss free meal. Dishes comes out after about 10mins of ordering via the QR code. Efficient. Came for late lunch and there were plenty of tables available. Halal. Located at b2 of Chinatown Point.

author: Adriel T
review_text:
I actually enjoyed the food here. Popped by for a quick lunch which wasn't too quick being that my food took about 32 minutes to arrive. All I ordered was a plate of noodles..

It was otherwise a nice place to dine at that is also halal.

author: Jarot Wahyu Ardhi
review_text: Halal muslim owned restaurant.. nice and delicate flavour with acceptable prices..

author: Nope Thanks
review_text:
Sadly the food is only average. The problem is that the dishes are rushed in the cooking process. All the ingredients for great food are there, just not utilized well.

Perhaps it will taste better if you eat here after the lunch rush. Maybe. But if you plan on coming here to eat, try heading to their other locations.

Also the iced coffee is 3 in 1 coffee. Unbelievable.

author: Alisa Fellah
review_text:
I’ve been visiting Segar since I was a child, long before they moved from Bedok, even before the construction of Bedok Mall. It’s always been a family favourite, with their claypot golden chicken being a standout dish we’ve loved for years.

Recently, we visited their Chinatown Point location. After the original Bedok spot closed, this became our go-to for awhile before the West Coz Cafe was built, but I’m sad to say the quality of the Chinatown outlet has noticeably declined. While the food is still decent and better than many other halal options, it doesn’t quite match the high standard it once did.

For instance, the beef fried rice, which used to have a wonderful char and tender beef with crispy rice bits, now lacks that signature char. It’s still flavourful but missing that crispy edge that made it so special.

The claypot golden chicken, once a highlight, was also disappointing this time. The golden sauce, usually thick and sticky, was more runny, and the chicken pieces were tough and mostly boney. The sizzling effect and caramelised onions that used to be a treat were missing, and the dish wasn’t served hot enough.

On a positive note, the Nonya lady’s finger dish was excellent and maintained its quality. However, the pandan chicken was bland, lacking the aromatic pandan flavour, and the oat prawns, though buttery and sweet, were overcooked and dry.

If you’re near HarbourFront, I’d recommend trying the West Coz Cafe location, which offers a taste closer to the original Segar experience.

Overall, despite my critique, the food is still bloody good—just not quite up to the exceptional standard I remember from the old days. If you’re near HarbourFront, I’d recommend trying the West Coz Cafe location, which offers a taste closer to the original Segar experience. Unfortunately, the Chinatown Point branch didn’t quite meet expectations, so you might want to consider other options for an authentic Segar meal.

author: Savan
review_text:
After quite a long time away, we returned for lunch and were pleasantly surprised. The restaurant now feels more spacious, and the interior is noticeably cleaner, brighter, and more inviting than before.

We ordered the 2-person lamb set, which included sliced lamb, sliced pork, lamb chops, hand-pulled noodles, lamb tripe, a basket of vegetables, lamb meatballs, and tofu. We also added an extra portion of sliced lamb, garlic pork slices (蒜泥白肉), and two skewers of grilled pork belly. To top it off, we enjoyed their buy-3-get-1-free Harbin beer promotion.

Our choice of the lamb herbal soup base was excellent—lighter on the herbs compared to before, but also less salty and refreshingly free of MSG. The broth was clean and naturally sweet.

Every item in the lamb set was delicious and of high quality. The lamb chops, sliced lamb, and meatballs were especially outstanding—rich in flavor without being overly gamey. Lamb lovers will definitely appreciate it.

A special mention goes to the garlic pork slices, which were tender and packed with flavor. The grilled pork belly skewers were smoky, aromatic with cumin, and satisfyingly savory.

The staff were exceptionally polite, professional, and hospitable. All in all, a great dining experience that we highly recommend!

author: Sharon Lim
review_text:
Near Malay mosque and Indian temple, near Chinatown Mrt station.
For lamb lovers.
I didn't know what to order as it was my first time. The staff helped with mobile ordering and recommended 1 person hotpot. The soup was very nice and comforting for me.
The self made noodle taste nice when it's more cooked (near the end) in my opinion. Vegetables were nice especially the black fungus 银耳.
Tried the BBQ too, was ok. Prefer it to be meatier.
The staff are very attentive too, will refill/adjust heat etc., made the solo dining experience very pleasant.
Will order ala carte next time as I think I prefer cut boneless lamb meat to the rest but still appreciative of the recommendation.

author: Mikey Boy
review_text: The braised beef soup was a spicy delight that had just enough peppers to keep you on your toes and yet could be easily handled by a novice. Highly recommend a visit if you're staying in Chinatown.

author: Marek Dusza
review_text: From the moment we arrived, we felt genuinely welcomed. The staff were incredibly supportive with our order and made sure everything went smoothly. The food was absolutely delicious, and the atmosphere elevated the entire experience. Throughout our stay, the team consistently went above and beyond to make us feel comfortable and cared for.

author: hitomi ahmad
review_text: absolutely fantastic! The broth is rich and flavorful, with just the right balance of spice and depth. Ingredients are fresh, portions generous, and everything tastes authentic. The staff are attentive and welcoming, making the whole dining experience smooth and enjoyable. The cozy atmosphere adds to the charm, perfect for sharing a hearty meal with friends or family. Definitely one of the best hot pot spots in Singapore — I’ll be coming back for sure!

author: S T
review_text:
Tried the Sauerkraut beef noodles - the broth is tasty and not too salty/overpowering. Light yet acidic but the ramen noodles were a little bland and floury. Ordered the lunch set $9.50 with drink - still quite value for money.

Also order the fry roasted mutton bun - it was amazing. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. Mutton was not gamey at all. Would go back for this!

author: Giovanni
review_text: Fantastic experience, the staff is so incredibly helpful and smiling, always present and never invasive. The lamb hotpot is to die for, not so spicy, just perfect balance. The meat is tender and flavorful, the quantity is big. Also the pork and the beef slices were nice, together with the vegetables. We also tasted lamb skewers (with cumin), chicken wings filled with shrimps (but we could not feel the shrimps), and the lamb pancake, amazingly crispy even if the lamb patty was too firm, probably not much fatty, and definitely the broth is the king of dinner, don't miss it.

author: Ayaalan.foodie
review_text:
Great first visit with warm service and authentic decor. The spicy lamb spine pot and collagen soup were flavorful and satisfying. Loved the beef tripe appetizer and tender lamb ribs. Refreshing dessert to end the meal.

Highly Recommended.

For more photos and details, check out @aya.yeaney (IG)
https://www.instagram.com/p/DF0IVS1p03e/?img_index=1

author: Joey H
review_text: We got the 2 pax lamb spine hot pot. Lamb tasted great, portion was huge for 2 persons, and the soup base was mildly spicy. Service could be more prompt though. Would come back again for the food.

author: 林谦颐Karen Lynne
review_text:
Friendly & kind staffs helped me, 1st time customer, got free membership & saved well.

The lambs are fresh & tender & juicy & very well cooked! Can’t make it at home that kinda pro quality! Really worth the price!

口水鸡 & 夫妻肺片 both are authentic & delicious, I ordered one more 夫妻肺片 as takeout!

Will definitely come again & try hot pot & noodles. Highly recommend.

author: Jacqueline Lee
review_text: We ordered the collagen soup based with lamb chops incl grilled ones. We had divided preference for both and dessert come free w every hotpot ordered. The bamboo shoots will hv to cook slightly longer otherwise it'll be too hard. Overall, the experience is good.

author: alena lim
review_text: Visited on a weekday 8pm, ordered the $59.90 set for 2 (price after member discount before gst & svc charge), after the relevant charges, bill was about $72. For this price point, I expected better service (at least for staffs to replenish "unlimited" items included in the set / offer to refill soup base). However, the supposed set inclusive unlimited sauces, and osmanthus jelly were all not replenished (the osmanthus jelly was literally completely empty from the time we went to take sauces til the time we wanted to take dessert LOL) and no form of apology was given... Mind you, you're paying for this 'unlimited dessert'! Disappointing experience for a 4.9 stars rated restaurant, staff even tried to upsell the store credit promo, haha, no way am i returning! 🙄

author: Hui Ting Ho
review_text: Exceptional service, exceptional food, exceptional ambience. The smell of mutton and spices hits you once you enter the restaurant. A great place for mutton lovers. A restaurant with one of the best service ever!!! Better than many high end restaurants. Staff would provide a hot towel to warm your hands once you’re seated. They would give suggestions to the food to order and would promptly replace our plates with new ones. We have a baby with us, and the staff would switch on the lights to the unopened area of the restaurant to let our baby look at the fish to entertain him. This is the restaurant where my baby is willing to sit on the high chair for the longest time! Likely because the chair is comfy. Staff would also try to entertain him and even gave him a stuffed toy as a gift! Would definitely come back again and highly recommended!!

author: Mun Jun Yong
review_text: If you are looking for delicious lamb skewers, soup, pancake, noodles, and everything lamb, you've found the right place. The food is absolutely yummy and the service amazing with great attentive staffs in a comfortable environment. Worth every penny!

author: Olive橄榄廖
review_text:
Love the spacious tables and seats. Very detail design in the restaurant

Food
We had BBQ and steamboat.

Love the mutton base soup. Love the mutton and chicken skewers.

The rest of the food are normal.

Service was good too, very attentive and friendly.

And of the meal, they even offered dessert.  We went there during lunch and ate from noon to 3pm.  Great for gathering.

Would go back again alone just to try their single pot..

author: Victor
review_text:
I had one of the best hot pot experiences at Chuang Yang Ji. It's such a lovely restaurant with mutton related hotpot, ingredients and ala carte dishes.

The mutton skewer is definitely a must order. Spiced version isn't super spicy, good for everyone. Tender lamb with generous portions of spices, eat it while it's still hot.

We had the lamb collagen set which comes with a ton of ingredients. Our favourite was the lamb meatballs, it's so springy and flavourful.
Second would be the lamb ribs, the meat still sticks to the bone but it's amazing.
Soupbase was great, it's light and easy to drink.

None of the mutton had a strong lamb signature smell but they all taste good.
Ingredients were fresh and portions were of a good size.

Staff service is excellent, comparable or better than HDL. The staff were cheerful and seemed happy working here. It was easy to get attention. They even helped scoop out the floating scum without us prompting them.

Dining environment was clean and spacious, our clothes didn't smell too much of steamboat after. Aircon was cold enough, didn't break a sweat.

There was a good selection of condiments, their special chilli is pretty good.

Overall, a great experience here. Will definitely return in the future to here or their other outlets.

author: Jason Liaw
review_text:
First Visit, Impressive Experience!

Tried the lamb hotpot and collagen soup - absolutely delightful! The lamb meat and bone were tender and flavorful.

Staff were exceptionally helpful and polite, making our dining experience even more enjoyable.

Definitely recommend this place! 5/5 stars

author: Belles Marcial
review_text: The food at Chang Yang Ji was absolutely delicious! The staff (Apple) was incredibly friendly and attentive, and it was a great value for the quality of the food. The prices were reasonable too. It’s a perfect spot for families and circle of friends…

author: Shihao Foo
review_text:
Came here as my gf and I felt like having some clear mutton soup. I chose the noodles version while my gf chose soup + rice set. We both like what we got, but I preferred the meat in the noodles which was thinner and easier to chew.  Soup was clear nourishing. The staff has a phrase that they always repeat, about how the soup is good for the tummy (养胃). I’m not sure if it’s true, but it sure felt that way.

Total price was $30 which I felt was very value for money, considering the restaurant environment.

If you are wondering why the Google ratings is so high, I’ll let u in on a secret - the shop offers a small side dish for a 5 star Google review. That said, I’m writing this the day after my meal, so I’m not influenced in any way. The only downside I’ll say is that their ordering website is clunky and difficult to use, with errors when it came to payment, so we had to order through staff and pay at counter instead. But their staff’s service was good, so I’ll keep the 5-star rating.

author: Mr Yeo
review_text:
We came on a rainy Sunday. We ordered the lamb soup. This place is famous for their lamb and soup. Special thanks to Wei yang yang for the awesome service.

PS: previously they didn’t have the ice cream machine and now they have it. Nice desert after the meal.

author: randall
review_text:
Honestly quite good for kbbq! Didn't have much expectstions coming and we got the pork set. 73 bucks for 450g of meat with egg and soup. Quite worth for 2 big eaters of 3 small eaters.
The meat is obviously the star here. The kimchi tina soup was so so. Steamed egg is normal as usual. Got the upgraded double cheese but honestly not that worth. Hence 4 stars for food, so stick to the meats!
Service is damn good imo. Super friendly staff, even brought me for a mini tour to look see. Overall quite happy

author: Gabriel Ting
review_text:
Great service and great food!! Really fresh!!
Enjoyed the Meat and the Kimchi and Lettuce all great! Fresh and healthy

Check out the coconut ice cream very light after the meal. Yuzu ice cream will help clean the palate as well

author: Aaron Lee
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Absolutely loved the Korean BBQ here! The meat was fresh, beautifully marbled, and full of flavour. Every cut was perfectly presented, and the side dishes complemented the meal so well. The staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole dining experience even better. Paired it with some beer — just perfect! Definitely one of the best BBQ places I’ve tried. Highly recommended! 🔥🥩🍺

author: Bing Dun Tan
review_text:
I found my favourite kbbq place. Came here a couple of hours ago. The jap chae maybe a bit too much sauce but the noodle is very springy and q, like what I had in korea. Would suggest to lessen the dark sauce. Also, no cold noodle so it was one minor blemish.

That being said, the ajooma sets are great value. Comes with seafood (or beef) soup and the steam egg. Usually i dont take the steam egg coz most places make it too sweet or too bland. Here? A sweet (no pun intended) spot was hit.

All in all i will be back for sure in the near future.

author: Peini Chong
review_text: The restaurant had a great atmosphere.. Service was friendly. Meat quality was good and fried chicken was juicy.  We left feeling full and extremely satisfied.

author: Ling L
review_text: Authentic Korean BBQ experience! The meats and dishes are genuinely Korean, well-prepared, and full of flavour. Prices are very reasonable for the quality, and the ambience is great—comfortable and lively without being too noisy. Service was attentive and friendly, making the whole dining experience enjoyable. Definitely a place I’d return to & will try their fresh lobster next time!

author: Mike Chia
review_text:
Great food and we’re returning customers 👍 Love the selection of beef and pork — a good go-to place for meat lovers. My son especially loves their Jjajangmyeon. Overall, the menu items are pretty solid.

Only downside is parking, which is common for this area. Will still come back! 😊

author: Pui Yee
review_text: Great food and service! The quality of the meat is good and even the other dishes were delicious (steamed egg and kimchi soup). Will come back again! :)

author: Sakulrat Satayanan
review_text: Very friendly staff and Amazing service! Beef and pork belly is very tender and fresh too

author: Jolene Zhou
review_text: My 3rd visit to Ajoomma. Always a good time! Love the beef soup and seafood pancake. Don’t have to bbq on our own and service is always great. Looking forward to my next visit already!

author: Lily Fong
review_text:
Nice atmosphere, great staff services and meats are fresh and tender.
Will come back again!

author: Alwyn HoHo
review_text: Highly Recommend this place if you are planning to dine with your loved ones or with your colleagues. There is a KTV room for you to sing your heart out while you enjoy your Korean BBQ.

author: Tan Leddin
review_text: Very nice place! Food is great and the waiters are very friendly and helpful. Yap was especially helpful and always serving with a smile. Great place to celebrate a friend’s birthday. Ventilation is great so there is no smoky smell. Toilet is really clean as well. Awesome place to spend a Friday night with friends!!

author: Magdalene Ong
review_text: Chose this place because of the high reviews but was very disappointed. Got a beef and pork set but the meat was so bland and tasteless. Had to cook ourselves which I did not expect given the prices, as more upmarket kbbqs usually cook for you. Kimchi soup was like diluted kimchi water with shreds of pork. Overall it was $130++ which is reasonable for the amount of meat but not worth it for the taste and a very expensive unenjoyable meal overall.

author: Joseph Fong
review_text:
Meat was fresh n juicy.
Staff were friendly and attentive.

Recommended !!
Will revisit .

author: Mendi Sim
review_text: The food is very fresh and nice… the kimchi is very delicious… we went for the buffet which is very worth it..

author: viet hoang
review_text:
Good bbq (we ordered fresh pork set), tender chicken. The korean pancake is good too. Free flow banchan.
I rate this a 6/7 🫴🫴
Cleaned everything left no crumbs

author: Flo Yeow
review_text:
This is a very good Korean BBQ restaurant. The impeccable service, food quality, and overall vibes set it apart from other, more casual KBBQ spots in the area, making it an option you should try at least once.

While the extensive menu can be a little confusing compared to a traditional KBBQ place, it allows them to offer a wide range of premium ingredients like lobster and expensive meat cuts. We opted for a simple KBBQ set meal, which saved us the hassle of navigating the many pages.

I particularly appreciate that the team cooks everything for you and is quite patient throughout the process. We were able to relax and enjoy a wonderful evening of good conversations and delicious food.

author: Q w
review_text: We came with 6 pax and ordered 3sets of pork and beef , was extremely enough . The food was super delicious. Mr Ben and other staff who serviced us during the dinner  were very nice . Food, people , entertainment all made us a happy one. Would definitely come again and highly recommend!

author: Kurt Tan
review_text: Nice ambience with friendly and attentive staff. Food is decent and reasonably priced. Loved the kimchi and the generous side dishes. They even let us try the beers before ordering — great service all around!

author: Punto Dewa
review_text:
Maxwell Hawker Centre is absolutely one of the best places to enjoy local food in Singapore. The atmosphere is lively, busy, and full of great smells from every corner. We loved it so much that we ended up coming here twice during our Singapore trip.

We tried a bit of everything: Hainanese chicken rice, chili crab, chicken noodles, and a few other local dishes. Every stall had its own flavor and style, and the food was fresh, delicious, and very affordable.

It’s also a great place to sit, relax, and soak in the local vibe while enjoying good food. Lots of choices, fast service, and the energy of the crowd just adds to the experience.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Singapore. We’ll definitely come back next time!

author: Nickin Sitaram
review_text:
One of the best Hawkers in Singapore.

We planned this around being starving and making sure we researched which places to eat at.

The food was phenomenal. Everything comes out fresh and cooked to order. Nothing rewarmed.

It's a great hustle bustling vibe full of locals and tourists. The atmosphere is fun, fast and hot. Great to see all the stalls to see what they do and specialise in.

We ordered everything we researched and way too much for us. We had a lovely local lady sitting opposite us so we shared everything with her and she doggy bagged it all too.

This is a must place visit and again, none of us had any tummy issues even after eating like the world was coming to an end.

author: Kimberly Do
review_text:
Maxwell Food Centre is my favorite hawker center, and I always find myself coming back here. I usually stop by for the sugar cane drink, a coffee drink from the Vietnamese stall, and especially the fishball soup from Teochew Fishball Bak Chor Mee.

The line for the fishball soup is usually around 20 people, but it can easily take close to an hour. I’m not entirely sure why, and it does feel like it could be more efficient, but honestly, the soup is so good that it’s hard to complain. It’s rich, comforting, and incredibly satisfying.

Despite the wait, I’m always craving it and always end up coming back. Some places are just worth the time, and this is one of them.

author: M *
review_text:
This hawker center is conveniently located on top of the MRT, offering a variety of delicious food options. The famous chicken rice is highly recommended, but it’s worth noting that other chicken rice dishes are equally tasty. There are also many refreshing drinks, such as sugarcane with lemon.

One recent addition to the menu is chilli ban mian stall, which is a delightful dish featuring eggs, anchovies, fish balls, and prawn paste balls. While it may not be overly spicy, it’s well-made and worth trying. There are similar stall that also sell equally nice noodle and some dumpling.

Overall, this hawker center is a great place to explore local cuisine, with a wide range of dishes from Western to Eastern influences. It’s definitely worth visiting a few times to sample some of the delicious food.

Non aircon and can be warm during day time. Need to chop the table for sure as many tourist and local will visit.

author: SICILIAN-AMERICAN
review_text: This food court is smaller and more expensive than Chinatown complex. They also have fewer tables and fans. Not as many choice either but still worth going to if in the area. I got some good food here and it just a little more expensive. I got all this for $13 sgd ($10 usd)

author: Francis Ho
review_text:
Came her for early dinner before the crowd. Surprisingly many stalls were closed for vacation or rest.
Chanced upon this Malay food stall but run by a Chinese couple. The stall is called Alipapa briyani and Alimama.
I ordered the recommended Green chilli chicken rice ($7.50). The chicken thigh was over deep fried till the skin is almost black. Luckily the meat was still ok. Overall it was a nice plate of chicken rice but the green chilli wasn't outstanding. Couldn't taste the spiciness of the chilli.
23.11.25

author: Amanda
review_text:
📍Xi Duo Duo 喜多多, Maxwell Food Centre

🥟 𝑺𝒉𝒂𝒏 𝑫𝒐𝒏𝒈 𝑭𝒓𝒊𝒆𝒅 𝑫𝒖𝒎𝒑𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈𝒔 [$7]
loved the spr light & crispy crust— paired so well with the dumplings & gave it that extra satisfying crunch! 😩✨ each one was generously stuffed w minced meat & chives & the skin had js the right thickness!!

🍜 𝑩𝒆𝒊𝒋𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒁𝒉𝒂 𝑱𝒊𝒂𝒏𝒈 𝑵𝒐𝒐𝒅𝒍𝒆 [$5]
spr generous portion of noodles & minced meat!! noodles were well coated in that rich, savoury sauce once mixed & i rlly enjoyed this bowl till the v last bite 🥺

def cmg back the next time i visit maxwell food centre— but till then ill be thinking abt it 😌

author: Nhan Nguyen
review_text: Delicious and affordable food for tourist who prefer to just dive in then continue their trips. Fast service and seating area is clean. Most shops close at 9.pm

author: Fahriza Berliana
review_text: prices are affordable and it’s close to the MRT station. a bit hot and some spots could be cleaner, but can’t complain… overall it’s good! will definitely go back!

author: JR FF
review_text:
Spacious hawker center, somewhat built for tourists. More airflow than the typical hawker center, and therefore provides a more comfortable experience.

Really enjoyed the blurb about the hill (mount erskine) that used to be in the area, and how it was used to reclaim what now comprises the Central Business District. Showing Singaporeans the mighty works of our forefathers, and how we stand in an unbroken line of admirable people with significant and consequential deeds.

Home to a host of well known names, including the famous visit by the beloved Anthony Bourdian to Tian Tian Chicken Rice.

author: TwoSomeVoyage
review_text:
Visited Maxwell Food Centre looking for the famous chili crab at Stall 41, but it was closed until Christmas. Chili crab in Singapore is well known, but the popular places are pricey, so I was happy to explore hawker options instead.

Ended up eating at a chicken rice stall that usually has a long line—worth it. The chicken was tender, portions were just right, and the chili sauce is very spicy, so be careful. Cutlery comes one per bowl, and extras cost a small fee. Credit cards are accepted, which is convenient. Tried a Michelin-listed oyster dessert nearby—interesting to try once, though personally I prefer Korean-style oyster pancakes.

author: Lee
review_text: Got a rojak, tian tian chicken rice set (medium) and a hokkien noodles. Seats and tables are not very clean. Tian tian chicken rice stall had a queue. Service was prompt but the chicken rice was so-so only. The hokkien noodles did not appear like what was on the signboards of the store. Rojak was alright. Overall food was average.

author: Clive G
review_text: Maxwell Food Center is super easy to get to by train, which makes it perfect for a quick food stop. It’s located right opposite a beautiful Chinese museum, so you can soak in some culture before or after eating. Most of the food here is Chinese, and the must-try dish is definitely the chili crab—so tasty and full of flavor. It’s a great place to experience authentic local eats in a lively setting. Just note that it can be crowded with a wait time to get tables and the food

author: Paul Ciprian
review_text: A place where you can eat tasty and cheap Asian dishes. The offer is extremely varied, it's hard to decide what to choose. Very crowded, at certain times. The conditions are spartan, tables and chairs fixed to the floor, in some cases plastic cutlery, there are no napkins, the tables are not always clean. But it's worth a try.

author: Estela Duque
review_text:
I came to know this hawker centre in the mid-1990s while at my first job as professional in the Tanjong Pagar area. I ate here at least 2-3x per week for lunch, plus the occasional supper, when there was overtime work to be done.

This week I'm visiting 30 years later, it's now called Maxwell Food Centre and the whole area around it is completely different: new skyscrapers all around and an MRT station built in 2022. The 2001 renovation that changed it from a medium sized shed into +3,300 msq facility with more than 100 stalls, apparently cost SGD3.2M!

I'm very pleased to say the food stalls are still excellent quality, I had my fill of old favourites: black carrot cake, fried kway teow, and Hianese chicken rice.

If you're here for Tian Tian Hianese Chicken Rice with Michelin Bib Gourmand rating, it's better to come early rather than late. There's always a long queue at the stall, and they tend to run out of items late afternoon. When I came on Sunday at 18:00 there was none left of the lovely rice cooked in chicken broth or the roast chicken. So I was able to get steamed chicken only, served cold with warm brown sauce (the only downside of this visit).

author: Edmund Tan
review_text: One of our favorite hawker centers to enjoy Singaporean hawker fare with friends when they visit me and my wife in Singapore. Lots of good food like chicken rice, banh mi, fried carrot cake, rojak and popiah.

author: Renee W
review_text:
Great range of Hawker market stalls. Highly recommend Tian Tian chicken rice worth the queue although it does move quickly. Chicken was flavoursome, tender recommended getting the rice added and poached mixed plate.
Chendol dessert stall - do not recommend plate was $2.5 owner took $10 and did not give change. Ignored me when I questioned it added to which the desserts were not great.
Lovely older couple running the oyster omelette stall also recommend checking them out.

author: Joe Wheeler
review_text: We went to several food centres in Singapore and Maxwell was my favourite. The epicentre of Haikenese chicken rice. There is one place that has long queues but they are all the same - I tested. So don’t queue, support some other dude cooking chicken for almost no money.

author: Katie
review_text:
Delicious food stalls, very authentic and reasonably priced food all throughout.

You can get an assortment of all types of foods, cuisines, deserts and drinks. We ate here and a few other Maxwell's and preferred this, the Lau Pa Sat one is touristy and more uptown blackpool-fake feeling with chains and not locals. But good if you want one million flavours of overpriced satay sticks.

The food was delicious here. And very close to the station.

author: Yogesh G
review_text:
one of the best food centres in SG. must try items -
1. fried snacks (vegetarian stall)
2. beancurd rice balls with soy milk
3. xiao long bao
4. durian chendol
5. items at Market stall (at the entrance from Buddha temple side)
6. hainanese chicken rice
7. soybeancurd

author: Wiz Yeo
review_text:
We finally got to try the famous Kok Sen Restaurant, a spot that's always packed and comes with a Michelin Bib Gourmand reputation.

Overall, we had a very good and satisfying meal, with every dish being well-executed. It's definitely a top-tier zi char experience, though perhaps the Michelin hype set our expectations a little too high.

We ordered a wide spread, including their famous signature dishes. The Big Prawns Hor Fun was a clear standout, with a generous, silky, and flavourful egg gravy that was full of wok hei. The prawns were large and fresh. The Claypot Yong Tau Foo was also excellent; the stuffed items (eggplant, tofu, peppers) were delicious, and the rich, savoury claypot sauce was perfect over rice.

The other dishes were all classic and cooked to a high standard. The Crispy Roasted Chicken had paper-thin, crispy skin, and the Stir-fried Beef Hor Fun was loaded with tender beef. We also enjoyed the Prawn Rolls (Hei Zho) and a fluffy Fu Yong Omelette.

The service was exactly what you'd expect from a place that is perpetually this busy. It was highly efficient and fast-paced. While you can't really call it "friendly" in a warm or chatty sense, they were absolutely not unfriendly. They were professional, attentive enough, and got the job done.

Here's why it's a 4-star and not a 5-star for us: all the food was genuinely good and definitely above average, but we just couldn't pinpoint that special "Michelin" x-factor. It's fantastic, classic Cantonese zi char, but we weren't blown away in the way the reputation might suggest. That said, it's a solid, reliable, and delicious meal that I would still recommend.

author: OB1
review_text:
Kok Sen lives up to its Michelin reputation, drawing a noticeable crowd of tourists, but the wait time was manageable—we were seated within 20-30minutes ( we arrived at 6:50pm). They offer both indoor (air-conditioned) and outdoor seating, which is a nice option. ( If you come after 8 p.m., there is most probably no more queue.).

For our group, we ordered the Prawn Hor Fun (small $20), Beef Hor Fun (medium $14), Cereal Prawns, a fried vegetable dish, and Sliced Fish with Bittergourd, plus 5 barley waters, totaling around $109.

The Hor Fun dishes were the definite stars—incredibly smooth and executed perfectly. The Cereal Prawns were also excellent.

However, a couple of items were disappointing: The fried vegetable portion we ordered was quite small, almost comically so ("pathetic," as you said), and is definitely something we'd skip next time. The Sliced Fish with Bittergourd also didn't quite hit the mark; the flavors felt separate, as if the two main ingredients were cooked individually and tossed together, lacking that essential zichar harmony.

Despite these minor misses, the overall meal was satisfying, driven by the quality of their signature noodle dishes. I would certainly return for the Hor Fun.

author: Sassy Que
review_text: First visit to the Michelin guide restaurant… super long queue on a Friday evening. We ordered the signature prawn hor fun, claypot YTF, sweet & sour pork, fu Yong egg, roast chicken & 三色蛋贡菜. Overall a pleasant visit and the dishes were nice though on the salty side. #foodporn #sg #dinner

author: Bugwagen
review_text: Nice Zhi Char (stir fry)! We love the spicy big prawn hor fun.  It was delicious! The other dishes we ordered was just ok.  Didn’t know they have so many Michelin awards.  We managed to get a table outdoor, but there was a queue and everyone in the group has to be present before they let you have a table.

author: Jeremiah Su
review_text:
Really good after the Reno.

Insiders really noisy though as it’s enclosed and echoes quite a bit.

Food was amazing, albeit a little salty.

Would definitely return because their Hor Fun has wok hei taste, and super yummy!

author: Alex
review_text: You might need to queue up after 7 pm even on a weekday as this restaurant is quite popular. Seems like the big prawns hor fun is a popular dish there and so we ordered it. The small portion is actually good for 2 to 4 person (if you're ordering other dishes to share) and it came with 2 big prawns cut into half. The claypot yong tau fu is also good with lots of ingredient. 9% GST and a 3% service charge will be added to your bill.

author: Ming Wei Lee
review_text: Seen them from the pre-renovation cash only days until the current setup. Food is great albeit being slightly pricey even by Singapore standards. Place is packed and one way around the queue is to make a booking in advance but do arrive on time to respect the reservation. Also they can get quite chaotic at the counter and entrance area. Not sure why they design it that way as it's a huge bottleneck.

author: Serene Gan
review_text: Being their customer for years, service drop. 5pax then expect 1 of us to sit at the stool and share the table. Their Michelin stars is just for show, especially they just to earn more $ at lunch crowd. 4 dishes took 40min to serve, one by one. Food are yummy but the service already spoil the business. Noisy at lunch hours. Another restaurant down the road is much better and even have 10% discount when spend more than $80.

author: Paul Lim
review_text:
I really enjoyed my first visit here, so I came back tonight to celebrate my mum’s birthday. Unfortunately, it didn’t turn out as well as I’d hoped.

We wanted to order some of their signature dishes like yong tau fu and crispy chicken, but both were already sold out. I wonder why some signature dishes were already gone as early as 7.30pm. So we went with other items instead. The big prawn hor fun was tasty, though it lacked that wok hei fragrance. The kam heong chicken, which I’d tried before, was still just as good as I remembered. Apart from that, most of the other dishes were pretty ordinary. The vegetable dishes also lacked wok hei, the sweet and sour pork was average, and the crispy tofu tasted rather bland. The salted egg yolk prawns were over fried and turned out tough, while the curry fish head didn’t taste fresh as the meat wasn’t sweet at all.

To top it off, there was an issue with the bill. My mum had told the cashier we only opened one bottle of wine, but the bill showed two. The waitress agreed to refund $10, but she should have amended the bill straightaway. After we left, we realised the 3% service charge and 9% GST were still calculated based on two bottles instead of one.

Overall, it turned out to be a disappointing evening for what was meant to be a birthday celebration. A real letdown, especially when we came with high expectations.

author: Kian Hong Lim
review_text: One of the best Hor fun I ever eaten. Must try! Small portion for the big prawn noodle soup is huge, enough for 3 pax. Price is well worth as portion is big and ingredients used is quality and fresh. Gem in this area!

author: Steven Wong
review_text: A nice place for a good lunch with friends. Love their prawn horfan and fried frog legs. Should come with a bigger group to be able to try more dishes.

author: Supakij Khomvilai
review_text: Good Singaporean restaurant. Found it from review in YouTube and other recommendations somewhere. Our group of 13 people are really enjoyed our lunch there. We made a reservation through WhatsApp of the restaurant which is the easiest way to do and I recommend you to do it to secure your seating. Seating area are air conditioned. Every dish are really good, fresh ingredients and well cooked. Price are reasonable. Credit card accepted. Staffs are helpful. Enjoy!

author: yohanes kusika
review_text: It’s so good, no wonder they got the Michelin reputation. The hor fun is super nice!! All the food is very nice! Highly recommended!!

author: Piow Piow
review_text: Must make a reservation first to avoid long queue during peak hours. Overall tastes normal and on standard but not really impressive. Reasonable price and portion. The crews respond with be slow during peak hours.

author: Yvonne Chou
review_text:
I recently had lunch at Kok Sen Restaurant and it truly lived up to its reputation as one of Singapore’s classic zi char gems. I ordered the Claypot Yong Tau Foo, Bittergourd Black Bean Sauce Pork Ribs, Black Bean Beef Hor Fun, and a pot of Pu-Er Tea.

The standout dish for me was definitely the Bittergourd Black Bean Sauce Pork Ribs. The pork ribs were tender, juicy, and beautifully coated with a rich black bean sauce that was both savory and slightly smoky, pairing perfectly with the gentle bitterness of the gourd. It was comforting, homely, and full of wok hei.

The Claypot Yong Tau Foo was hearty and generous, with each piece absorbing the flavorful broth. The Black Bean Beef Hor Fun also impressed, the noodles had that irresistible charred aroma, and the beef was well-marinated and tender.

Service was brisk and efficient despite the busy lunch crowd, and dishes came out piping hot. Prices are on the higher side for zi char, but the quality, portion size, and authentic taste justify it.

If you’re looking for a taste of traditional Singapore zi char with bold flavors and wok hei, Kok Sen is a must visit.

author: Eren Erol
review_text: first of all, this is not a Michelin starred restaurant. They were only "mentioned" in the Michelin guide. And to be honest, there's nothing Michelin here. First of all it gets extremely busy during lunch hour in that small place. Some of the tables are for 8-9 people, and if you're not a big group you might be sitting with somebody else that you don't know. Prices are so cheap, and so the quality. when you take a look at the kitchen from your table, you can see there's no form of hygiene in there, and there's heavy use of cheap plastic equipment. I can't review the food here because they took my order and FORGOT to bring it. after waiting for 45 minutes, I asked where the food is and they said they forgot to send it to kitchen. That was very disappointing and I had to leave because I had to catch my flight from the airport. Very upsetting experience with them.

author: Mrs L
review_text: Used to frequent this tzechar years ago but the food has deteriorated so so so much!  Sambal prawn was so gross - more oil than sambal, sambal flavor mediocre and the worst part, the prawn was not fresh and badly executed.  Pork chop was average at best.    Mee goreng ordered at a tzechar when it’s good it’s good but this one was yucks to the max.  The only dish worth stomach real estate was the egg furong.  Overall a disappointing meal which is such a pity given how good the food here was back in its heydays.  Thankful we have so many great tzechars in Singapore we can frequent.  Lots of mainland China tourists who will sustain the business here though.  Though for me, never again.

author: Jane Le
review_text:
We had lunch at this restaurant last Tuesday with our colleagues.
• Venue: Conveniently located in the Chinatown area, near Maxwell MRT.
• Reservations: Recommended, especially during peak hours. The restaurant is medium-sized, and reservations help you avoid the long queue. Reserved guests are given priority entry.
• Opening Hours: Opens at 12:00 PM.
• Atmosphere: Local-style setting with air conditioning — comfortable for a casual group lunch.
• Service: Quite fast and efficient.
• Food: My favourite dishes were the shrimp hor fun, black hor fun, and fried egg — all very tasty and satisfying. Especially all the shrimps are fresh, not frozen shrimp.
• Cost: Around $270 for 12 people, which is reasonable for the portion and quality.
• Overall: A solid lunch spot with good value. Will definitely come back to try other dishes.

author: MELISSA CHIA
review_text: First time here with 4 friends to celebrate birthday for a friend. Heard through TikTok. Michelin?? Kinda disappointed. Overrated. The Signature hor fun too salty though the 4 prawns are fresh. The yam basket, birthday girl complain saltfish. Curry fish head so so. I eaten better ones in heartland coffeeshop.  The 沙皮雞, chicken meat is fake one. Use flour n meat mixed paste  taste like fishcake, a letdown. Overall service is ok. Enbience too noisy, toilet stinks. Told not to be late but we are early still gotta wait till exactly 7.30pm appointment time then get seated. Well unlikely to come back. Not worth the queue n waiting time. Too pricey for this type of food.

author: Krysta Chan
review_text: Quite good value for money. Decent food though I personally don’t feel that it’s outstanding. When we arrived, there were people queueing even before they opened. Typical SG foodies! 😂 thankfully Boss made reservations.  Noise level is a bit too much for me but you get used to it after a while when focus shifts to the food 😆

author: Velvina Lim
review_text:
Had A happy belly.

Lavi taco offer a brunch menu with unique Mexican-inspired dishes, and did it impress!

- Signature Birria Tacos (Limited,
$25/2 pcs)
Slow cooked Brisket and Oxtail  which is juicy, tender, and flavourful loaded full inside crispy taco shells. The shell is somewhat similar to Prata and crispy with every bite.
The melted cheese within adds oomph to the taste.

- 72Hr Sticky Beef ribs ($36)
This dish is fork tender and fall-off-the-bones meat.
The cornbread is simply good!

- Lamb Rack ($38)
2 pieces of lamb rack which is thick, with appropriate fats that make the whole dish enjoyable.
It's so meaty and taste is similar to between satay spices or the Chinese Spice powder on bbq meat . It would be great to be served with Yogurt or Sour cream as I do not fancy the Sour, green sauce on the dish.

The dishes are different from other Mexican dishes that we've tried. I could say it's one of the best. There's several sharing platters, which we saw that come in a big portion.
The hosts are very friendly, and the 2 chefs in kitchen even bade us farewell as we're on our way out from the open kitchen.

Conveniently located at Maxwell Mrt right next to the hawker centre.

High table and chairs for indoor,  and there's a outdoor seating for people watch.

author: Chi Hong Hwang
review_text: Great vibe. Very chill. Good place to hang out with friends. I was here with one of my sons. He was buying me my birthday dinner. We had good conversations about life and things. The tacos were great. We had a platter which came with beef, prawns and vegetables. Very tasty. The accompanying beers and cocktails were nice. Perhaps one suggestion is to provide napkins for wiping hands. Can get messy but thankfully toilets are just a stone throw away.

author: Christopher Leong
review_text: Great vibes at this taco joint last night. The tacos were on point. The wife was especially impressed with the fish tacos and the masala lamb ones were outstanding too. We liked the small touch that they lightly fried the tacos for the saucy lamb, while they baked the tacos for the fried fish. The esquisites were also a flavour bomb. Highly recommended, though best to go down on cooler nights.

author: r qian
review_text:
The food is so nice!! Love the beed tacos & the thai fish tacos 🌮
The tacos looks a bit small, but the fillings inside it’s actually A LOT!!

Especially shout out to the loaded nachos, they do give a generous portion of cheese in it as well.

The atmosphere there it’s totally different once you step in. Will definitely wanna try again!

author: Charm C
review_text:
Place is fully outdoors, so can be a little humid and hot at times.
Food is amazing, especially the beef birria tacos! Can be on the pricey side ($25 for 2 tacos) but for the quality it's definitely worth trying. No GST and service charge though which is a plus!

author: Eleanor Ang
review_text: The place is hard to find if you dont drive. However, once you reach the place, it has great atmosphere. We ordered the butter prawn tacos and crispy thai fish tacos. Was looking forward to the butter prawn tacos but i feel that it isnt buttery enough for my liking. I prefer the cripsy thai fish.

author: Soo A
review_text:
Hidden gem that are known by many now and it is so difficult to book a table these days 😭 but they have amazing foods and cocktails (next door). Vibes are amazing. I enjoyed every minute here.
Staffs are friendly but there are not enough staffs covering the place. Difficult to get the staffs' assistance, it's better that I sort things out.
Quite warm because it's outdoor terrace, so wear light or sweat.

author: Nowo Kasturi
review_text: Oh Lavi, Lavi, Lavi~ look at this beauty. Can hehe haha make your own taco. (But i dont like doing work for my food. My friends like to tho!)

author: Nick
review_text:
This place for weekday nights is surprisingly chill and what better way to end of a hard day of work then popping by here for some Tacos and drinks. Side note thought theres no air conditioning but then its an open space so at night if its windy its pretty relaxing actually.

For food wise, I would think its definitely an above average. The Fish Tacos is definitely the highlight and the friedness compliments well.

author: Jovial
review_text:
Hits the spot 100%. Soft flour tacos at the perfect thickness, chewy + never soggy. And oh do they go heavy on the fresh stuff: not just quantity but crunch, colour, and flavour, with a super satisfying swipe of white Baja sauce to tie it all together. Every bite is bright and lifted by a creamy, high quality guac. You’ll want a napkin, but trust me when I say you won’t mind.

The birria hard taco brings the indulgence to all that veg-forward comfort with its brittle fried shell, tender slow-cooked brisket, and a rich, meaty consommé. Every bite gives you melty cheese, braising juices, and satiating warmth.... ahh. Sip cola, chase with a citrusy gulp, and you’re set for a solid, satisfying, and very vibey meal.

author: Melodie
review_text:
Food was good! The atmosphere was really nice too but there were diners smoking which wasn’t very pleasant

Fish taco was good

author: xyyy
review_text: Went there a few weeks ago with friends and had a lovely time. The tacos were deliciously seasoned especially the fish tacos. Staff were friendly and helpful, made us feel comfortable from when we first step foot in their vibey open air area. Came on a weekday night so it was rather quiet but we thoroughly enjoyed the more laid back and chill atmosphere. Will definitely come back!

author: fels k
review_text:
Great Mexican fare in a vibrant, energetic environment! Got the meat platter for 2 to share amongst 3 people and we were stuffed! Jalapeño poppers were amazing as well.
Must get the guacamole (+$3) add-on, seriously fresh and creamy. Staff were friendly and vibes were great! Will come back again :)

author: Carmen
review_text: Great tacos! The prawn ones were an absolute standout - highly recommend!! The birria/oxtail ones were also recommended to me - too spicy for me but my friends loved them. The queso chips were moreish, really great to pick at. I also got the churros - warm and chewy! I think the dipping sauce could be a bit thicker but that’s minor nitpick. Great vibes in the courtyard too.

author: Emerson Boon
review_text: Good ambience; there is no airconditioning but there are some fans. Was able to seat 2 persons without making a booking. We had the Mala Chicken and the Birria; both were rich and delicious. Will come back for a weekday dinner after work.

author: Keith Li
review_text:
Got the 69 bucks sharing platter. The Argentinian prawns were really yummy! They were quite fresh and sweet too. Brisket was a little tough but the seasoning made up for it. Mala chicken was alright, also a little tough but still can.

The other condiments served alongside was quite good, I like the roasted peppers!

author: Sherry
review_text: Amazing food and service. Came for the live music on Wednesdays but it’s moved to Saturday. My fault for not checking beforehand. We still had an amazing time.

author: SY Oh
review_text: A pretty cool outdoor setting with graffiti art but it was kinda noisy to hear each other. Ordered two pints of premium suntory beer (which never fails!), two yummy fish tacos and one rendang chicken nachos to share! Rendang chicken was alright, was expecting a little more! But glad we didnt over order as the portion was just nice for two.

author: David Clark
review_text: Some of the best tacos and gluten free food you’ll find in Singapore. Caught in a “shower” so stayed for beers too. Great options in the fridge and Little Creatures on tap. Lovely team and staff

author: Jonathan Wan
review_text:
This is your typical quintessential Perth, Australia; pub experience. Carrying the vibes of the what the former revered Fremantle Little Creatures use to offer; this place is pumping. The menu pricing would make the former Australian prime minister Scott Morrison question whether Australians can’t afford housing because of smashed avo on toast, or eating at Lavi Taco.

Write a review for free Pandan Churros

author: aindrila karmakar
review_text:
A wonderful spot for Italian food in Robertson Quay!

Had such a lovely experience at Rosso Vino. The location by the river is beautiful and the ambience is warm, cosy and perfect whether you dine indoors or choose the al-fresco seating outside.

We tried their Christmas festive menu and really enjoyed the dishes — everything felt thoughtfully curated and authentically Italian. Their regular à la carte options also look great, so definitely planning to return for that too.

Most importantly, the hospitality here is amazing. The staff are friendly, attentive, and make you feel genuinely welcomed from the moment you enter.

Overall, a great place to enjoy good food, a nice atmosphere, and wonderful service. Highly recommended!

author: Brandon T
review_text:
The food was absolutely delicious and authentic - I ordered the bruschetta, napoletana (one of the best pizzas I've ever had) and tiramisu.
Service was also exceptional and professional.
I would definitely come back if I'm ever in Singapore again.

author: Eian Tang
review_text: Kirv and his team’s excellent table service goes great with good tasting foods. I’d recommend Rosso Vino for cozy family meals and small group get-togethers. 👍 The only gripe was the level of cleanliness in their restrooms — not pleasant enough. On top of that, it’s located outside of restaurant where it’s not sheltered.

author: Joel Koh
review_text: I recently enjoyed the set meal for lunch for two at Rosso Vino and had a wonderful experience. The food was delicious and well-prepared, but what really elevated our visit was the excellent service provided by C Yan and Danny. They were attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal. The combination of good food and outstanding service makes Rosso Vino a great choice for lunch, and I'd highly recommend it to anyone looking for a quality dining experience.

author: Junhui Ong
review_text: Went for a Sun lunch and was served by Kirv. The service provided was impeccable which made the dining experience amazing. We ordered the cheese and Italian cured meats selection together with the bruschetta which were delicious! Followed up with the generous portion of seafood risotto. Ended with tiramisu, loved the texture and taste of the cream and the bitterness of the espresso. Rosso Vino also has a very relaxing atmosphere with good views along the river.

author: Jerry Ngo
review_text:
Had an awesome evening at Rosso Vino. The food was appetising and flavourful. The restaurant full of charm and the service was a delight.

The wine recommendation was on point. The waiter recommended Doppio Passo IGT which was fruity and smooth to drink.

author: Judy Ong
review_text: Full of authentic Italian flavours and well prepared dishes. The waiting staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole dining experience enjoyable. Will definitely be back again.

author: Emily Tan
review_text: KIRV is an amazing server. Welcoming, polite, friendly, comfortable. We came here for a birthday celebration. They prepared a candle and played the birthday song. The handmade pasta was fresh. Pizza bread was fluffy and nicely burnt. We sat in the air conditioned area so it was nice and cooling. The outdoor seating looks nice too. Great vibes. Quality food. Strong cocktails. 1 for 1 daily 4-7pm. Worth it.

author: Neil Alexander
review_text:
Always a delight. Authentic Italian cuisine and alfresco dining by the Singapore river. Every time I visit Singapore this is my go to place.
Carlo is a great host and all the staff are great. Cyan was my excellent server.

author: 송지현
review_text:
The food, the service, and the atmosphere were all so good.
Order anything!
Everything is delicious.
And the meticulous service of the staff makes for a very happy time.
I was able to have a happy and enjoyable time thanks to the aweni staff especially who served our table.
I hope the company rewards her well.
I always want to see her smile.
Thanks to her, I want to visit again.

author: Mathew
review_text:
My cousin recommended me to this lovely place and I went with my family. We were seated outside. The view and atmosphere of the restaurant was absolutely outstanding.

We ordered a spread and tremendously enjoyed the food! Most importantly, the waiter - Don - service was immaculate and he provided such exceptional service! We would definitely be coming back for more!

author: RUSSELL YAP
review_text:
Ate here on National Day; made a reservation earlier to make sure we had a seat. Food was pretty good, tastes good. Personally felt the pizza was a bit salty (but my partner said it was ok) - presumably it’s a personal preference.

Service was fantastic, servers were attentive and quick to respond. Special shout out to Pat for amazing service! Appreciate the attention and detail to us!

author: Michelle Entwistle
review_text: I had an excellent meal at Rosso Vino last night. The pasta and sauce were delicious and so was the panna cotta. The service was excellent I was served by Cyan. There was a lovely atmosphere and beautiful setting. Thank you so much for a lovely evening at your restaurant. Highly recommend a visit.

author: Loy Hui Yang
review_text: Enjoyed their Sunday brunch thoroughly with my friend! Go for their foccacia and cheese board for appetisers, pastas/pizzas for a satiating main and end off with their molten lava cake for the perfect finish ❤️

author: Marcus Hew Mun Kok
review_text:
Lovely Christmas Eve dinner at Rosso Vino. The pasta was excellent—especially the pesto and lobster pasta, both flavorful and beautifully prepared.
Special thanks to Kirv for the attentive and warm service despite the festive crowd.
Highly recommended for a special occasion.

author: Selah V
review_text:
I had my birthday dinner here. I love the table we were give. It was just beside the river. The people and dog watching was amazing and relaxing. We ordered  simple. I particularly liked the Margherita. It's always unassuming but the tomatoes they used were really sweet. It was a refreshing dish. The lasagna was good and meaty too. Everything was light and pleasant. I just kinda wish they have more mains.

The service was warm and friendly. I think what I like most is the location. I've been to another Italian restaurant around the area, but their location beside the river and the street makes it really relaxing. Really chill.

author: Iqwan
review_text: Just landed in SG and came in for a late night meal. The food was great and hit the spot. We were served by Pat, who was an absolute superstar. She explained the recommendations expertly and served with a smile. 10/10 service - will return.

author: Joey Tan
review_text: We had a really great dinner here! The food was wonderful and we enjoyed everything we had. Our favourites were the lasagne and pizza. Kiru was our server and they were really friendly and attentive. Thank you for a great time!

author: Cate. S
review_text:
Great Italian Restaurant near the river.
Perfect place to sit outside and enjoy real Italian food. Also the service is friendly and fast. I did not had a reservation which is recommended when you come on a Sunday. Had the burrata fresca and the fettuccine Bolognese - will come definitely again.

author: Jennah do
review_text: My favourite local Italian food in Singapore is Rosso Vino, it is located at Robertson Quay, I love the delectable and scrumptious flavours of their Italian Cuisine and the tranquil and serene atmosphere while eating al fresco, overlooking the picturesque and beautiful view of the Singapore Clarke River. Or, I can choose the indoor seating that gives off an authentic and classy vibe. I always chill out at this place with my friends or family on the weekend. The food has an authentic Italian taste, and is much more tastier when paired with their refreshing Red wines. My daughter loves to eat Pizza Burrata, Fettuccine alla Bolognese and Tiramisu. For me, I love all of their food. Every time I come to Rosso Vino, I would try different types of food on their menu. Moreover, the staff are friendly, polite and professional. Carlo, the co-owner of this place, is fantastic. He is very friendly and makes us happy every time we visit this place. He also pays attention to details of the food and drinks. Keep it up Rosso Vino 👍

author: Eileen Kwek
review_text: Bought 红油抄手 from a beef noodle shop.  OMG, every dumpling is so big and the sauce is so savoury with black vinegar.  Best I have ever eaten!

author: Shaolin Leong
review_text:
A relatively small food center.
2km from where we stay & we always jogged here have dinner & walk back .
The famous CKT is "so so" to us , with terrible long waiting time.Not worth the wait ! The wanton noodles is not bad surprisingly! BKT is ok too ! Prawn noodle at the corner has loyal supporters too !
Yet to try the rest ! Parking I heard is a headache  !

author: Crimsonpig101
review_text: A busy foodcourt which is pretty hidden away, 25+ food stalls. No air-conditioning just wall fans. Tried the Michelin guide stir fry noodles for medium size $8 which were good but was it worth the queue time?

author: L Chan
review_text: This hawker centre has been around since the 1970s. Set beside the Alexandra Canal, it’s one of the few places to enjoy a meal with a waterfront breeze & city lights. Despite renovations over the years, it has kept its bustling, open-air charm, remaining both a community dining hall & a slice of hawker heritage by the riverside

author: Amos Lee
review_text: Lau Goh Teochew Chye Thow Kway is run by a half deaf and mute couple. There’s a picture on the counter, what you need to do is point the order you want to let the lady boss know. The price are $6, $8 and $10. There are three types which is black, white and yuanyang. I personally prefer the black one. The portion is quite filling.

author: hua
review_text:
Zion Hawker Centre is my go-to spot for a delicious Char Kway Teoy, I highly recommend Stall 20, “River side good food”.
It’s not the super famous stall with a endless long queue. Here is definitely one of the best I’ve had. I always order white, extra egg, and without beansprouts. There was wok hei, pork lard and the taste was just so tasty. If you’re a Ckt lover, you absolutely must try this one! The queue is shorter, and you won’t be disappointed.
Highly recommended.
The place is bright, clean, and in the eve it has a nice breeze, making it a great spot to enjoy the food.

author: Regine Lee
review_text: It was a Saturday 4:30pm, most of the stalls are closed. I haven’t take my lunch so wanted a quick bite. I saw braised duck stall has 3 person queuing so thought it will be fast. End up i queued for 20 mins. And the food was not worth waiting for. The soup was too salty to be edible. The rice had a rotten taste (maybe weather too humid, rice spoil very fast), the rice was also cold and hard. The duck meat was too tough. Overall, i regretted getting this. I did not finish it even though is my first meal of the day.

author: Joe Lau
review_text: The food center is beside the river with very good vibe. We have the Michelin kuai zha but found it abit salty.

author: FS M
review_text: We went here for dinner. The queue at Zhu Wei Xian big prawn noodle was short so we took the chance to order it. The broth is very tasty, the pork practically falls off the ribs, the prawns are generous and chunky. Very economical for $8 per bowl. Add some chili padi with soya sauce for more flavour. Highly recommended.

author: Prettyme Yu
review_text:
Love the wanton mee and prawn noodle here.

My hubby likes the char Kuey tiao.

author: See Fly Low
review_text:
When did eating in Hawker centre become so complicated? 🍜

Just had the most ridiculous experience at Zion Road. Since when did our hawker centres become so over-engineered and monetized that it’s actually a headache to eat there?

The $0.20 Empty Bowl: Asked for a small empty bowl for my 5 year old daughter. Was told it’s an extra $0.20 because "cleaning is outsourced." Since when is a bowl a luxury item?

The Logistical Mess: The food stall says one thing, but the drinks stall tells us we must return cups to them directly because they "opted out" of the system. So I had to return noodles and tray to the tray return system, then return the Kopi cups to the drinks stall. WTH.

My immediate reaction was why this noodle stall so hao lian. Until I realised they are just the victims as well

Why must everything be monetized until it's this difficult? It’s supposed to be a community space, but it feels like every single movement is tracked, charged, or outsourced. It’s hard not to feel like the priority has shifted entirely from serving the people to just squeezing out every last cent.

Is this really the "efficiency" we're aiming for??

author: Edwin Sim
review_text: I was hoping to find some authentic traditional hawker food here but was a disappointment. I ordered and waited for over 30 mins for white carrot cake, fried kuay teow, satay and chicken wings and no way they were even close to what I wanted with old school common hawker food. All were below average and the better one is the chicken wings but from my taste bud it's not fresh.

author: Allan Lambert
review_text:
One of the more popular Hawker Food Markets - located above a normal veg, meat and hardware market.

By far the most choice which can be intimidating. Follow the crowd.

Easy to find from the local metro. Enjoy.

author: Shing Low
review_text: I recommend these 2 stalls. The black carrot cake has crispy edges and taste is juz right. The steamed dumplings are very tasty...no 'porky' smell. Both stall owners/staff are very patient and polite. Great buys!

author: Hs Auto
review_text: Nice food and serve with big portion.. worth coming to eat very authentic Hainanese boneless chicken rice

author: Noble Noble
review_text: One of the best. Unrivaled despite having a fierce rival a few stalls away. Been eating for years. It has a seafood taste in it. Pardon my photo. Gobbled it up before taking photo. Aunty is very sweet and uncle very chatty!
