author: Emmanuel Reyes
review_text: One of the oldest hawker centres in Singapore. We decided to have lunch here as it was in one of the stops on our hop on/hop off bus. Multiple food outlets to choose from covering all things Singaporean. I opted for the Hainanese Chicken Rice and it was delightful. Service was quick and portion size was adequate. Although open air under covered area there was ample fans running to keep things cool in the public seating area. Overall a great experience.

author: H L
review_text:
There were a few famous stalls with queues that we didn’t go for.

Seng Huat Western - 4.5/5 ⭐️
not sure if there’s no queue or because they gave out buzzers. Regardless, the food was really good! It’s the traditional western comfort food we used to get. their coleslaw ⭐️ might be the star of the show it’s not the creamy kind that I dislike, instead it’s light and refreshing maybe because of the lime/lemon juice that they added into it! Fries were also well fried and crispy.

Riverside Good Food - 5/5⭐️
Kinda sad that there’s not much queue compared to the famous Zion riverside char kway teow. No comparison since I didn’t try the famous one, but riverside’s char kway teow might be one of the best I’ve had!! There’s wok hey and there’s also plenty of fried pork lard 😍

author: Fajar Priyanto
review_text:
The most popular is of course the char kway tiauw, but there are others that are as good. The bbq chicken, the beef soup, the prawn mee, the zhi char. I like the old uncle chen tng soup $2.5
Simple and refreshing.

author: Truth Fairy
review_text:
Great hawker Center beside the river. Surprised that there were seats during lunch hours, which is a good sign. Tried the food king good carrot cake and wonton Mee. Both are better than average. Was mind-blown by the carrot cake taste at first, but thought it was jelat as we continued eating. Queue was quite long for carrot cake, expect 15 mins. Wanton Mee not bad, have a variation of fried and dry wanton. Soup was good.

If you are wondering why their drink stalls are long queue, not because it’s good or special, it’s because one person is mending the whole stall. Queued for sugar cane longer than for wanton Mee.

Ps. A lot of OLs and OMs come here. Avoid if you don’t want to meet your colleagues or your ex classmates who are working around the area.

Edit 25/2/25: wanted to try their big prawn noodle as they are famous for it here. Sadly. Didn’t bring cash and the store only accepts cash. Got their cai fan instead. Would say, taste flavourful but the price … for student/the broke/ or those who have saw cheaper caifan. Actually the worst part is, their banner wrote $3 for 3 veg. Ordered 3 veg (1of it is tofu but there’s no meat I have inspected before buying) they charged $3.7. So more of  i got cheated. Sad. Just buy with caution and be prepared to pay more than what’s advertised.

author: Super Fragrance
review_text:
Ordered small ckt for $4.50

Pros
Taste. Sweet but I guess more important spicy which brought out the savoriness.

Many fresh hum. At least relatively speaking. It is not a big plate but quite a few hum. Bloodiness adds to the taste.

Eggs is also very distinctive cooked.

Cons
Well it is meant to be halal. Not halal certified but owner is Muslim. So no lup cheong or pork lard to go with it. Sadly.

Still a delicious plate

author: Benjamin Goh
review_text: Got the $4.50 plate, which was 75% filling so most people should be satisfied with the $5.50 one. The chilli is pretty moderate but if you don't eat spicy at all it may be a little too much for you to handle. Flavours are great with the mix of sweet and spiciness that blends well together. Also didn't realise the stall was Muslim owned until writing the review, a nice bonus I guess.

author: Tan
review_text:
✅️ Halal
✅️ QR Code payment
✅️ Delicious
✅️ Easy to order
✅️ Friendly staff
✅️ Not oily

❌️ No pork lard

Do note that as this is a halal-certified store, they do not have pork lard. Surprisingly good though! I love how it doesn't feel oily and still has the char kway teow taste. It's very nicely done! Be patient with the stallholder as he is doing everything by himself. It is worth the wait, can afford to get the medium sized if you have an appetite.

author: Suhaimi Taryo
review_text: The char kway teow by far the best I ever taste. Really tasty delicious, cockles well cooked, wok hey fumes delightful.i recommend all  as Muslim Abang is very professional on his char kway teow. Kudos ..👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻

author: Mohamed Azhan
review_text:
Legit Char Kway Teow that's Halal. Flavours are there, wok hei is present......as good as Halal Char Kway Teow can get.

Friendly owner and helper. Recommended if you happen to be in the area.

author: Nurul Afifah
review_text: Ordered the medium size Char Kway Teow at $5.50 (as pictured). Very flavourful with lots of cockles included. There's also the option to add extra cockles for $2. The owner is Chinese-Muslim so the food is halal~

author: khamdan mahamud
review_text:
Flavorsome Halal Char Kway Teow!

Rating: 5/5

I'm so impressed with this Halal Char Kway Teow! The dish was expertly cooked with a delightful balance of flavors. The noodles were tender, and the ingredients were fresh.

The large portion was incredibly value-for-money, easily enough for two meals. I loved that I could enjoy a satisfying, filling meal without breaking the bank.

Service was friendly and efficient.

Highly recommend for those seeking delicious, authentic Halal Char Kway Teow in generous servings!

author: HMK Ithnin
review_text:
Posted awhile ago.
2025 came back n giving an update....still the same taste.

The best i must say....chinese style with a chinese muslim chef.
No doubt the slow waiting time...but its worth every plate u go.
All the ingredients are fresh..especially the cockles.
He cook basically each plate at a time.
Dont expect to get your food fast,to those who is hungry please skip this place,or maybe get something quicky,the rojak nearby not bad.
Must avoid praying time...
100% satisfactionq

author: Suzanna Alias
review_text: Best char kway teow, and my daughter, the fussy eater, loves it!

author: Sean Goh
review_text:
Finally tried this Halal fried kway teow from Bukit Merah View Hawker Centre. I wanted to try this the other time round when i was here for lunch, unfortunately they were closed and i try their neighbor stall, coincidentally also sells fried kway teow too. Got to know of this stall through a Tv interview and saved the place ever since. Reached there late afternoon and there wasn't any queue and i was able to order immediately. Prices for the char kway teow starts from SGD$4.5 onwards.

Portion for the fried kway teow was generous. its comes with sliced fishcakes and cockles which was a little small. Taste wise, not bad, hint of wok hei but seems to be lacking in flavors.

Overall, a decent fried kway teow that i have tried lately. The owner is actually very friendly, even managed to strike a conversation with him while he was preparing the food.

author: Nurin Jazlina
review_text: best kway teow ever! me and my husband's favourite, we always go there. uncle is very friendly too. cheap and there is even a qr code for those who dont pay by cash. and it's halal so i really urge the muslims who crave genuine chinese kway teow to try.

author: Asyraf
review_text:
Amazing how it can still withstand the flavour and complexity despite it’s journey from Bukit Merah to Pasir Ris 🤣 Super friendly uncle and it was nice that they are extremely thankful for every single customer that came to purchase their food.

In terms of the food itself, it’s just spicy enough and flavourful enough, but the key ingredient is the hum. So I will ALWAYS go for the extra hum option. Go for small for a snack, medium for a proper meal, and large if you’re famished!

The best part of the whole thing, when I went there around 7+, there was NO QUEUE! Amazing. Would definitely come back again and again if I stay in the area. Best halal certified kway teow in SG hands down.

author: Wun Hui Chong
review_text: First time tried uncle ckt, ordered extra spicy and he delivered. Not many hawker will use chilli padi to fry it. I was quite surprise! The taste is very pleasant even though he don’t use lard. And the uncle is very chill and friendly . Even though our interaction is short but pleasant. After eating I dabao one for my brother. You guys can come and support this stall!

author: Luke He
review_text: 3 (good quality but not my taste), freshly cooked kway teow but just not to my taste. I came around 6pm at Sunday, and owner told me get food 20 mins later. It’s freshly cooked and ingredients are good quality like oyster with no bad taste. But I do not like the overall seasoning of it. You may find it good tho.

author: Danial Durrani
review_text: The spot to go for halal char kway teow. I come here at least once a week. The medium size portion is super filling and full of cockles. Do stop by to support this bro.

author: muibadah
review_text: One word. Actually TWO!! Delicious & Patience. To gain deliciousness, you'll have to be patient. He's a one-man show, but believe me when i say it, it is worth the wait. Just have lots of patience. Seriously... 😋👍

author: Teck Chye Yeo
review_text:
I read about this place online sometime back, but I never got around to try it.
Truth be told; I'm an old-school foodie, & Char Kway Teow must be laden with pork lard for me, or it's a no-go.
However, I serviced my car in Alexandra Road, and this was close by, & as luck would have it, the workshop finished withe the car early, so off I went for a bite of Halal CKT.

I was apprehensive at first, but the soft-spoken hawker took to his wok as I waited, & done, I dug in with bated breath.

Just look at this photo of my plate. It looks like the real deal, lard and all ya?
It's got the Wok Hei I tell you! None of that sinful oily taste, but in its place, a clean clear, sweet-sauce induced flavour, with generous amounts of fish cake & cockles.
I liked it! It's smoky, charred strands of kway teow, layered in just the right amount of sauce, with none of that eekie aftertase of lard!

Will I be back?
Well. If I'm in the neighbourhood, why not?

author: Ridwan Mustafa
review_text: Delicious affordable halal char kway teow from a chinese convert islam muslim owned. Has 3 pricing! Small:$4.50 Middle $5.50 Large $6.50. Ordered the small one and it look pretty decent. Service wise can be improve. Just don’t come during peak lunchtime period between 12 to 2.30pm as he’s busy and will give sour face (whoever order when he’s making the order as he’s only 1 person no assistant)

author: Zaza Md Taat
review_text: Decided to give this plate of char kway teow goodness a try. It's pretty ok-nice, but not in a way tat one shd travel all the way to B.Merah just to try this out (leave that to me heh). Their plate of CKT uses dark sauce which i dont normally like, coz im used to mum's versh which is a brown-pedas2 sauce. I rarely buy CKT outside & if i do, it'll be beef CKT. Their cockles are not big, pretty small really & i alrdy asked for extra but it's not really visible unless u start eating into it. Fast service, clean stall, overall clean hawker ctr.

author: Elfinaa Elfinaa
review_text: hi,, I have eaten at this uncle's shop. My husband and I come from Kulai, Johor, Malaysia. This uncle's story really inspires us to become true Muslims.The stall is very clean.Uncle was welcoming us and very friendly to us.The char kuey teow is Good and delicious.Thanks uncle and May Allah protect and love you always..hidayah milik Allah SWT…

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Shaolin Leong
review_text:
Building a wet market near a hawker center in oder to support & provide the daily necessities as well as providing convenience to the residents living in the estate has always been the mission of HDB and URA.
This hawker center is actually quite big !
As I moved in lately so I took the opportunity to explore the area. Tried the fishball & meatball noodle,carrot cake & coffee today.
As for the wet market side most stalls were closed as it was around 1 plus when I was there. Heard the wanton noodle is quite nice but an old man like me can only clear 2 items maximum in a meal ! Looking forward to my next visit now to walk 2km back in order to burn off the extra calories !

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Emily Ho
review_text: Food wasn't as good as other hawker centres. The char kway tiao had little ingredients and no wok hei. Just lots of fried carbs. The satay was decent but there are better ones. Rojak had too much sauce in it, not much fruits and the you tiao was hard, asked for spicy but the sauce wasn't very spicy. Wouldn't waste calories at this hawker. centre.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Karthick Sonaimuthu
review_text: A hidden gem with lots of great food. There are a good number of Michelin star hawker stalls. My favourite are, Carrot cake, NaNa Curry and the western food shop. The ambience is not great, But foe good food its ok to compromise on the ambiance.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Roger K19
review_text:
The laksa from this stall is delicious.

Updated 2 Oct 2024
Al-Latifah Indian Muslim stall
There is a new prata stall that has opened, which has been operating for 20 years at Orchard Road. Their prata is delicious and crispy, served with flavorful curry.

The Malay stall selling lontong is my favorite too. They still make their rice cake, which is very rare nowadays.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: CK Cheong
review_text: Many good food options like mutton soup, fried carrot cake, duck rice, wanton noodles and Nana curry. The hawker centre us a little run down and could definitely do with some upgrades. It is also not easy to find parking especially during peak hours and weekends

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Xinren Zhang
review_text: Not all stalls are available, which is normal. The tables are spaced nicely to avoid crowding. Special stalls to note:1 chai chuan tou mutton soup(michelin award) opens only 11am-1.30pm or until sold out. Closed on mon. 2 na na curry(michelin award) for extra spicy curry. 3 hakka thunder tea and yong tau foo.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: May Wong
review_text: Carrotcake clean no burnt bits. But michelin 2024... i don't agree. Not as good as toa payoh green mountain but better than tiong bahru market carrot cake.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Djoko Purwanto
review_text:
Yummies ...  with a few HALAL stalls
01.01 al-syafiq
01.02 yusoff mee

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Ramesh N
review_text: Great old school hawker centre. Enjoyed the NaNa Curry. Spicy but tasted good. Hokkien mee was also tasty with bits of fried pork crackers on top and mixed with into the noodles. It was hot in the afternoon but will go there again.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Richard Tan
review_text:
Ate here several times. The floor and tables are cleaner than other HDB hawker centres. The cleaning contractor must be managing their workers better than other companies .

Good variety of food choices. No parking problems.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: jtango
review_text:
Be prepared to queue for 20-30 mins for Heng Heng Coffee. A go to for the caffeine ‘pick-me-up’.

The fish ball noodle from Hong Xing handmade fish and meat ball is delicious and must try.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Adam Koh
review_text:
Anyone who went there, pls try the wantan noodle. The stall is locate at near the carpark. The portion they give is really worth the money as compare with other stall.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Beautiful Life
review_text: The food centre has many stalls selling different kind of food. The bak chor mee and the fried carrot cake is highly recommended. Also another good place for foreigners to explore into local food.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Edo Lego
review_text: Waited for about 20min for this yong tau fu egg noodle. Not disappointed as the taste in dark soy sauce is good. It came with five different ingredients by default. There are others can be chosen from also. Price is below $5. Will update the stall name.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: derek neo
review_text: A Huge hawker center with many stalls some a few with Michelin Bib.  Nice airy and clean environment with ample parking around the hawker.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: D. Lim
review_text: Old hawker center with affordable food and good variety. Surprisingly, there are 4 western food stalls here.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Adam Schmitt
review_text: Now this is the real deal. With a plethora of options, I stumbled upon fantastic selections at incredibly reasonable prices. Situated in a bustling location, it exudes a wealth of character that makes the visit absolutely worthwhile.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Desislava Filipova
review_text:
Great streetfood market with good diversity of chinese, indian, indonesian, vietnamese cuisine. More than 50 booths with main courses, desserts, drinks.
If you are a streetfood lover, it is a must visit. Prices are very low for Singapore.
Great value for money!

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Loo Poh Keng
review_text: Alot of good hawker food.But q is long for the better ones and most good food finish selling by noon.

restaurant: Bukit Merah View Market & Hawker Centre
author: Patrick Lee
review_text: 17Jan 2024 - This is a large food centre with many stalls. You'll find 2 to 3 stalls offering the same food, giving you more options to choose from. To sample as many food stalls as possible, it's recommended to go early, preferably between 10 am and 2 pm, as some stalls close after 2 pm. There's also a spacious area for cyclists to park their bikes, making it a good gathering place for cycling enthusiasts. Keep in mind that competition among stalls brings out the best, making it a rewarding experience for food and cycling enthusiasts alike.

author: Cindy S
review_text:
Quite popular local seafood restaurant, spacious place with quite many tables.
We ordered crabs both in chilly and ego yolk, nice. Other seafood are also fresh.
Waiters are too busy, so don’t expect proper service - prepare to clean your own plates and refill tissues.

author: C
review_text:
Had lunch at Chuan Kee Seafood and the food was great — we ordered the Seafood Claypot, Tofu, and Sweet & Sour Pork, all delicious and very good value at about $15 per person. It was also surprisingly uncrowded for a weekend. Rating: 5/5.

Chuan Kee is a long-standing Teochew-style zi char spot known for clean, seafood-forward flavors and wok techniques passed down through generations. Its cooking stays true to old-school hawker traditions, focusing on freshness, balanced seasoning, and consistent execution.

A dependable classic that continues to serve honest, heritage-style zi char done right.

author: Kelvin Wong
review_text:
This place is hidden in the industrial building area in Tiong Bahru. This restaurant is well known for their seafood, however this time we only order simple Chinese dishes. The food is unexpectedly great, even comparable to Hong Kong style small restaurant standard.

The pepper beef is tender and savory. The frog is sautéed well with the sauce. The veggies do not look appealing but tasted unexpectedly fresh and soft. The shrimp is great as well. The satay was great too. One thing is that the portion is not big enough.

Most importantly, this place is value for money. When you can see so many local families dinning with their family, you know you did not go to a wrong place.

author: Joey S
review_text:
Finally fixed my chilli crab craving here. The seafood quality is top-notch; both the crab and prawns were remarkably fresh and sweet.
The restaurant is crowded, but the vibrant atmosphere adds to the experience.

author: hua
review_text: Nestled in the industrial area, this hidden gem offers a delicious experience for local zhi char food. Many tasty food here. Their nyonya fish and heavenly four kings veggies are a must to try. While their pork satay is equally good too. Outdoor seatings are the best. Price is reasonable and there’s ample parking available. We have visited this place many times. Most of the times they are very crowded after 7pm.

author: Merryheart
review_text:
Chuan Kee Seafood is a very lively Malaysian/ Singaporean Chinese eatery that embodies the best of zi char dining - a huge menu, bustling atmosphere, and dishes meant for sharing.
Service was excellent throughout our meal; the staff were warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly, which added to the overall experience. Everything we ordered was cooked well and satisfying, and the pricing struck a nice balance - moderate, yet very good value for the quality and portion sizes.
Highlights of our dinner included the Bi Feng Tang Wok-Fried Prawns (crispy, fragrant, and addictive), Duck Wrapped in Lotus Leaf (aromatic and tender), and the Signature Homemade Beancurd, which had a lovely silky texture. The Curry Fish Head was on the pricier side at $50, but worth it given that it was prepared with fresh Red Grouper - rich curry, generous portion, and great with rice. Another standout was the Four Heavenly King vegetables with sambal; the spice level was spot on and the sambal had just the right depth of flavour.

A sweet treat at the end - complimentary ice cream and soybean custard added a nice touch.

Overall, this is a fantastic spot for a casual but delicious zi char meal with family or friends. I'll definitely be back to explore more of their extensive menu.

author: les wong
review_text:
I found my favorite zichar.
We ordered moonlight Horfun, cheese pork ribs, sambal kangkong and crab fried rice. I love the wok hey from Horfun, cheese pork ribs was flavourful too. Paid $35 for 4 dishes, quite a good price for today’s pricing standards.

It’s also a nice touch they have free flow newly cooked pop corn, soya bean curd and ice cream / ice drops.

Service was also good, friendly and not pushy to sell you expensive dishes.

We would definitely be back soon to try more. Highly recommended.

author: Andrew Tan
review_text: Place was packed with people during dinner time. Service staff was really accommodating n friendly despite being busy. Food fresh, taste good and price is affordable and reasonable.

author: Adrian Ng
review_text:
casual zichar place in an industrial place, yet it's packed with people looking for good, fresh and reaonably priced food. fabulous to have fish steamboat on a rainy and cooling night. the sambal made the 四大天王 dish (brinjal, lady's fingers, long beans and petai) highlight of the meal. snack on biscuits, popcorn, bean curd and ice cream (one per pax) before, during and after the main meal ;)

only catch is drinks are cash only (beer was added to the food charges though) (I didn't have "money" to buy even a glass of hot tea 😭)

service is brisk and friendly, and yet there is no service charge 👍

author: Grace Chua
review_text: Vibrant , good and prompt service. Food is good and affordable! Pre-ordered the Lotus Seed Chicken which is hard to come by these days. The sweet and sour pork, la la soup and yam ring is very good too!

author: Alvin Ho
review_text: The sweet and sour pork was delicious! We also really enjoyed the superior la la soup, which had incredibly large and tasty clams. The tofu was decent, and the crab was alright. Service was excellent, and we appreciated the complimentary bean curd and ice cream.

author: Ivy ali
review_text: More than half of the lala served were not fresh, either couldn't open the shell or with rotten taste. Informed the counter after dinner, the lady who looked like boss unhappy with my feedback, no apologies from her and sound like accusing me of cheating her when I didn't even ask for a refund.

author: Pris Tan
review_text: Average at best. Si fang tofu fish promfret har giau kai   four heavenly king vege. Reasonably priced. Prompt and efficient service . Staffs frequently asked whether news to top.up soup.

author: Tan Ellie
review_text:
Haven't had such a good tze char in a long while.
Flavour: great! Enjoyed all dishes
Price: friendly if you avoid seafood - medium prawn (amazing salted egg flavour that comes with some curry mixed in so it is not gelat) was $33, though there were probably 12 prawns. For comparison, small garlic pork rib was $12
Freebie: free snacks and dessert (ice cream)

author: Karyn Wong
review_text:
food was tasty and affordable. 6 of us spent $165 in total and we had salted egg sotong, koh loh yoke, drunken prawn, egg, veg and the lala that they recommend. lala was huge by the way.

comfortable dining space, not too noisy. pleasant for good conversations.

easy to find parking lot.

author: Calbee Cracker
review_text: Fresh seafood, delicious zhi char dishes and freebies to munch on. Their satay is a must try! Price is fair and no service charge even though they are so friendly and helpful. I will gladly bring family and tourist here.

author: Lingual Tan
review_text: Seafood is not fresh. Worst bamboo clams I’ve ever had in my life - they were tasteless! I thought you could never go wrong with bamboo clams? I regretted ordering 6 pieces. When I gave feedback to the wait staff, she merely responded no refunds can be given and walked away. Clams in soup was nothing extraordinary and was overly peppery. Wouldn’t come back again and would NOT recommend. Plus, drinks only accept cash, and if you pay with Paynow, they charge you GST.

author: joe fong
review_text:
My second time here.  Definitely a local zhi char place, that served top grade ingredients and local delights.

Recommended to local and tourist too

It is a local eatery so dont expect resturant style service but yet good food.

Had the wet style seafood bee hoon,  is full of umami and generous portion so reasonable price.

Chili crab was good quality, sauce is towards the sweet side..for me I like it less sweet more spicy so it is a preference.  Overall i can say the crab is great like jumbo for the look of it.

author: Kevin Kwok
review_text:
Ok this place is outside so it's going to be a little hot and chaotic. We came when there was no line and only a few tables. Lucky us! The service isn't good but the food is! The menu seems huge so I would look at photos here on Google maps and just tell the staff this is what you want.

Cash only. The seafood fried rice was our favorite.

author: Hidden Bites
review_text:
I got recommended this restaurant from Singaporean! So I tried. The seafood was very freshh! The chilli crab was delicious! 😜 also the fried rice wassss really yummy.

This place *only local people not much tourist*

author: Jinghorjiak
review_text: This is not my first time coming here. This food centre is a place to find many good local food. Standard of food here is quite high. Noodles, rices, xiaolongbao….etc. most all are above average. Will back again to try the food from other stalls.

author: sarion chow
review_text: Terrible noise level at the centre aisle of the food center, worse than before renovation. Not sure what they did during renovation but noise seems to come from the ventilation fan system. Extremely high pitch and disturbing, can't believe they would allow this to pass inspection. Spoils the whole eating experience when the food stalls are still great as before.

author: AshtonY
review_text: Look for Uncle Kuah in the market for your plants and flowers needs. My go to shop if I'm in the area. Quality products with honest pricing and very friendly Uncle. You will not regret!

author: Eugene Khoo
review_text: Bloody good food. The chook rice (Rong Ji) and the kway chup (Shi Le Yuan) here depicted are must trys. Faith Nasi Lemak is God's gift too. It's a hawker centre, so not for a first date unless she's a keeper. Go on. Be a man.

author: L Chan
review_text: Lots of well-loved & famous hawker stalls in one big place. Atmosphere is lively & welcoming. Nearest MSCP with linked sheltered walkway is block 88A

author: Flo G
review_text:
This bustling hawker centre next to the market has plenty of food choices especially as a breakfast haunt.

There are a few porridge, chee chiong fun ( including fresh made)  stalls, wanton noodles, prawn noodles, lor mee and many fishball ball noodles plus 2-3 vegetarian stalls.

Also has a good variety of Muslim Malay Indian choices.

Lunch options include chicken, roast stalls, satay bee hoon, Hong Kong slice fish beehoon.

Plenty of food and nostalgic choices.

Seatings are cramped and always full, not a comfy hawker centre to sit and linger. More of eat and run.

Such a pity.

author: Terence Ng
review_text: On a Tuesday evening, 75% of stalls are open, unlike most old hawker centres. A good dinner venue. The Teochew satay beehoon is really good, prepared with pride. Wish the liver is less cooked.

author: Jentzen Fong
review_text:
•Bak Kee Satay BeeHun

I recently had the pleasure of trying "Bak Kee Satay BeeHun", and I must say, it left me thoroughly satisfied. The star of the dish was undoubtedly the satay sauce, which perfectly complemented the noodles. The rich and creamy satay sauce had just the right balance of sweetness and spiciness, creating a harmonious flavor explosion, which I find it very creative.

The noodles, accompanied by tender squid, succulent pork liver, and thinly sliced pork meat, were a delightful addition. The variety of textures and flavors added depth to each bite, making it a truly memorable experience.

One word of advice to fellow food enthusiasts: devour this dish quickly! The noodles have a tendency to soak up the flavors, and while that might sound tempting, it's best enjoyed when the noodles are still slightly firm.

•Fried Oyster

Out of so many dishes the stall offered, I would recommend their Fried Oyster, non-greasy, and the oyster was just cooked right. Not too raw or not too cooked.

Char Kuey Teow was just so.. so only in my opinion, and nothing to shout for.

Little do you know:
The difference between fried carrot cake black or white are not only the colour of the sauce itself, but also the taste. To all tourist, remember to choose the white instead as that's what local Singaporean will choose. If you are curious with the black sauce, it tends to be sweeter if you like it.

author: Andrew Tan atomi Singapore
review_text:
There's something truly special about this hawker centre that evokes nostalgia and sets it apart from others in Singapore. Tucked away in cozy HDB enclaves, it feels like a hidden gem that deserves to be cherished and preserved. It's a comforting reminder of the simpler joys in life.

It’s inspiring to witness these hawker stalls thriving after the pandemic's challenges, even amidst the quieter atmosphere following the election rallies.

As we await the election results tonight, let's take a moment to pause and reflect.

Regardless of the outcome, we trust that the ruling party will assemble a new cabinet to guide Singapore toward a brighter future.

Now is the time to close the widening gaps, unite, and move forward into this new era under PM Wong’s leadership.

author: Esmond Chun
review_text:
This is to review the stall name "Luck樂 Wanton mee. Ipoh hor fun".
We ordered the hor fun $4 and wanton soup noodle $4 for a try.
For hor fun I don't think is good as I can't even find it tasty, the hor fun that used is too thick comparing with traditional way,  even they tried to get the grave to make it smooth. Ingredients provided is reasonable more than many other stalls.
As for the wanton noodle, the BBQ pork used is nice, tasty and some fatty.  As for wanton putting too much pork meat that find a bit too hard. Overall, this could be a new stall as can't find in the directory.

author: Rachael — home
review_text: Wow! A must visit hidden gem in Singapore! Clay pot chicken curry was the tastiest soul food ever! Great vibe with food and also vegetable market.

author: Pamela Yap
review_text: 85 Redhill is a great spot for local food lovers, offering a variety of stalls with different options. I tried the satay bee hoon, which had a rich and flavourful sauce, and the carrot cake was perfectly crispy. It’s a fantastic place to explore the food scene at Redhill Market!

author: 리ybbo비읍
review_text:
One of my go to Hawker for breakfast, lunch probably not recommended for dinner.
Prata, duck noodles, Chee Cheong Fun, Nasi Briayani, chicken rice, curry rice, bread and toast, soya beans, soft boiled eggs. What you name it, will definitely full-fill your 90% of your choice.
Prices might not be as economical as you thoughts, but it won’t be rocket high. Saturday & Sunday are packed, avoid peak hours.
Enjoy!

author: Edwin Indera
review_text:
Hidden Gem Unearthed - Redhill Food Centre Singapore! 🍲✨

Amidst the bustling city, I stumbled upon a culinary oasis at Redhill Food Centre. This unassuming hawker centre revealed a hidden gem - a delightful $1.5 chicken rice with a mouthwatering taste of soup. The flavors danced on my palate, leaving me pleasantly surprised by the incredible value and authentic taste.

Redhill Food Centre is a treasure trove of local delights, where passionate hawkers craft affordable and delicious dishes that satisfy both the stomach and the soul. A true haven for foodies seeking a taste of Singapore's gastronomic delights without breaking the bank.

author: AC Chan
review_text:
Shi Le Yuan Teochew Porridge 实叻圆潮洲粥
Simple and comforting, homely fare that reminded us of the typical Teochew dishes that my late-grandmother used to cook, back in the Eighties. My personal favourite is the flavourful minced pork with fermented black bean. It’s so delicious, I ended up consuming two bowls of rice.

author: Harry Kek
review_text:
Plenty of food choices and the prices generally are cheaper than most other hawker centers.

NEA should look into the cleanliness of the place.  The regulatory supervision and compliance are bad because some of the stores put their things outside the stalls.
The floors are generally not that clean and a lot of common areas are not clean.

Just compare to the present Beach Rd hawker centre and you can see the vast difference.

author: ri fieschi
review_text:
love capturing the atmosphere and environment 85 redhill food centre. brings back alot of memories, 80s/90s. will miss this area once i moved out from this neighbourhood. love the sugar cane, the indian food stall there, everything there is affordable and cheap cheap good food!

will always come back here! <3

author: Kelvin Teo
review_text: Great food located within Redhill hawker centre…… limited space for parking but worth going there every time for the greatness of food variety

author: Nur Muhammad
review_text:
Seng Heng Braised Duck is the best stall in this quaint and rustic food centre.

You can either go for Kway Teow noodles, yellow noodles, or mixed noodles. They have a dry  and soup version.

Choice for rice is available as well but noodles are superior here. The duck neck is addictive and sinful, and the soup is light with a peppery kick, an amazing palate cleanser.

Pro Tip: Come before 9am as they usually sold out by 9am! Early bird gets the worm, they start operating as early as 6am!

author: LaMisT Neo
review_text:
Despite some patrons not clearing their own plate and trays, the tables here are generally clean. There are tray return points at every row of the hawker center which is manned by a young staff each. These staffs actively goes around clearing the table.

Due to the good service by the staff at the tray return points and also he location of the tray return points there were hardly any pests.

Food options are quite limited by dinner. However some of the popular ones are opened till quite late (chicken wing bee hoon, chinese noodle, roast meat, curry rice etc.)

author: Franco Chan
review_text:
Came here craving teh tarik, satay, and tu tu kueh — and all three wishes came true!

☕ Teh tarik was fragrant, smooth, and nicely pulled.
🍢 Satay was juicy, well-marinated, and smoky with delicious peanut sauce.
🍰 Tu tu kueh was soft, warm, and freshly made — comforting and nostalgic.

Perfect place if you want a mix of classic local flavours in one visit.
Will definitely come back again 👍

author: Hatsune Miku
review_text: Sorry for dashing all the foodie's hopes, but Haig Road Market & Food Centre isn't as great as many make it out to be. Food there is mostly average, and I haven't been served bad food except on 1 occassion by a noodle stall, which I will not name here. This noodle stall is newly opened, and has not been around for a long time. Lesson learnt? Buy from hawkers who have a long time presence here and you won't go wrong. And there is no lack of them too. Some of them have been here since I was in primary school and is still in operation. The wanton mee here is very popular although i find it average. Another stall worth mentioning is the fried oyster stall that also serves carrot cake. The auntie here actually fries her carrot cake with thin bits of fish cake. This adds an extra layer of unami that further enhance its taste. This is one of my favourite carrot cakes. Yong tau fu isn't bad but a tad expensive and the cai peng here is pretty affordable(most stalls). Also have a mutton soup stall here which is a plus as mutton soup is hard to find in Singapore. Another ok hawker centre in Singapore, but over-rated by many reviewers.

author: Paul Ciprian
review_text: A kind of fast food/canteen often found in Singapore. Many small stands selling cooked food, in spartan conditions. Tables and benches fixed to the floor, trays not very clean. You don't get napkins, I haven't seen them anywhere, neither here nor in other similar places. The food is tasty, there are long queues at some stands. Crowded! Cash only.

author: Yum yum Cool
review_text: This hawker coffee stall right next to KINEX Mall ( next to Wantan Mee n Economic rice) was Surprisingly Good as the popular coffee stall ( coffee Edition) was closed on Sun. I decided to try out new stall  n did not want to queue too long for another coffee stall. There was no queue but a clean n neat coffee stall. Ordered 2 yuan yang n 1 tea O ping , our verdicts were all good for this stall . Coffee has a good robust beans taste where is almost like those popular coffee stalls. Tea was smooth . I will buy from this uncle again !

author: Y Teo
review_text:
Food market reopen on dec 22 after 3 mths renovation with a number of new stalls.

New hello steam fish is good - small half seabass steam fish with one veg and rice for $7.80.  Second new stall fei mao fish soup is good too - grouper fish head soup with rice $6 - business is good for dinner and my fish was a bit undercook - staff lady is not friendly.   The original teochew fish soup is excellent with long lunch queue but overprice - rice is $1.  New fishball/minced pork noodles is good too compared to the old stall.

Yet to try is new 3rd chicken rice stall, curry puff, Sarawak noodles…

These new stalls have injected some vibrancy to the hawker centre and a wakeup call to some of the lethargic older stalls.

author: Bryan (SMAD)
review_text: Trying out the reopening of The Coffee Edition! Good food, good drinks.

author: Joyful Explorer
review_text: Comfort food. Chose some of our favourite to share. Always busy during lunch crowd on weekdays and hard to find a table. No wait for us on a weekend brunch.

author: Siah Hx
review_text:
Some stalls in this food center only accepts cash, i suggest bring along cash when visiting. And quite many stalls do not provide extra cutleries when requested. Service is below average at most stalls too.

The food center is warm and stuffy on a hot day. Crowded during meal hours too. Washroom and hand wash area available nearby.

author: Gourmet Deli
review_text:
Al Hadi Satay
Really good, meat tender n juicy
Smokiness of the meat makes u drool 🤤
80cts a stick where to find in Singapore
🥢🥢🥢even better than the infamous stall in AMK big market.

author: Steve
review_text: I always here for the Ban mee and nice cup of coffee, btw this hawker have many Arab servant stalls suitable for halal people.

author: Angel Tan
review_text:
Dropped by Haig Road Market & Food Centre since I was on a journey to the east! Tried out dishes that I’ve never eaten before, eg. Sarawak laksa which came with big prawns & a strong taste of spices, & Mee rabus with thick & sweet gravy. The Fried carrot cake was sweet & crispy with its slightly burnt sides, & we ended off with desserts coz of the hot weather (I had the Ice jelly cocktail). Couldn’t leave without getting some of the famous Putu piring!

IG @pingguo301

author: Jason Ng
review_text:
It's my first time at Haig Road Food Centre, and I can tell you it's definitely not my last time! Had loads of good food there and here is my review for each of them

Signature Kolo Mee ($5.50) from Lin Yu Mei - now this is probably the best Kolo Mee I've had. The noodles were perfectly springy, well tossed in shallot and lard oil while not being too oily and the chilli was amazing. It was very fiery, and yet it had a beautiful aroma which made this dish even better. Never mind the minced meat and char siu, just give me their noodles and chilli and I will be a happy man.

Pork and Chicken Satay ($0.80 each) from Mei Mei Satay - the satay meat was pretty sizeable! I loved the marinade used; it was well charred and it made the meat quite tender, even for the pork version. The satay sauce unfortunately isn't peanut-y enough, but it was fine for me as the pineapple juice helped cut the meatiness of satay!

Putu Piring ($2.50 for 4) from Haig Road Putu Piring - now this is a famous one, and I couldn't leave the food centre without having it! Indeed this was probably the best Putu Piring I've had. The flour and gula melaka used was somehow different, it was much more aromatic than others that I've had before. A sweet treat to end the meal!

Definitely coming back for these 3 items again 😍

author: Mr Jun
review_text:
Forget all the famous hawker centres that you got from YouTube. Come here 😁
Love the food, not too crowded, love the people, and there is a free water fountain at the back.

author: Cheong Loong
review_text: A great hawker style food centre with mix of Chinese, Malay n Indian traditional food under one roof . One can surely find something that suits one taste bud on that day. Be pampered to some popular items like wantan noodles, prawn noodles, chicken rice, claypot rice ,curry, chinese deserts , mee goreng, satay, rojak , longtong, mee rebus,  nasi brani, mee goreng n goreng pisang and putu piring. There is more variety  but  just follow the long queues and one will not be disappointed by the food . Have a heavy meal but leave some room for dessert.

author: Helder Rodrigues de Araujo
review_text: Nice food market with quite a few choices. They have two dedicated rows for Muslim food and the remainder of rows served other varieties. I settled for char siu with plain rice which came in at less than $5 SGD. very good value for a decent portion of food.

author: Khairur Azhan
review_text:
- Variety of food but environment not so clean.
- Rosy & Nora's Popiah goreng & popiah basah and its dipping sauce were good.

author: Cat T
review_text:
Tried the Chinese style mutton soup and fell in love, especially the tendons. Although not cheap...
Mei Mei Satay - The medium size plate of carrot cake at $4 was good value and delicious.

author: Ramsey Wee
review_text:
Every time I walk past this stall always long queue , decided to try their mee Soto , kinda disappointed that the begedil ( Malay style potato patties ) is those factory made , not hand made 😑 . Shredded chicken meat no taste at all 🙄. Only the broth and chilli is good .

Behind the food center , there's a aquarium shop , price are all super reasonable . Friendly environment in the wet market .

author: Koh Gary
review_text:
Old school market for center, no frills, genuine local flavors.
Love this duck noodles stall, Uncle Lee is friendly and cheerful, makes your meal a happy one.

author: Ming Leow
review_text: Nice hawker centre. I went for Mee Rebus. Super and Kopicino!

author: WanderWithWit
review_text:
Review of Old Airport Road Food Centre

Overall, Old Airport Road Food Centre exceeded my expectations with its impressive variety of Singapore heritage dishes. It’s an excellent place to experience a wide range of local flavours, and I’ll continue exploring more stalls and updating this review over time.

I also appreciated the creativity behind many stall names, with references to places like Chong Pang, Kallang, and Blanco Court, which add a nostalgic local charm to the food centre.

⸻

1. Old Airport Road Fried Hokkien Mee (#01-99)

★★★★☆ (4/5)

A wet-style Hokkien Mee with noticeable wok hei. While the prawn flavour is relatively mild, the $8 portion is generous, featuring four prawns along with pork and sotong. A satisfying plate and good value for those who enjoy a slightly soupy version.

⸻

2. Famous Old Airport Fried Oyster (#01-101)

★★★☆☆ (3/5)

Tried the $10 3-in-1 oyster omelette with oysters, prawns, and squid. Portion was generous, but the omelette was soft and soggy, heavy on tapioca flour, and lacked crispness. Prawns were overcooked, and squid ran out quickly. Not worth the price.

⸻

3. Chong Pang Huat BBQ (#01-90)

★★★☆☆ (3/5)

Prices are higher than typical hawker stalls, with $1.60 chicken wings and small satay portions. Value was disappointing, and hygiene concerns left a poor impression. Unlikely to return.

⸻

4. Jin Fried Rice (#01-63)

★★★★★ (5/5)

One of the best fried rice stalls I’ve tried. The mala fried rice with Chinese sausage, sunny-side-up egg, and pork chop was fragrant and full of flavour. Despite switching from Japanese rice to regular rice, the quality remains excellent. The pork chop was juicy and a clear standout. A must-try.

⸻

5. Chuan Loo Bee Hokkien Food (#01-111)

★★☆☆☆ (2/5)

The only stall open after 10pm, so I ordered the Imperial Pork Ribs Rice. Despite being cooked to order, the pork was extremely tough, and the sauce tasted odd and unpleasant. Very disappointing and not worth the price.

⸻

6. Whampoa Soya Bean (#01-68)

★★★★☆ (4/5)

Offers more than just soya beancurd and drinks, with a good variety of traditional desserts. While cold soya drinks can be slightly diluted, the desserts are excellent.
Recommended: Soya beancurd with ginkgo & lotus nuts, peach gum soup, taro peach gum soup, yam ball soya milk.

⸻

7. Unkai Japanese Cuisine (#01-88)

★★★★★ (5/5)

A great variety of bentos and set meals at wallet-friendly prices. The salmon bowl came with a generous piece of salmon on fluffy Japanese rice. Simple, satisfying, and good value. Will return to try more items.

⸻

8. Western Barbeque (#01-53)

★★★☆☆ (3/5)

Despite the long queues, the chicken chop didn’t stand out. No bun is provided, and the only sauce available was garlic sauce, which lacked flavour. Decent, but there are better western options nearby.

⸻

9. Famous Kallang Airport Fried Oyster (#01-55)

★★☆☆☆ (2/5)

Generous with oysters, but the omelette was overly oily. The excess oil overshadowed the dish. Still searching for a better fried oyster omelette.

⸻

10. Salt (#01-128)

★★★★☆ (4/5)

A western-style stall selling spaghetti, chicken chop, herbal chicken, and fried wings. I tried the Sous Vide Grilled Chicken with Aglio Olio. The aglio olio was decent, garlicky, and not too oily. The chicken chop was glazed with teriyaki sauce instead of the usual western sauces.
While acceptable, $9.90 feels expensive for a hawker centre given the portion and simplicity.

author: Lee Mijares
review_text:
The Old Airport Food Center was my first taste of hawker center dining in Singapore. There were so many choices that i found it hard to choose the food I want to eat! We settled at the first stall and ate fish and i found a stall at the back that sold beef stew and xia long bao. The place is spacious and there were a lot of people and black birds!
Tips: Save your spot near the entrance. Its breezy here with the giant fans. Avoid dining in the middle because its too warm. Also, take your tray and tableware to the shelves at the back as a courtesy to the next customers.
Food here us affordable. I only spent less than 8 dollars for my meal.

author: Lionel Tolmay
review_text: Great experience at the Old Airport Road Food center. I tried the Lor Mee as it seemed like everyone was having it. I also had a curry potato pie and it was fantastic!

author: Pauline Ng
review_text: Ordered fried black carrot cake, chicken curry prata, Michelle curry puff, satay, Hock Lian Huat Prawn Cracker & Ngoh Hiang. The famous hokkien prawn bee was closed when we arrived at 5:30 pm; ate from another stall.

author: Julius Tan
review_text:
Old Airport Road Food Centre, established in 1973, is a highly popular hawker food centre in Singapore. It boasts a wide array of stalls, each specializing in traditional local dishes, offering a diverse culinary experience that caters to all tastes. While the food centre may show signs of age and the environment is not the most hygienic, the quality of the food remains exceptional.

Notable stalls include Nam Sing Fried Hokkien Mee, Hua Kee and Cho Kee Wanton Mee, Whitley Road and Albert Street Prawn Noodle, Dong Ji and Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow, and the renowned Lor Mee, among many other famous hawkers.

author: GK T
review_text: Car-parking is by the new HDB parking app without the barrier. More lots are being made in view of the 24-hour NTUC supermarket that wld be located in the food centre. The carrot cake and the fried Hokkien mee are must-trys. Also, Ban Mian we got has evenly-sliced ban mian and well-cooked too as they don’t stick together.

author: Peiyi (Potato)
review_text: So far food is ok, not very wow. Mutton soup quite bland but meatball is nice. Live prawn noodles are good. Western barbecue is decent, old school western but I’m not a fan of the garlic sauce. Salt fried chicken quite salty and herbal soup isn’t very Gao but not as bland as the mutton soup. Charsiew from idk which stall is not bad. Nyonya chendol is nice

author: Loh Ricky
review_text:
One of my favourite hawker center, you can find plenty of local delights here and their price are reasonable too
You can take MRT to reach here, if im not wrong is Dakota station, short walking distant to the hawker centre. This hawker centre is very packed in the evening but there are many fan around so not very stuffy. There is a newly built Multi storey carpark, so drive to park here is more convenient now compare to last time.

author: L Chan
review_text: One of the most iconic hawker centres, known for its wide variety of local favourites & legendary stalls. Lively, spacious & full of heritage. Linked sheltered walkway to MSCP Block 49A. Expect long queues at famous stalls

author: Sam Kai Xiang
review_text: Well this is one of the best food court in singapore where you can get local delight for the true taste of Singapore !  The chicken rice here is underrated nice

author: Tottochan
review_text: Went after work hours and sad to find out some stores close at 7pm or before 7pm. Not many options left for dinner, especially those featured on blogs. Managed to order food but not our first choices.

author: Brandon Goh
review_text: Finally found the time to go back and eat at this hawker centre after the renovation. Noticed the wanton mee stall I regularly patronize  has shifted to the opposite side where Nam Sing Hokkien Mee is. Cho Kee wanton mee stall is still at the same location. But I noticed the uncle of the stall was there when I visited. I have never seen him there before since my younger days. I am 60 now and I used to stay around the food centre and visited regularly when I was a little kindergarten boy. I can still recognize uncle's face because he is exactly the same just grown older. Amazing! But the wanton mee is fabulous! QQQQQ LOH HAHAHAHA. The other stall is just as good though. Guess I have to go back more often to rotate eating wanton mee from both stalls!

author: Watcharapong Homprang
review_text:
I traveled from Thailand to visit Singapore during July 25–28, 2025.

On the morning of my last day, just before heading to the airport to fly back to Thailand, I stumbled upon the restaurant in this photo by chance. I didn’t know the name of the place, but I tried the food and it was really delicious. The young woman who was serving was also very lovely. It’s a pity I discovered this place on my last day—otherwise, I would have gone there every day!

author: Ken Tan
review_text: Exquisite Cafe - best lemon tea. This brings out the nuances and flavour of the lemon 🍋 in the tea

author: Marcus Nah
review_text:
Plenty of nice food.. if you see long queue just go for it..

But the hawker is rather quite noisy...

author: Sean Wang
review_text:
This place has countless options for food so there will be something for everyone; from barbeque chicken wings, desserts such as egg tarts, western food (mostly Hainanese), Chinese food (fried rice, soup dumplings, etc.), to Muslim food varieties. The portion size can vary according to which store you order from, as there are multiple stores that sell similar food items, and some with slightly different recipes which can change the texture and the taste profile.

As with all hawker centres, you will have to clear your tables and place the trays in the designated tray return area. It will definitely be noisy around the center area but there are seats where it's a little quieter in the edge spots if you want to have a quieter experience.

Expect the place to be crowded during lunch and dinner so finding a table can be difficult during these peak periods. You may have to share a table with others, so be polite and ask if they can share their table if you cannot find one. Otherwise, you can take your time to look for a seat while you wait for your food or come by during less crowded periods after 8pm or before 6pm. I went to this place around 7-8pm but I still managed to find a seat. Most of the stalls will give you a buzzer when you order so you can keep track of when your food is ready.

author: Joseph Chin
review_text: My review is on (not the food center) but L2 vendors. Many old time vendors have been there for over 40 years! And NTUC is opening an outlet too. But i like to promote one interesting used book stall run by a lady named Ah Fang very friendly and worthy of our browsing through and support oki

author: don Toh
review_text: Crowded place with a lot of foreigner these days. Find a seat may take some times but it maybe the shortest time spend there.

author: Tan Lai Heng
review_text: Many many choices of food to choose from. But if you are parking, might have limited spaces to park unless you park at the multi storey carpark.

author: Johnny Venom Blaze
review_text: 5 stars review cos they have the best Nasi lemak in Singapore! 786 nasi lemak is to die for!!!! Stall 01-34!!! Cheap value for money n your tummy!!!

author: Flo Yeow
review_text: With a rich history of excellent local food, Geylang East Hawker Centre remains a staple for the community. While it might not be the "best" hawker centre in Singapore, it is home to many stalls with impressive long queues that speak to their quality. It’s a reliable spot for a simple, authentic meal. If you live or work in the area, you should definitely check it out at least once!

author: L Chan
review_text: A long-running neighbourhood market & hawker centre built in the 1970s, with both wet market stalls & cooked food. Popular in the mornings & afternoons for affordable local eats, but like most heartland markets, most stalls close by late afternoon. By evening the place is dark & quiet, with only a handful of stalls still open. Recently upgraded with better flooring, lighting & ventilation, it remains a true community hub serving the daily needs of Geylang East.

author: Hatsune Miku
review_text: Living in the east and near Paya Lebar, this food centre is no stranger to me. But truth to be told, I dont really like this food centre. Most stalls here serve mediocre food, and the MacDonalds nearby might be a better food option. Yes, there is a rather famous stall selling duck and fish porridge, but it goes downhill from here. The carrot cake here sucks, kway chap sucks, nasi padang sucks, wanton mee sucks. And there is a very long list that goes on from here. The stalls that narrowly escape my wrath are the two congee stalls and pig organ soup. If you are not here for the duck and fish porridge, you shouldnt be here. Geylang East Market Food Centre is a total let down.

author: Chong Evon
review_text: Was there this morning for breakfast, very windy environment. I choose the vegetarian stall today. The zai-er super nice freshly fried  and combo with fried tofu and curry veg super delicious. Do support!

author: theresa heng
review_text:
Decided to have chee cheong fun for breakfast and it was really delicious. Best thing ever? I added char siew to my prawn CCF and it was only $0.50 for adding ingredient. Total price of fresh prawns+char siew CCF was $4.
Good value for money

author: HFZ
review_text: Wide range of food options, usually more popular stalls include Muslim food and drinks (nasi padang, mee bakso, teh halia teh pandan, etc.) and Chinese food (duck porridge, chicken rice). Western and Japanese food options also available although not really recommended, pretty average nothing special. Drinks are pretty affordable as compared to the nearby coffeeshops, wider range of beverages sold too.

author: Han Lee
review_text:
Many choices and quite cheap there. The place is also airy and huge. A good neighborhood food center.

Enjoyed the soya bean grass jelly drink. So many other food I wanna try!

author: Ls Lin
review_text: You can find number of tipical local food stalls here.  I tried traditional porridge with additional egg this morning,  worth for value

author: Deon Jong
review_text: Queued more than 30 minutes for the best braised duck. Queue is not very fast moving but it is worth the queue. Had it with rice alone and it was divine. Sauce was not overly salty and herbal tasted 👍🏻

author: tunicatelor
review_text: Decent selection of food. Not difficult to find a table before noon.

author: Jason Por How Tan
review_text: Lots of decent food options here. Special shout out to the 肉骨茶 stall at the last (outer) row of the hawker centre. Top quality and cheap price, definitely worth a shot.

author: Scarelion Tanned
review_text: Their Lo Mee no joke….thick and slurpy! Bonus points for self serve garlic and chilies 🤤

author: Tan Junyu
review_text: It just reopen after 3 mths renovation and it packed with people. Alot of people queuing for the pig organ soup, wanton mee and fishball noodles. Apity that bittergroud beef is overcooked, tough and too salty.

author: IP P
review_text:
Very dirty tables.

Cleaners are getting lazier nowadays despite almost no need to clear plates and trays from tables already.

Town concil and NEA dont bother about cleaniness and smokers smoking in the food centre Sat, Sun and PH 10am-12noon.

author: bh
review_text:
The food center is located in an older part of the estate border some light industrial zone.

There are some local favorites like Hokkien Mee, Porridge, etc. In all frankness, the cleanliness in this hawker center is not high, the whole dining environment is dark and gloomy in certain corners, the floor can be quite dirty at times too.

author: Feliz
review_text:
Awesome traditional Malay kueh Kueh,
try their epok epok ( potato curry puff and sardines puff )

Each cost $1 .

They started 10 years ago by selling their Kueh Kueh at the mama indian shop below their home .

Now they have their own stall ,  #01-45.

Open : 6.45am to 2pm
Everyday.

Enjoy 😋

author: Chong Yew Kee
review_text:
After breakfast

Ordered
Kopi Gao Gao 👍

Half boil eggs perfect timing 👍

Stall owners helped remove the egg shells
Excellent good service 👍

Stall No #01-48
New Leaf Coffee

Will definitely come back ❤️

author: jim teo
review_text:
This mee chiang kueh (stall #01-18) is good. Not too small, not too thin till it becomes flimsy, generous filling of peanuts and not too sweet compared other sellers from many other stalls at other places.
Fans of mee chiang kueh should not want to miss trying out this traditional food.

author: X D
review_text: This hawker centre has one of the best Porridge stall in Singapore Mei Xiang Porridge 01-34

author: WDG Dingguo
review_text: Classic hawker centre that was renovated. Better ventilation, seating and lighting

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Tini Seng
review_text: I takeaway regularly from this shop and I really enjoyed the thunder tea. However, recently I find that the thunder tea is salty. I usually will put the whole thing and mix with the ingredients. But yesterday, I added one scoop only and gave up the rest as it's too salty.  The caipo is also more salty and the ingredients more oily. Standard seems to have drop :(. Hope they will restore the standard otherwise will find other leicha store to try.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Doraemon
review_text:
Kitty and I were on the lookout for a lunch spot and turned to Google to find Lei Cha options, which led us to a highly-rated Lei Cha restaurant in the Geylang area. Our experience at this establishment was a mix of satisfaction and room for improvement. The Lei Cha dish, though flavorful, lacked the ideal temperature, not reaching the comforting warmth that would enhance its overall enjoyment. Additionally, the soup, while tasty, was a bit dilute, missing the robustness expected in traditional Lei Cha.

The service at the restaurant was commendable, with attentive staff creating a pleasant dining atmosphere. The presence of free-flow peanuts for self-service was a nice touch, adding to the welcoming ambiance. Pricing was reasonable, with white Lei Cha rice at four dollars fifty cents and brown rice at five dollars, a justifiable value.

During our meal, Kitty noted her preference for the Lei Cha served in the Punggol area. While the taste of the soup was similar at both places, she found that the soup at the reviewed establishment was slightly dilute in comparison. Nevertheless, she expressed a continual preference for the Lei Cha experience in one Punggol hawker centre.

The stall owner recommended their 客家南乳炸肉 (Hakka Fried Pork), which Kitty found to be very nice. If you visit this place, consider ordering this dish to enhance your dining experience.

Taking all aspects into account, including feedback on the dilute soup and rice temperature, we awarded the Geylang Lei Cha establishment a four-star rating. Our culinary journey highlighted areas of improvement for an even more enjoyable dining experience.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Oscar wong
review_text:
Very friendly staff, food is clean and super yummy!

Very fresh vegetables, definitely one of my favourite now ;-)

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: megan
review_text:
The place is more comfortable than others. It’s a standalone shop, near the temple and there’s a sheltered walkway from paya lebar square and the MRT.
I arrived at around 11.30 and there were people queuing for takeaways and eating there.

It’s also 50cents cheaper for the brown rice as compared to other leichas.

THEY ACCEPT CDC VOUCHERS!

THE TEA IS GOOD. Finally. It’s herby and you can see the seeds. It’s a little bit salty but not overly salty.
Everything else is cooked well too. They include haebi as well.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Shan Leong
review_text: Overall the taste was good 👍, have the authentic taste. The 南乳肉 and the 酿豆腐 was nice. Recommend to add on . 🤣 Service was fast and friendly. Location was easy to find, many parking lots around there. As for environment is non aircon and consider clean.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Reina
review_text: Food is very good. The most affordable and healthy lunch option you can find around paya lebar area. But they really should change their opening hours to 13:00 so it does not mislead anyone. Every time I come in just after 13:00, they are always sold out.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Yaw Zhe Syuen
review_text: I order leicha and yong taufu. The amount is pretty decent and the yong taufu is really tasty! Gotta thanks the boss for recommending it to me. Definitely will go back when I’m craving for leicha.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Jayon See
review_text:
One of the better Lei Cha in Singapore. Ingredients are all fresh and fragrant, the soup is aromatic and less salty, definitely on the healthier side.
Fried Pork in Fermented Tofu is a must try too, it is crispy and flavourful.
Price wise it is quite cheap in my opinion, and the portion given is almost huge.
The place is also clean and tidy, feels comfortable to dine in the shop.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: XY L
review_text:
Amazing food - very fragrant, nutty tea and rice mixed with fresh ingredients. The bonus was the pork belly! It’s a meal I love so much that I’d love to move my house closer to it.

I had them taken out and delivered before. Equally good!!!!

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Singer
review_text:
I try to frequent this place fortnightly or weekly, food has always been great and healthy

Two types of rice offered, White and Brown. There is also Fermented Pork on the menu and a sizeable piece of Meat Tofu specially on weekends. The Vegetarian option is with no Shrimp added to the regular Tofu served

Thanks for serving this area

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Joel Chan
review_text: Fragrant thunderbolt tea / soup which didn't taste too green-fy. The vegetables were fresh and crunchy. Overall, I really loved the meal and will definitely be back again. $5 for the brown rice thunderbolt tea set and add-on fried pork for $2

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: L Chen
review_text: One of the best hakka lui cha ever eaten!  Veggies so fresh and crunchy, soup so delicious!  The fried fermented pork belly is a little fatty but nicely seasoned and super tasty!  Happy meal $5 (brown rice), add fried pork $2.  Awesome, love it, will be back again soon for more!

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: JW
review_text:
I love lei Cha in general but this Lei Cha has such good review for a good reason!
Simply delicious!! However, I find it too filling so I usually request for no rice and it is just nice for me ☺️ Price is super reasonable too!

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Jim J
review_text:
A very small eatery, just 10 mins walk from paya lebar mrt.

Healthy vegetarian alternative.
Very crunchy & with free slow peanuts. You can order fermented pork if you want some meat.

I quite like their lei cha but the tea., it may not be to everyone's liking.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Glen Ho
review_text:
Woah.. "flavour bomb in a bowl" is how I'd describe the thunder tea rice here.

Ordering is pretty straight forward and instructions on the board are pretty self explanatory. You get to pick between fragrant or brown rice, and also to add peanuts or not.

Serving size is very value for money and every element of the dish just mixes together to create one bowl of awesomeness.

Location is in a quiet corner of paya lebar, and is more convenient to access by car, with car parking lots in the blocks behind. I greatly appreciate how clean the location is overall too.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Lee Poco
review_text: Small corner shop selling the best lei cha in Singapore! Recommend the brown rice and add the extra fried pork belly if you like.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Vidya Andarikha
review_text: One of the best thunder tea rice I've tried. Their portion is huge, my jaw felt a bit sore after munching all those veggies, but it's worth it!

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Zelrick Kun
review_text: One of the best LeiCha I had in Singapore. Although LeiCha isn't for everyone, their LeiCha isn't overpowered by the "grassy green" smell. Worth trying if you are sick of having greasy food and looking for healthier option.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Kit Lim
review_text: Been buying takeaway from them for few years. Noticed today the vegetables ingredient is so much lesser. Always tell my frens this place gives lot of ingredients.

restaurant: Thunderbolt Tea by Boon Lay Traditional Hakka Lui Cha
author: Ed K
review_text: A simple lunch at a self service coffee shop or sort. A special healthy food that a friend introduced. Food Quality A+ n Quantity A Service None

author: SoJuNey
review_text: Cheap, good, and vibrant! So many types of food, but we started with the classics of chicken rice and shrimp satay. Winner winner chicken dinner. Will come back to try other things. Some places take cards but better to be safe to bring cash. Short walk to catch the light show at Marina Bay.

author: Mackaz Sajiaos Tan
review_text:
Lau Pa Sat is easily one of my favourite places to enjoy a meal in Singapore. The moment you step inside, you’re greeted with the lively sights and smells of truly local food. From satay and chicken rice to laksa and char kway teow, it’s a place where you can taste the heart of Singapore in one stop.

What I love most is how Lau Pa Sat brings together both locals and tourists. It’s a must-visit spot for anyone wanting to experience authentic Singapore flavours, and yet it still feels like a gathering place for everyday Singaporeans. The atmosphere is always warm and buzzing, especially when the satay street opens at night.

On top of all the good food, Lau Pa Sat is full of history. Housed in a beautiful historic building with its iconic cast-iron architecture, it’s a reminder of Singapore’s past blending seamlessly with its modern city life. Eating here feels like enjoying a meal inside a piece of the nation’s heritage.

A vibrant mix of flavours, culture, and history — Lau Pa Sat never disappoints. Perfect for both first-time visitors and anyone who loves great local food.

author: Z M
review_text: Lau Pa Sat FOR THE WIN... forget going to restaurants and paying a premium. Go to Lau Pa Sat and try all the delicious mix Regional food that Singapore has to offer. In one very clean very, affordable spot. You could try Korean, Indian, Chinese, middle eastern all-in-one go. Fan at night it turns in to satay street. Great food and awesome atmosphere. You'll have a great time whether you're with family friends or a Solo Traveler.

author: Paul Ciprian
review_text:
A more elegant, cleaner hawker center than most of the others in Singapore (personally, I have never seen a more beautiful and clean one). The tables and chairs are no longer so cheap and fixed to the floor. That cheap canteen atmosphere is missing here.
The building, a historical monument, is very beautiful. In the evening, especially, the atmosphere is very nice. Inviting smells, a very varied offer, garlands with lights that remind of Christmas, but also crowded. A place you must try!

author: E H
review_text:
On Christmas Eve, we had dinner at Lau Pa Sat, an iconic hawker centre housed in its distinctive octagonal cast-iron structure, recognised as a national monument.

With around 80 food stalls, it truly offers something for everyone. From chilli crab and dumplings to teppanyaki, the range of Asian cuisines is impressive—I even got a little lost trying to find our table. My 82-year-old mother couldn’t stop talking about the egg tarts for days.

Just outside is the open-air Satay Street, where the entire road is lined with tables and chairs and around ten satay stalls. The smoky aroma from the grills is irresistible and naturally draws you in.

Some may say it’s a tourist spot, but I’m proud to be a tourist. Places like this are exactly why we travel, and we absolutely loved the experience.

author: Sumarno Khoo
review_text: Although the location is very touristy, Lau Pa Sat food center is one of the most organised and comfortable hawkers center in Singapore. The outlets are very well curated in terms of quality and varieties and the seatings are adequate and spacious.

author: Rola Daoud
review_text: Def a MUST VISIT!! Huge variety of food that you don’t know where to start!! You do have to hunt for a table but it’s so much fun with a big group. Food prices are very affordable and the food is delicious. There is something for everyone. Highly recommend the bbq meat and squid skewers. And the traditional rice with chicken and veges on the side. Variety of drink options. Such a vibe and great experience.

author: Rulita & Nikola
review_text:
Lau Pa Sat is a fantastic place to experience Singapore’s food scene in one spot. There’s a huge variety of food options, so everyone can find something they like, and the quality is consistently good.

The atmosphere is lively, especially in the evening, and sitting outside adds to the experience. It’s a great place to try different dishes without having to move around the city.

Perfect for food lovers and a must-visit if you want to taste many flavors of Singapore in one go.

author: Mano Recto
review_text:
The satay experience at Lau Pa Sat is simply unforgettable — a true slice of Singapore’s street food culture. As soon as the sun sets and the grills light up, the air fills with that irresistible smoky aroma of spice and charcoal.

I ordered from Best Satay Stall No. 8 — the chicken, beef, and shrimp satay were all excellent. The meats were juicy and well-marinated, with that perfect char from the grill. The shrimp satay was especially good — plump, sweet, and cooked just right, paired perfectly with the rich peanut sauce.

It’s vibrant, crowded, and a little smoky, but that’s exactly the charm. Great food, lively energy, and a fantastic night-out experience under the city lights.

author: John Chong
review_text:
5-Star Rating for the amazing variety of food from all over the world !!
All my favourite Singapore dishes are also available. Chicken Rice, Biryani, Nasi Lemak, Mee Pok, Dim Sum, Ban Mian, Mee Soto, Prata, Thosai and of course Satay.

Lots of international options including Turkish, Indian, Fillipino, Indonesian, Western, Korean and more.

And all at reasonable prices.

Only downside, place can get quite warm during the day as its not air-conditioned

author: Kelly V
review_text:
I went here late at nine really great atmosphere. The first thing I saw was Sapporo beer on draft so I had to get a pint or two!

Then went to fried buns and had the chilli oil dumplings with noodles. The noodles were absolutely delicious just the right amount of chewiness. The chilli probably could’ve been a bit spicy.

For dessert, brownie cheesecake, also could’ve eaten two slices so good.

Overall experience would recommend !

author: aye phoo
review_text: This food center is much cleaner and more organized than other places. We got chili crab 🦀 and it was nice. But my highlight would be the sambal stingray from Homg Kong live seafood stall. So many food options! Wish i could try all. The sugarcane juice with lemon is not tasty though. The shop watered it down. I can’t taste any sugarcane flavor.

author: Catherine
review_text:
A large local-style hawker area suddenly appears in the middle of central Singapore, and the atmosphere is great. Even though it’s designed for tourists, it still keeps the charm of a real hawker and feels very comfortable.

We tried several dishes, and the Indonesian satay was especially tasty. One downside was that the beer pitchers were different sizes even though we ordered the same item.

The place was clean, but since many foods are eaten with your hands, tissues weren’t always available. It’s better to request some or bring your own.

Overall, it was an enjoyable tourist experience.

author: Rachel
review_text: A great cultural experience. The food was great. First night we ate inside the hawker stall with a lot of choices tho lacking dessert options. Second night we went back for satay and otah. The street is closed after 5pm and many rows of tables and grills are setup for satay.  On a cool night it’s a great experience.

author: Anshika Singla
review_text:
Great place to visit while in singapore..
U will get every type of cuisine Indian, Chinese, French, Thai, continental, Mexican, Asian.
Also there are good seafood options. Even desserts and drinks are amazing.
So a must try place.
Closes at nearly 9pm.

author: Kiran B
review_text: Lau Pa Sat is an absolute must-visit in Singapore,an iconic food haven that perfectly blends heritage charm with an unbeatable variety of flavours. The moment you step in, the vibrant atmosphere, sizzling satay stalls, and endless food options pull you right in. From perfectly grilled satay to delicious local specialties and international bites, every dish feels fresh, authentic, and full of character. With great seating, lively nightlife vibes, and food that never disappoints, Lau Pa Sat delivers an unforgettable dining experience every single time.

author: Ilaria Mariani
review_text:
Amazing variety of food and such a lively atmosphere! We went multiple times during our stay and always had a great experience—tried grilled seafood, Korean dishes, Chinese classics, and more. Every time, the food was delicious.

The setting is very cozy and comfortable, with a traditional market-style vibe where you simply grab what you want from a stall and enjoy it anywhere in the hall. Outside, the street transforms into an open-air dining area in the evening, which is super nice with a great view of the city’s skyline—it’s really something special.

Very much suggested if you want to enjoy authentic flavors in a unique and vibrant environment. A must-visit food destination in Singapore!

author: Badar Khoirul Imam
review_text: Lau Pa Sat is one of those places in Singapore that you instantly fall in love with. The moment you step in you will feel the lively ambience with delicious aromas floating from every corner. It is the perfect spot to enjoy local flavors especially if you love exploring food like most Indonesian travelers

author: Rory York
review_text:
We ate here a few times and definitely recommend it.

Satay street is worth doing too, atmosphere a lot nicer outside than inside. Not that the inside is bad, just noisy at times.

Check captions for names of food recommendations.

author: Nickin Sitaram
review_text:
Wow wow wow... What a street and atmosphere. It was fantastic to be there and absorb the great vibes.

The famous satay street lived up to it's expectations, it was just lovely.

It's really important to add how clean it was.
