Considering the number of people and satay sticks they must go through.. the place was again immaculately clean with no rubbish on the floor and the tables constantly clearer. The culture is to clean after yourself. One that should be adopted here back in England.

The satay was fantastic. The stalls say it's all the same but there is a clear winner with massive queues for it. Definitely visit this.

We had chicken, pork, lamb and prawns. Beautifully cooked and full of flavour. More importantly, no stomach issues experienced by any of the family. Win win.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Minkytreswa
review_text: Old school but clean and bright environment. Plenty of parking when we arrived at 6.30pm. Fast and friendly service. We ordered Assam fish, baby squid, deep fried pork, salted egg prawn, steamed garlic squid, coffee pork rib, deep fried mushroom with Kailan, sambal kangkong with cuttlefish, bak kut teh, crispy chicken. Total of 8 paxs. Dishes were all good. Herbal bak kut teh a bit too light for my liking. We ordered quite a lot of beer too. Bill came up to $360. Got too greedy during meal halfway and forgot to take quite a few dishes. Will be back again for sure

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Mun Chong
review_text:
Cabbage chicken - weekend only dish - chicken probably double boiled wrapped in cabbage leaves. Cabbage leaves were close to melting (highlight #1 of dinner)
Garlic steamed sotong - a bit sweet
Onion omelette - nicely cooked
Chinese spinach cooked with 3 types egg - highlight#2 of dinner
Fried noodles
Fried rice
Recommended condiments were sambal chilli, fresh red chilli and freshly minced garlic - highlight #3

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: YKC
review_text:
Free parking along the road is no more. Gantry carpark by G-Tech.
Should have stick to the potain bak ku teh.
Tried the following dishes.
String bean fried ok, Assemblies fish not so fresh, dry and asam sauce too thick. Coffee spare ribs ok, but Clayton tofu can be improved.
Rice is of low quality type. How expensive is the rice that you need to lower your standards?
The JB vibes no more after gantry installed.

Beside this aircon restaurant, there is a non aircon restaurant seems to have a much bigger crowd.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Chong Tee Lim
review_text:
Goodyear Seafood Village Tampines offers a lovely destination for family and friend gatherings in a laid back kampong style setting. The restaurant’s Pontian style herbal bak kut teh, served in a claypot, is fragrant and flavourful with a herbal depth that’s lighter than Teochew versions but balanced with garlic and ginseng. The ribs are firm yet tender and absorb the broth beautifully, making it a satisfying shared dish.

Aside from bak kut teh, the zi char menu shines. The Assam fish head is a standout with a tangy spicy sauce made from scratch that delivers a satisfying depth. It showcases fresh sea bass served with vegetables and pineapple. Other highlights include golden garlic pork, prawn paste chicken, cabbage chicken claypot, hotplate tofu and salted egg yolk pork ribs. Portions are generous and flavours bold enough for sharing.

The ambience is rustic and peaceful. Dining here feels like stepping into a Malaysian kampong with open air seating and greenery around. The venue is spacious with both indoor and outdoor seating options, making it family friendly.

Service is casual and warm though not highly polished. Staff are generally friendly. Parking can be a challenge on weekends and reservations are wise if dining in larger groups. Delivery and takeaway through WhatsApp is also available if you prefer to enjoy the food at home.

Overall experience offers great value. Expect to spend around 8 to 13 dollars per bowl for bak kut teh, with zi char mains starting from 12 dollars depending on size. The generous portions, rich herbal broth, and standout dishes like Assam fish head and prawn paste chicken make it worth the slight effort to travel out a bit.

For family or friend gatherings this is a solid choice with delicious dishes suited to sharing, affordable pricing, relaxed vibe, and a touch of rustic charm you don’t often find in the city.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Thomas low
review_text:
Good Year Seafood Restaurant is always my choice when thinking having a nice meal together with group of friends .

The restaurant is clean and spacious with friendly staff and boss .

Food tasty and fresh ingredients and the prices is very reasonable 😀

Good Year Seafood Restaurant definitely worth to visit 😀

Garlic pork 👍
Curry 🐠 Head 😋
🦪 🥚😋

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: YappariStory
review_text: Every dish is extremely delicious and the meal is inexpensive. We only paid about SGD 160 for 7 dishes and beverages (family of 8 pax). The staff and the bosses are also very service-oriented and amiable.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Frankey
review_text: Today, we went there for Father’s Day dinner. Their yam paste with Gingko nuts is like our childhood taste. I will sure return for the yam paste! It’s so nice!  The damage is only $176.00 for 5 pax.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Sing Wee Choo
review_text:
Passed by, and thought to try try. Had the seafood hor fun as a taste test. (for me, any good Tzi char place must first serve a good seafood hor fun. Generous servings of sotong, fish slices, 2 medium prawns... (none of the fish cake slices nor tiny prawn nonsense you find in those other franchise-type Tzi char...) Wok hey gao gao.... Yummy. Will be back with family to try more of the menu. Will review ratings...
Crowded on weekends. Call to reserve seats. Charges GST.

Another visit, tried lala bee hoon, ee mee and potato leaves... Yummy!

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Manong Josh
review_text: Mediocre non-pepperish and less taste BKT. Ambience is nice but more noisier now due to new road. Food is normal not like before but still acceptable.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Lorelai D
review_text:
One of us have been talking about this BKT place for the longest time, reminiscing the BKT that he has tried, so we decided to head over there.

I see a few tables order BKT and also curry fish head, but it will be a bit much for us, so we decided to go for chai po egg, BKT, salted egg yolk pork ribs and also spinach with eggs. Only after we ordered that we discovered we have pretty much ordered a dinner full of eggs LOL.

Chai Po egg was okay, goes well with the chili, can’t really go wrong with this one, it tasted like home cooked, I do wish that it comes thicker which will compliment the other dishes better.

Spinach with 3 eggs, which are eggs, salted egg and century egg was well done, the broth was really nice and the salted egg yolk pork ribs were tender, just like how it usually come in.

As to the highlight which was suppose to be the BKT, it was more on the herbal side, good generous amount of ingredients. I do wish that the herbal flavor can be a bit stronger but the ribs that goes with it was tender. The perks of going to a proper BKT shop is they will refill the soup for you, which you don’t get it here, however still a good bowl of BKT and you get to also order other zhi char dishes which is easy to order when you come as a family.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Sarah Wong
review_text:
Came here on a Thurs evening so there is no parking issue. It’s our first time. The service is friendly, and the food is VERY good. I’m not sure if this sounds comprehensible, but we can taste the “labour of love” from the chef(s)? Some food is prepared “simply because” it’s an order, but some food, tho’ simple, like homecooked food by a loving Grandma, can be tasted. Goodyear’s food is like that.

We ordered lala beehoon, yuanyang kwaytiao, spiced pork, sweet potato leaves and prawn rolls. Except for the veggie, the rest are signature dishes. Bill is $87 including tea.

For the food quality and portion, rural town vibe, cleanliness (old but clean), plus warm service, the price is reasonable.

Will definitely be their repeated diners 🤣

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Andy Lee
review_text:
Food is great. Love the prawn, and those who love spicy will love the curry fish head.
Only one complaint. We had an appointment, but was only seated after 30min delay. Add another 15min before we could place our order. By the time we eat, it was after a hour wait. Understaff, but the employees are friendly.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: opo c
review_text: Can’t believe i hadn’t tried this place before.  Food was really nice.  Monday had special offer on fish head curry and they did not skimp on quantity or quality as the fish was really fresh.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: JH
review_text: Big seating area, some are air-conditioned and some are alfresco. Food was really good, especially the golden garlic fried pork. Wanted to try the cabbage chicken but portion was too big for 4 of us, definitely will come back to try.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: LP Pua
review_text:
We are exploring various Zi Char stalls and seafood restaurants in Singapore with 4-star ratings on Google Maps. Although this restaurant had a 3.9-star rating, we decided to give it a try due to its unique JB-like location.

The Kai Lan was of the same standard as other Zi Char stalls. The Golden Garlic Spiced Pork, a dish we hadn’t seen elsewhere, turned out to be the star of the meal. The weekday dinner promotion, Fragrant Garlic Chicken, was crispy, sweet, and enjoyable. However, the Curry Fish Head was the Assam Curry type, which wasn’t to our preference. Rice was slightly pricier than average at $1.20.

While there is a 9% GST, there’s no service charge. Overall, the experience had more hits than misses.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Cadell Teng
review_text: Fantastic food and atmosphere at reasonable prices. Perfect for large family gathering and dinner. Table size for 4 to 8 available.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Sheue Lin Ng
review_text: Ordered a lot of dishes to try. Few favourites. Assam fish curry, the sauce was thick and very flavorful. Crispy pork with garlic. This dish is delicious. The batter on the pork is light and fluffy. It's loaded with lots of garlic.  The crispy chicken was bit too salty.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Jowe Chu
review_text: Yummy food and quick service. Crowded but we got seated quickly on a Saturday. Ordered fried garlic pork, prawn paste chicken and oyster omelette. The fried dishes are v crispy and nice. The omelette has a nice chili crab like sauce.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Sky leo
review_text: First I was surprised to hear this place, the Bak Kut Teh soup can only add once. Then after adding, it didn’t even reach half of the claypot. The waitress attended to us still argue this is the standard. Quite disappointed with this restaurant.

restaurant: GoodYear Seafood Village Tampines (Zi Char and Bak Kut Teh)
author: Scott Bender
review_text: Real local place,food atmosphere. The staff understand your English-speaking better than you think.  Point to pictures. You share dishes among the group.

author: Parthipan Somasundaramm
review_text:
No Respect for Customers – Extremely Poor Service

I spent $56 at this restaurant and was appalled by the service. The waiting time was around 30 minutes, which was frustrating enough.
After finishing my meal, I asked to pack the leftovers. The staff gave me a flimsy plastic sheet—free, but entirely unsuitable and unpleasant for takeaway.
Will this owner of the restaurant accept this plastic cover?

When I asked for a proper container, they told me it would cost 20 cents. I paid because I had no choice, but charging for something so basic after such a large bill is a clear sign of disrespect.
The staff member (wearing glasses) was dismissive and lacked any form of professionalism or courtesy.

This experience wasn’t just about the 20 cents—it was about a complete lack of respect for customers. No transparency, no hospitality, and no effort to make customers feel valued. I will never return, and I strongly advise others to think twice before dining here.

author: Esther Kong
review_text: My good to place for well-prepared tzi char. The staff are friendly and the chef is very experienced, especially when preparing crab dishes. Do call to reserve if you want to try out any crab dishes.

author: Loh Soon Shan
review_text:
Kimly Seafood is perfect for a festive CNY feast! The Vegetarian Salmon YuSheng was fresh and flavorful, the XO Sauce Smoked Duck Fried Rice rich and aromatic, and the Prawn Paste Mid-Wings were crispy and juicy.
Loved their Scratch & Win campaign—spend $45 for a chance to win up to $11,000 in cash and prizes. Great food, fun vibes, and exciting rewards! Highly recommend!

author: Yw T
review_text: Waiting time is on average 30min, food is ok normally but i got the salted egg fish today and it was void of any salted egg sauce and fish is overfried

author: ツLim
review_text:
Zichar takes minimally 30 mins to prepare so be mentally ready, taste wise very bad for zichar too...
drinks stall the drinks are SO DILUTED! Cannot taste any tea or coffee.
I think the only good store here is the Western food

author: Maya D
review_text: If you're looking for an affordable meal with fast service, Kimly is a good option. The food is okay, but the value is definitely there

author: Alex
review_text: We came here for the CNY set reunion dinner. Food is average only. The steam fish has a foul smell and in the end it was only replaced by fried chicken wings which is not worth the money we paid for the set dinner. I would rather they refund us the money for the steam fish rather than replacing it with some cheap dish. Will not come back here again for their set dinner. There are cheaper and better tasting options elsewhere.

author: Cheryl Lee
review_text: The western is better than other places i feel, had the salmon and chicken cutlet. The sides are pretty good, macaroni cheese, mash potatoes and coleslaw.

author: Wong Kean siong
review_text: "Terrible experience at Kimly Zi Char! Ordered food and it was completely wrong. Tasted awful, like it was leftover from yesterday. Worst part was waiting 40 minutes for the food with no apology or update from staff. Definitely won't be back."

author: Mei
review_text: The food was fine, but the service could be improved—we had to wait over 10 minutes for our drinks, and even when our food arrived, the drinks still hadn’t been served.

author: Keith Lim
review_text: Decent selection of food.  The nasi lemak store is serves good nasi lemak and their carrot cake is really nice

author: Chng Philip
review_text: The worst minced pork noodles in town. The cook at 0520am not interested in cooking. Wanted A but given otherwise!! Buy from this stall at your own risk. In the end, I throw away the entire bowl of noodles away which was so soft!! Thank u for making breakfast a wonderful one.

author: Jennifer
review_text: The chicken here is always a let down. Full of flour and no meat inside. Tomato egg has shell inside. Wasted money on such low quality food.

author: chip soon ng
review_text: Newly opened JWS Grille Factory: The patty in Hawaian Pork burger was grilled to the right juciness. The yuzu fries is a must-try. The yuzu mayonnaise, with actual bits of yuzu zest you can see, adds the perfect tangy taste to the plain fries. If you are not too hungry, go for the 2 pieces chicken wings with 1 side (sweet potato fries recommended).

author: Kelvin Cheung
review_text:
Food taste: Their fried rice, fried noodles, bee hoon, hor fun taste have all deteriorated, blend and doesn't taste nice anymore.

Food price: Don't ever order medium size ones. Charged double the price, give a bigger box without much quantity increase. Just order 2 small packets for better value.

Service: They are always rushing and usually very grouchy.

author: Daren
review_text: BLOODY LONG WAIT. Don’t come if you don’t want to wait. Has been 1 hour and not a single dish has been served.

author: Jeffrey Lim
review_text:
Worse place to order food. Do not patronise even if there's nothing else available. They made us wait for so long and in the end told us it's not even being cooked after we had enquired.
Frankly don't even deserve 1 star.

author: Goh Siauleng
review_text:
The staff said this is “cooked” 🥱
Who dare to eat 😥
Blk 742 , very bad service..

author: Amanda Ang
review_text: Ordered our food and waited for 2 hours via foodpanda. Called them but food wasn’t prepared at all & they mentioned that it’s on the way, but it was not. They forgotten to prepare our food. We asked what time the food will be ready but the lady who answered the call kept giving us generic replies “I asked them to cook already”. We told them we will complain, and the lady just told us to complain. Very disappointed with the poor customer service & for such dishonesty.

author: Jeff Chua
review_text: Prawn cheong fun turned out to be an impostor. It was dry and hard, more like 虾米 cheong fun.

author: Yvonne Tan
review_text:
This hawker centre is pretty airy. To avoid the crowd and queue, best to come before 8am, both weekdays and weekends.

If you are a wanton mee lover, wouldn't want you to miss this - Xing Ji wanton noodle!
Its mee gia served is springy (al-dente), veg given is always fresh (unlike many wanton stalls that sell "old" caixin that is "too fibrous" to swallow) & wanton size is just nice - bite-sized. Paired up with its boss' homemade chilli, it's simply heaven! It's usually sold out fast (esp Mon, before 11am) on weekdays.Closed on Tue & Wed. For weekends, best to arrive before 12pm to grab a bowl.
Xing Ji is definitely a good food rep for SG-style wanton mee in Tampines.
Note: If u r into HK-style noodles, this may not be for you.

Next must-try: Thosai, Appam
@ Rajarani Thosai.
Another long queue if you come after 8am.. every thosai is served fresh n piping hot. It's no wonder its queue never stops (unless sold out, oc)

For nice aromatic local nanyang kopi, go for Quan Fang. $1.40 for Kopi - ask for di lo siew dai (di lo: direct down; siew dai: less sweet) - then u can savour the pure goodness of the kopi with condensed milk added.
Ask for Kopi-O, if u just wanna enjoy a cuppa coffee with only sugar.
No sugar option? Ask for:
Kopi-O Kosong

Xiong Kee fried carrot cake (2 stalls - one operated by a couple, the other operated by their son) is another go-to if you enjoy a savoury plate of fried black or white carrot cake. Both stalls are yummylicious. The other carrot cake stall on the other side of the market is pretty good too, offering tumeric option.

For glutinous rice lovers, can try the stall located right behind the Tiong Bahru fried fish ball, Yi Le Shu Shi.

Oh ya.. the Chai Chee Pork porridge is for you, if you fancy thick savoury bowl of porridge, cooked to perfection.

Each portion is of reasonable size, so if you have a smaller stomach space, best to come with a few friends so you can try all the different stalls. If not, just make a few more trips!

author: Hatsune Miku
review_text: Another over-rated food centre. Most of the food here is either average or below average. Nothing fancy here that taste good. Honourable mentions here are the nasi lemak and fried carrot cake. So bad, that i almost puked my food out. Not going to call these stalls out, but you know who you are. Did I mention how arrogant the people selling the sarawak kolo mee are? Overall, I have not had much good experiences here at this food centre. But the fishball noodles at Hui Lai is pretty decent, and I think is one of the better stalls there.

author: Elatse
review_text: Tampines Round Market is a fantastic spot for fresh food at unbeatable prices. The market is always clean and well-maintained, making it a pleasant experience for shoppers. I love the variety of stalls offering everything from fresh produce to delicious cooked meals. The atmosphere is lively, with friendly vendors ready to help you find what you need. It’s a great place to explore local flavors without breaking the bank. Parking can be a bit tricky during peak hours, but it’s worth the visit for quality and affordability. Highly recommend for anyone looking to enjoy authentic local cuisine!

author: Cheong Loong
review_text: A nostalgic food place where one can find most hawker food of the past under one roof. My fave stalls are the dry chillie prawn noodles , sarawak mee  with your choice of ingredients. Local finds like fried carrot cake, nasi lemak, mee siam, prata, sugar cane, fried fish balls and chinese dessert . A family n friends hang out during  weekends. Do come early and not be disappointed, as most stalls start in the morning n food run out by lunch time.

author: Doris Chen
review_text: The Round Market is very crowded on weekends morning. The food price is reasonable while the taste is mediocre.

author: Dawn Tan
review_text: It's a food centre, so no, no impeccable service but definitely friendly. Atmosphere here in the morning is great thou. Very friendly neighbourhood. Lotsa great food to choose from. Fried fritters, desserts, noodles/rice/porridge, chwee kuey, char kuey (only $2.50! And is on the 2025 makansutra guide), drinks...

author: crystal
review_text:
the food is good here!! ALSO, very cheap!! lots of varieties. also, besides the hawker/wet market there are a lot of other amenities.

this place honestly feels so nostalgic, i've been here so many times and it really is a part of singaporean culture!! i would recommend to tourists as the local food here is great!!

author: Brad Marvine
review_text: A busy food court that has a wide range of scrumptious food. The area is very crowded, especially during peak hours (lunch and dinner). Service is pretty good!

author: Leslie Teo
review_text: The Econ beehoon stall is cheap and good. The Kolo Noodle stall has great delicious options and the noodles are served in a unique metal plate. Most of the coffee stalls serve good traditional coffee.

author: Terry Lim
review_text: had this pork rib noodles, decent but the food in this market are more exp than average i feel. the food quality in this place is decent at best not amazing either. tried many stalls but nothing wowed me except a malay stall at the outer ring of the hawker with long queue

author: Treasure Pot
review_text: Good variety of food. Sunday brunch , carpark was full but the wait was quite fast.tried the spicy fried black carrot cake at stall #01-17, good taste cost $3.50. the iced kop at $1.70. the food centre is spacious and windy seated outer seats facing shoplots. The pork and prawn noodle soup is a must try cost $4.5 with generous ingredients and tasty soup.

author: YS Cheng
review_text: Quite a number of nice stalls to choose from but they usually closed very early. I reached around 1pm and most of the stalls already closed. This hawker centre is rather old so ambience is not that pleasant. Food wise was okay.

author: Syed Ahmad Alkaff (Armodeco)
review_text:
As a person looking for halal, there are not much options. But the options you have are not bad. Can't go wrong with nasi lemak or nasi padang etc. Prices on average for a cheap meal is $4 which is the best part.

All in all 7.5/10 !

author: Dee Kwok
review_text: Loads of good hawker stalls at the round market - prawn noodles, fried carrot cake, those, fish ball, kolo noodles, youtiao, lotong/mee siam (this stall has super chip wings too!), and lots more to try!

author: Agnes “ManKiller” Sem
review_text: My friend recommended me this fishhead steamboat here. The soup tastes good with the charcoal fired soup. Think they called it chilli prawn, cooked with tofu is nice as well.  I love fish so i am open to try all places for good soup n fish. I had red grouper here.  I always love song fish.

author: Gordon Wong
review_text:
Needless for food pictures as this well-known Round Hawker Center filled with choice of great local meals.

But since government guidelines of clearing and returning our own trays after meals, tables are often left dirty and staining wet for most cleaners consider not their job in ensuring table cleanliness no more.

Here is a differing fact on a weekend morning packed with breakfast crowd while the Cleaners been busy pushing their trolley of plates & bowls for wash central, but also making time going around to help customer wiping tables for their meals.

This way, there are more table turnovers to serve timely.

Will definitely make this a top choice for my weekend breakfast places.

author: Joe Lim
review_text: Sarawak Kolo Mee Stall offers one of the best wonton-based noodles in the East. This is the second time I came at the last minute before they closed and the owner was kind enough to take my order. We ordered the Kolo Mee which comes with braised pork ribs. The noodles are QQ and the soup stock is rich and umami flavoured. The dry wonton noodles with char siew and fried/boiled wonton is a winning flavour bomb. The chilli oil sauce is spicy, umami and flavourful. I will definitely come back again. The owner is very friendly and welcoming. Kudos to that despite slogging from dawn till 2pm+ 🙏

author: Christopher de la cruz
review_text: classic go-to for breakfast if youre eastside or tampines.. i always go here for my Lor-Mee cravings.. the 137 Lor Mee..

author: HooiChew Tan
review_text:
Year 2018: Many good choices of Hawker food with reasonable price. Crowded and hard to get a parking during weekend. Unfortunately, A bit dirty at the tray return area as birds flying around there search for leftover food as the return trays was not collected promptly and send to wash immediately. Wish this can be improved for better hygiene for the eaters. 3 stars 🌟 rating for year 2018.

Year 2022: Good Sarawak Kolo Mee, long queue. The birds 🐦 eating leftover food around tray return area shelves not found during this visit. Wish this will not happen anymore. With this upgraded it to 4 stars 🌟 rating for the improved hygiene ambience at tray returns area.

Year 2023: Table never clean after other eaters left. Terrible table cleanliness and clean response time. Zero 🌟 for the table cleaning response time. After years still no significant and game-changing improvements.  Bad table cleaning frequency.  You want everyone come bring their own tissue paper to clean by themselves????

author: Joshua Wong
review_text: Prawn noodles and kolo mee both always long queue. Both good but I like the pigs tail soup from prawn noods stall more. Malay food and nasi legal stalls also very decent. If only they could solve the parking issues during peak times.

author: Hermione Le
review_text: I personally like this place as there are only local food with local price, amazingly enjoyable. We got roasted chicken rice, teh alia, sugar cane juice and kuay teow which were all so good.

author: Muhammad Husain
review_text: Best place for breakfast, cooling and have alot of choice. All drinks stall serve good drinks teh Tarik and kopi. Food depends on the vendor but can say better that most hawkers, price is very reasonable.

author: Jason Choo
review_text: Avoid Malek satay , we ordered 2 mee rebus and 1 gado gado . Both was Luke warm and mee rebus soggy and quite tasteless . Gado gado was not boiled and covered with Luke warm sauce too .operators seems disinterested and when showed a dirty cutlery in the holders, she just threw that one in pail . Attitude was cold and unbothered . Avoid

author: CK Melody
review_text: Fried bananas are best! They have different sizes and prices. They have alot of bbq food, satay, carrot cake, hokkien mee, wanton mee, chicken rice, drinks. Abit hot. Alot of birds. Can come here to eat. They have a famous special big cheng teng. Super alot of ingredients. Got hot and cold version. Can support!

author: Wan Nur Sabrina Wan Mohd Mustafa
review_text:
I’m from Terengganu, Malaysia. I love this area food centre, tak crowded sangat macam dekat Geylang. But i hope, all the shop owner open on Monday. Because normally tourist/visitor still in Singapore on Monday . Better close the shop on Tuesday @ Wednesday.
Today i plan to have Hokkien Fried Mee today before we going back to Terengganu. But its closed. 😭😭😭😭

author: Din Neo
review_text: Lots of delicious Halal food here! I love it... The food is good and tastes great! There are many choices of food, kueh and drinks here. This place is a legend! Highly recommended!

author: mark Lim
review_text: It’s a hawker Center. Don’t expect super clean tables and NO birds. Nice breakfast place especially for Malay food stalls. Very obvious which ones are the popular ones. A few non halal food stalls. A very short ride (5mins) to ECP via Bedok underpass which u will end up near OBS campus.

author: Warqah Neufal
review_text: Almost all stalls sell some form of satay dish. As always, tables almost full of patrons. Not wheelchair friendly place. But quality & selection of food had vastly improved. (Together wth the price hike.) Still best!

author: Mohd Razif
review_text: Mee rebus at Yang's Epok Epok is the best mee rebus i've tasted. Legit. Makes me miss my late grandma mee rebus

author: dAMbaan Creation
review_text:
Pros;
- love the range of foodies to choose from
- chahaya rossaz, one of the recommended food stalls. Claypot rice flavourful and tasty. Loved it
- condiments and duck egg provided

Cons;
- crowded
- lunch-time carpark hardly available

author: Normawati Selamat
review_text: Waited for more than 30 min for the satay. Satay meat - beef & mutton - were very tasty. The satay gravy was thick & yummy with crunchy peanuts. 👍🏼 However, satay was not well grilled as there parts burnt & others uncooked. 👎🏼 Hokkien Mee was good! 👍🏼 We dabao-ed Roti John & found it to be miserably thin. 👎🏼

author: Sufi Sazali
review_text: Yuzz tasty corner has the most friendliest owner , despite it being a simple dish [putu piring] , it was served hot & fresh and it was really good and in my opinion better than most sellers , they are also not stingy with the amount of gula melaka in the putu piring , will come here again and bring my family here . Support 01 Yuzz Tasty Corner , can’t miss it .❤️❤️

author: Stanley Fong
review_text:
Also known as Bedok Corner Food Centre, is located at No.1 Bedok Road. This food centre is a very good place to try all kind of popular Halal street food at a reasonable prices. Of course there are also some Chinese food like Carrot Cake, Boneless Chicken Rice, etc.
It’s just a 10 minutes bus ride from Tanah Merah MRT Station.

author: Culaya Zahry
review_text: So far, the food is tasty and worth the price, but the place is somewhat untidy and not very clean atmosphere.

author: William Lu
review_text: Interesting foods selection here. Wasn't too crowded when we visited. Over-bought our dinner here because they were interesting to see. Taste was ok as well.

author: J Leong
review_text: basically one best hawker centre, you must try the curry noodle here and the fry carrot cake here is also quite good. There are two stalls of fry carrot cakes, you can randomly choose one, both are awesome. Watermelon fruit bowl is available here, it's really cheap but special,the uncle of stall is very kind. you can really try the soup here , it's definitely amazing, especially in rainy day. what's more is the duck rice here, the duck rice stall close to the fruit bowl stall is better. It's cheaper but better, u must try their chilli source, it's very spicy but palatable

author: Calvin Huang
review_text: Newly made over and varieties of halal and local delectable. Price is reasonable for most dishes and many local favourites and famous must try!

author: Jones Ng
review_text: Arrived here too early at 7am on Sunday, only a few stalls open. Take a Malay stall’s Mee Rebus $4. Coffee $1.20. Taste good.

author: Peter & Thelma Low
review_text:
We had char kway teow, orluak, hot cheng tng, Ayam berempah nasi lemak, goreng pisang and goreng chempedak.
The orluak was very starchy and not crispy altho the oysters look succulent and fresh. The cheng tng came lukewarm, and the taste  was flat. The berempah chicken was dry altho the sambal was nice. The worst were the pisang goreng and chempedak. The batter was limpid, the oil was heavy and they were cold. I suspect these were left overs from yesterday. Only the char kway teow was reasonably good.

author: I. M. FIZAH
review_text: Went there for early lunch. Saw a stall that sells halal hokkien mee. Bought the $6 plate. It was damn good.. finish it in less than 10mins then ordered again another $6 plate. Hehehe..

author: Andrew Mowat
review_text: This bistro has it all. Don’t be misled by the somewhat unassuming looks from the entrance, this place has fabulous coastal vibes and friendly staff to match. Everyone who works here has a genuine interest in customers, including a positive food experience. Talking of which, every dish we had was very enjoyable, from the simple but well put together Aglio Olio to the Indian and fusion dishes we tried. And unlike a recent experience with a nearby and well-known Greek restaurant, the prices here are very reasonable. A lovely little gem on East Coast Park.

author: Jordan Liu
review_text:
1. Chicken Tikka Masala - Good, interesting flavour

2. Chicken Lollypop - Very interesting flavour -> Leans more towards sour then spicy with a nice lingering aftertaste

3. Jalapeno Cheddar Corn Fritter - Best dish amongst the order!!! Love it!

4. The Satay Club (3 chicken, 3 beef) - Chicken was super tender! Beef was chewy, grilled just nice! Sauce was great and compatible with the satay!

Will recommend to go and will want to go again just for the Jalapeno Cheddar Corn Fritters! Hidden at the end of East Coast Park!

author: Siew Ching Tan
review_text: Came here during the Oktoberfest and was blessed with such a good atmosphere!! There were discounted alcohol, nice music, and even games! The lady boss and daughter were such great hosts to the restaurant, that it made us felt so comfortable dining here! We love the place so much, and were so pleased to chance upon this rare restaurant! Really a good place to recommend for groups! The food were also flavourful and unique! Special mention to their fish tikka and corn fritters!!

author: Dave
review_text:
Visited High Tide Bistro and Bar on a Friday evening with a group of friends, and overall, it was a pleasant experience.

The food was solid — not extraordinary, but definitely above average. One standout for me was the satay. While I’ve had great satay at hawker centres, this one felt like an elevated version you’d expect at a proper restaurant — juicy, well-seasoned, and grilled just right. The only slight letdown was the limited beer selection, which could’ve been better given the setting.

The atmosphere was lovely. Although it wasn’t a wide, open sea view, we still enjoyed the breeze coming off the water and the calming seaside vibe. Visiting during sunset made the experience even more enjoyable — the golden hour light and cool breeze created a great backdrop for a relaxed dinner.

As for the service, it was fine — nothing particularly memorable, but not lacking either. Some responses from the staff felt a bit slow, which was noticeable at times, but didn’t majorly impact our evening.

One thing to note is the accessibility. We came by Grab, and the drop-off/pick-up area wasn’t very clearly marked, which might be confusing for first-timers. Not sure about parking options since we didn’t drive.

Overall, a nice spot to unwind with friends by the sea, especially if you’re looking for a chill evening with good vibes and a few standout dishes

author: Irwin Harith
review_text: Had an amazing time for dinner last night. First time at the High Tide Bistro and Bar. Was recommended the butter chicken pizza and it was delicious! We all had a beef quesadilla which was also yummy. Will definitely come back again :)

author: Bert Grobben
review_text:
Chill beach front place. Simple outfit, but that’s all you need for a drink and some food. Friendly and attentive staff. Kinda feels like eating at someone’s home.

The menus looks broad. Portion sizes are big, and the items we have very tasty! Will come back for an afternoon at East Coast

author: Elizabeth Wong
review_text: we had an enjoyable dinner at High Tide on 3 Nov, it was 2 of us + our furry gal. there were only 2 tables at 5.30pm, so the service and food were very prompt. the lady owner was very friendly, served a bowl of ice water to our gal without being asked, and chit chatted with us about her own dog and the restaurant background. we ordered 3 dishes, the cauli pop, tikka platter and palek paneer. they were all delicious, the tikka came on a sizzling platter and looked so mouth watering that the other table also looked over and exclaimed. the portions are pretty generous, we were stuffed and yet still packed some leftovers home. the pricing is not cheap, but also not overly pricy, and with the bigger portions and no GST charged is still quite good value. the bonus is the seaside view, with the seabreeze blowing over us and the sunset starting in the distance, a very relaxing and chill place. Will definitely be back again.

author: TK Chew
review_text: Owner's mom who helps to run the place was super nice and gave great recommendations on their dishes. Their Indian and Nepal cuisine are genuinely delicious. Great atmosphere to enjoy the sea and look at planes departing from Changi Airport.

author: Yan X.
review_text: Came here for lunch while some of us were windsurfing at Passion Wave. It is a great place to relax on weekends, and you can watch people sailing as you enjoy your meal. The food is delicious, with the meat especially well-marinated. The stuffs here also very friendly and accommodating. We will definitely come back again!

author: Usha Devi
review_text: Had an incredible dining experience! The food was absolutely amazing – every dish was packed with flavor and beautifully presented. The view added an extra charm to the meal, making it even more memorable. But what truly stood out was the service – attentive, warm, and beyond excellent. Not to forget they are pet-friendly too!! Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for great food with a view and top-notch hospitality! 🌟

author: Meditate Zen
review_text:
High Tide Resto & Bar
For a weekend outing, I decided to visit a bar by the sea to enjoy the breeze and catch up with my friend over some heart-to-heart talk. We chose this spot as our meeting point and ordered a variety of dishes: Margherita Pizza, Aglio Olio, 12 sticks of chicken satay, Lychee Melon, and a Singapore Sling.

The food was satisfying, but the highlight was definitely the satay—big, juicy, and perfectly paired with the sauce. The staff were friendly and attentive, adding to the positive experience. Time slipped by quickly as we chatted, enjoyed the view, and watched the evening sky turn dark without even realizing it.

I’d definitely recommend this place for a chill night out, whether with your bestie or a loved one.

My ratings:

Food Quality: ⭐ 4.5/5
Food Portion: ⭐ 3.5/5
Environment: ⭐ 5/5

author: MJW Editions
review_text: We ended our East Coast walk here after doing so a few months back and just grabbing a drink. This time we came for the food and we were not disappointed. Great quality, Indian & western fusion going on too. Started with a mezze platter, then a spread of dishes, Fish Tikka, Sriracha Cauliflower, Tandoori Stuffed Jalapeno, Chilli beef, Butter Chicken and Kathi Rolls. A real feast and all tasty, washed down with a couple of ice-cold beers and cider. We'll be back as this makes a wholesome stop after a wholesome walk!

author: Pang Yong Song
review_text:
We were looking for a chill place for Father's day dinner and a pet friendly one so that we could bring our fur kid along.

Glad to have found High Tide Bistro & Bar. Vibes were chill and the owners were very prompt & friendly in their service. We found out they were owners of a Goldie too.

Our pet was provided with a bowl of ice water and he had doggie biscuits too!

Coming to the food, owners gave their recommendations. And they were definitely up to mark. Kids enjoyed the starters of Jalapeno Corn Fritters and Calamari.  That was followed by the mezza platter. Humus with Pita and the Falefel was great.  We shared 2 mains of Kathi Roll and Butter Chicken with an extra side of naan.  Kids totally mopped up the butter chicken sauce with the Naan and the rice goes so well with the dish.

Chill vibes with good food. Will come back again.

author: Dipti Modi
review_text:
Ummm may one of the bad days but right from food to drinks everything went bad that day including waiting of 50 minutes for Food. I understand the wait time but yet every restaurant accounts for more people on weekend. Not my choice to repeat except for Ambience.

I ordered Paneer and hummus platter. hummus was good and Falafel

There is a jaljeera drink with vodka. Badly made with over chilli and not a drink I would recommend. I asked to replace, but they totally forgot. Overall quite sad as I was quite excited 😊 to visit this place

author: Habibu
review_text: Good vibes and delicious food. Staff were very friendly and efficient. There is quite a number of Indian dishes but there is also a good selection of other types of food. Decided to go more Western instead. Will definitely return in the future!

author: Su YH
review_text: The food were great. Nice atmosphere when you come in the evening. Ordered butter chicken, it was nice n not spicy, kids can eat. Kids friendly too as they have kids meal and pizza which the kids will like. For adult, we can indulge on the various Indian food. The lady boss was very hosting n friendly. Very rare in Spore to find good service standard, yet I found it here. Food price is reasonable with service charge but no GST.

author: Somya Patro
review_text: Amazing surfer chill vibes at this restaurant! The bartender Dinesh had greaat energy. It was my husband’s first time in Singapore and first time trying a Singapore sling, and 10000/10 best one I’ve ever had. I told Dinesh I wanted to experiment with different drinks and he kept em coming - each one better than the next. Chili chicken and garlic naan was such a good combo, can’t wait to come back and try all the other food they have! Definitely a must have in Singapore. 😍

author: Vishal Shirsat
review_text: This restaurant was a customer choice for a quiet dinner. Away from the hustle and bustle of Clarke Quay and more famous places and nearer to the airport, from where he had to catch a flight. Its a very nice place to have a good, quiet dinner and drink. The cool sea breeze flows into this place, and light music plays in the background. The place is accessible by taxi or nearby car parks on the ECP. The ambiance is very good with a combination of high chairs and normal seating. The food is amazing. We chose the Chicken Tikka platter and were full with that. It was tasty and filling. The staff is very polite and nice. Would go again here to have another quiet and calm evening with good drinks and dinner

author: Johnson Ong
review_text: Mains are all served hot to my wife's delight. The lamb chop we ordered is tender and flavourful and it tasted even better with the fantastic sauce. The wedge potatoes that came along with it is crispy on the outside and fluffy inside. The palak paneer is the most delicious that we have ever tasted. The naan is fresh and soft. Last but not least, the service is excellent, serving us a jar of cold or warm water each. We will definitely be back to try other dishes.

author: Angie Ling
review_text: Was searching for a pet friendly place and this pops up! Decided to give it a try since I'm staying nearby, so why not... Mainly they were selling Indian and western food. But of course, we had to try the Chicken Tikka Platter, well recommended Minced Lamb Pizza and a Quesadilla! Was surprised that the quality of the food really turned out to be good! Avoid the lamb pizza if you cannot accept the lamb taste. Ordered a little too much for 2 person but it was superb worth it!

author: Derrick L
review_text: Huge variety of hawker food to choose from. From fried noodles to satay to zi char, a great place to chill and enjoy the sea breeze. There’s also semi alfresco seating where you can have a beer and enjoy free music from beer uncles.

author: Bugwagen
review_text: Lots of good food here.  👍🏻 We like the satay, hokkien mee, carrot cake.  Very popular hawker so parking can be a challenge.  Also when it rains, it is not fully sheltered

author: Qiuyi
review_text: We really enjoyed the food. We ordered grilled chicken wings, fried Hokkien prawn mee, and some Thai dishes, including papaya salad. The taste was nice and not too spicy — maybe you can ask them to adjust the spiciness level if you prefer. The most popular drink there is sugarcane juice. You can also enjoy satay, as many stalls sell it. That night, there weren’t too many people, maybe because it was a weekday.

author: TAL TAL
review_text:
I love this place for its variety of local food. My favourite 3 stalls are:
1. High Kee BBQ seafood
2. Leng Heng chicken rice
3. 60 BBQ Satay
These 3 stalls have been serving great food for many years. The owners of High Kee BBQ Seafood started off in the 1990s selling chicken rice. Reasonbly priced, great service.
Leng Heng chicken rice is one of the best in Singapore.  The chilli is superb.
The guys at 60 BBQ Satay are friendly. Satay is well cooked and gravy is shiok. All three stall owners have now become my friends.
There are others you must try too like BBQ chicken wings, soto ayam and fried oyster. Parking is a plenty. The place is well patronised during weekends.

author: Ma Ro
review_text: It's so good here. The FOOD is so amazing. I haven't had the time to take photos of other food we ordered😅 we order prawns, veggies, and satay. THE downside is not so accessible for tourist since the MRT and Bus is too far. You may get grab or have a local drive you here 🤗

author: KK
review_text:
As a Singaporean, I would definitely come here for the oyster omelette — it’s fresher than most places, with more oysters and plenty of egg, at $7/plate
How to get there: take the train to Siglap Station and exit via Exit 1 (cross the road opposite the station exit) > Walk straight and you’ll see an underground passage > Go down the stairs > walk through > and come up the other side > Continue walking straight and in about 8 minutes > you’ll see the park and lagoon on your left, with Lagoon Hawker just beside it. Eat while enjoying the sea breeze.
Remember to return the tray after food and no smoking is allowed at the park, hawker and beach.

author: JuthaMars C
review_text:
The location is really good to enjoy dinner. It is in the park but quite far from downtown.
The food is fresh and reasonable price. There are many restaurants and many types of food, such as seafood (chili crab), satay, Chinese, indian, porridges and etc.

author: Daniel Aiden Leo
review_text: specially come here for the satay,saw some reviews that the satay there is good and indeed is good, for 10 stick satay cost $9. I ask for 5 chicken, 5 mutton and a rice, in total cost me $10.Satay sauce  was very nutty and a bit on the sweet side, also ordered lemon sugar cane $3 and finally be for i leave for home, I took this bread ice-cream cost me $2 where you hardly find these days.

author: Sam Goh SE
review_text: delicious traditional food like fried kueh teow, fried carrot cake, fried oysters, fried Hokkein mee, bbq chicken wing, bbq sting ray, satay and popiah. All super good. we enjoyed our picnic lunch. bought takeaways to have picnic by the beach. so fun eating near the beach and splashing waves.

author: N8s Obregon
review_text:
It's one of the more popular hawker centers in Singapore. We had our meetup with friends here for an early dinner. They knew what to order and the food was great. Lots of choices of local delicacies and grilled food with generous serving sizes. They have a big open-air dining area, but as peak dining hours drew near, the place was full and there were already people waiting for available tables.
East Coast Lagoon Food Village is located by the beach and so after dinner, we strolled along the shore as we continued catching up with our friends.

author: Zokrath Tan
review_text:
This place has a wide and good selection of local foods if you want to be spoilt for choice. By local foods, I mean the Singaporean foods that singaporeans love to eat.

There may be multiple stalls selling the same kind of dishes, but they all have their own taste and regular customers.

Definitely go try the different stalls for satay, carrot cake, bbq chicken wings, and hokkien mee.

author: L A
review_text: The food is fairly priced. Usual place for a lot of beach goers. Good Food. Good Price

author: Michael Goh
review_text:
Crowded during week end and after office hour.
Full of human noises.
Be prepared for for cooking smell on clothes and hair.
Full of exotic local food (eg seafoods).
Overall, fun place.

author: Christian Jones Lucas
review_text: This place was very crowded and hot. The seating is outdoor fans but not all of the fans were on. Be prepared for workers from each hawker stall to approach you as you walk around to offer you the menu. Even if you aren't even close to their stall.

author: Inzaikun Chiba
review_text:
Great place to enjoy local beer 🍺 🐅 on the rocks 🧊 😳 and satays while sun setting on the beach 🏝️
You can walk from Siglap MRT station 🚉 per map attached

author: mag Chong
review_text: The food is excellent in many stalls we visited a good place after cycling

author: Sakura Stan
review_text: East Coast Lagoon Food Village in Singapore is a beloved hawker centre renowned for its wide variety of local seafood and grilled delights. Set by the beach, it offers a unique open-air dining experience with a laid-back coastal vibe. Popular dishes include barbecued stingray, satay, sambal squid, and Hokkien mee, all prepared with bold, authentic flavours. The smoky aroma from the charcoal grills fills the air, drawing in locals and tourists alike. Diners often enjoy their meals under the stars, accompanied by a sea breeze. It’s a perfect spot for affordable, delicious Singaporean food in a scenic, relaxing setting.

author: クリスタルキール
review_text: Very good food and beautiful view. We went gathering for dinner at East Coast Lagoon food Village.

author: Adrian Yong
review_text: Food Court offering a large variety of Singaporean local favourites. All self service. Parking can be a challenge in the evening.

author: Ikhwan Isnawan
review_text: My family and my relatives bring us to war called East Coast Lagoon Food Village during NDP Eve for early dinner. Food was nice better than Lau Pat Sat. Those friendly staff are here.

author: Christian Madonna
review_text:
The place was absolutely charming and inviting — clean, cozy, and beautifully decorated. I especially loved the huge flower display; it added such a lovely touch to the atmosphere.

The food was excellent — well presented and delicious. I had the smoked salmon and eggs, which were perfectly cooked and beautifully plated. Service was efficient, and I didn’t have to wait long for my meal.

The coffee was spot-on, and the Prosecco was perfectly chilled — a great combination for a relaxing brunch.

The service really stood out. The staff were warm, friendly, and attentive, happily accommodating my request to change seats. Every meal was served with a smile, and the team made a genuine effort to engage with us each time they passed by.

A special shout-out to Nicolas, who went above and beyond to check on us throughout our visit — his hospitality made the experience even more enjoyable.

Overall, a delightful spot with great food, lovely ambiance, and outstanding service. Highly recommended!

author: EugeneFCS
review_text:
PS.Cafe at East Coast delivers a calm, polished dining experience that feels like a quiet escape from the city. The space is airy and relaxed, with tasteful interiors that blend well with the laid-back coastal atmosphere.

Food quality is consistently good. Portions are generous, flavors are well-balanced, and presentation is thoughtful without being overdone. Whether it is brunch, coffee, or a full meal, everything feels carefully prepared rather than rushed.

Service is attentive and professional without being intrusive. Staff are familiar with the menu and handle requests smoothly, which adds to the overall ease of the experience.

It is a good place for a slow meal, a long conversation, or simply to unwind after a walk along East Coast Park. Comfortable, reliable, and well-executed.

author: Mikki B
review_text: Ps Café at East Coast Park has a very pleasant environment, surrounded by greenery and close to the sea, making it a relaxing spot to unwind. Parking is plentiful, which makes visiting convenient. However, the food was just so-so and didn’t particularly stand out. One downside is that there is no toilet within the restaurant itself, which can be inconvenient. Overall, it’s more about the setting than the food experience. Great place to catch up with friends.

author: Rick Kok
review_text: It was a great weather to sit outdoor at PS cafe East Coast. Coffee and breakfast was good. Not to mention, the service was excellent, especially with Nicholas and YY. They took great care to serve us from drinks to food, making sure my wife and I are comfortable. Nicholas even shared about PS cafe history. Both of us will surely come back to visit the staff and cafe again ❤️ The experience is wonderful. Well done 👏🏻

author: johnnykuochung
review_text:
🍔 PS Burger at East Coast Park 🏖️
One of my top 5 burgers in Singapore, hands down! 🤤 The PS Burger is a bit of a splurge, but totally worth it. The beef patty is juicy and cooked to perfection (I go for medium 😋), and the fries? Piled high, golden, and crispy can’t get enough of them! 🍟
I love pairing it with their lychee & lime drink sweet, tangy, and refreshing. The perfect balance to the richness of the burger. 🍹
Why I love it: After a long day, I cycle to PS Café by the beach to unwind. The vibe, the ocean breeze, and the great food make it my go-to spot for a little indulgence. 🏖️✨
It’s a bit on the pricier side, but trust me, the whole experience is worth it. 🥰

author: Sin Han Lee
review_text: We went to PS.Cafe East Coast Park for a birthday celebration and had a wonderful experience. Eileen, Maggie, Bernie and Kent were all very thoughtful and attentive throughout our meal. The food was excellent, and the ambience was perfect for the occasion. We truly enjoyed our time there and will definitely return again.

author: Leon Yip
review_text: We had a truly delightful dining experience at your establishment. The food was exceptionally well-prepared and delicious. Furthermore, the staff members were remarkably friendly and attentive throughout our visit. We especially appreciated the thoughtful touch of providing a candle for our cake. Thank you for making our celebration so special.

author: Fernshares
review_text: The servers are welcoming and friendly, asked for feedback if food is nice at random tables. The portion of BBQ ribs is quite generous, and ribs is cooked just nice. Like that they also provide generous amount of sauce. The walnut salad is refreshing and crunchy. The kid love the cheese pull of the Cheeseburger and fries from kid's menu. Seared Barramundi is good as well. Red velvet cake is soft and not too rich. Would love to come back again.

author: avni sinsinwar
review_text:
Really nice café! Loved the cocktails. I had Aperol Spritz, and it was perfect. The food was amazing, and I liked that the menu had the option to turn non-veg dishes into veg one, such a thoughtful idea.
Joy and Maggie were super pleasant and friendly, they really made the experience enjoyable. Would definitely come back again!

author: Jack
review_text: Very nice pet friendly restaurant at East Coast. Really well ventilated and doesn't feel warm at all. We walked 4km with our furry friend and the service manager quickly offered ice water once we were seated. Food is good and yummy but the service is what really stood out. Thumbs up to super friendly and attentive Eileen who even offered tips for our dog who needs to shed few pounds. Will certainly be back soon.

author: Grace Chew
review_text:
Great food, vibe and staff! We had the Margherita Pizza, Buffalo Chicken Bites, Shakshouka, Sticky Date Pudding and Carrot Cake! For drinks we had Sangrias (Red and White)

We enjoyed everything and the staff were so warm and friendly, especially Eileen who kept coming to check in on us ❤️

author: Fy Jasni
review_text:
Had such an awesome experience at P.S. Café! The service was warm, attentive, and made us feel so welcomed.

A big thank you to Manager Bernie for welcoming us with such a warm smile and making us feel right at home. The team’s hospitality truly made our visit extra special. 🙌✨

Special mention to Eileen, the trainee, who impressed us with her professionalism, friendliness, and genuine effort to ensure we had a great time. For someone in training, she really went above and beyond . 💯👏

Can’t wait to be back again. 😊😍

author: Chong Huong Wong
review_text: The experience is wonderful. I didn’t like a dish we ordered, we were given a new choice. The restaurant didn’t charge us for the dish we disliked. It was a pleasant surprise.  The gentleman serving us is very polite and understanding.

author: Steph Tang
review_text: Celebrated my 4th anniversary here, brought our dog along and was given a very good corner seat which was very helpful as we do not want our dog to disrupt service. Service staff - mainly a short hair lady, uncle at outdoor area and outlet manager all were very friendly and attentive. In fact, the best service in all the PS Cafes that I have been to and I have been to at least 5.

author: WT
review_text:
Very comfy ambience. We came here for breakfast and had their crab eggs royale, pancake stack and P.S Full Breakfast.

Service by Eileen is amazing. So thoughtful of her to give the kids colouring materials to keep them entertained while the adults do their ordering. She also offered to make the scrambled eggs well done to have it look like omelette when the kids wanted omelette instead of scrambled eggs. Upon knowing the cup of Alright Orange is being shared by 2 kids, she also have it split into 2. Seeing one of the kid upset, she brought 2 cups of babycino (milk foam with cocoa powder) to cheer them up. Kudos to her!

Overall, we had an enjoyable experience!

author: Jane Gammad
review_text: I had a wonderful dining experience at PS. Cafe East Coast Brunch (Dinner with Fam) The service was excellent, staff were attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was perfect throughout our meal 🙂 The food was not only beautifully presented but also full of flavor, with every dish tasting fresh and well-prepared. Truly a great place to enjoy good food and warm hospitality. Highly recommended and big shoutout to Ms. Bernie 👏 Filipino hospitality always goes above and beyond, we surely back again!

author: yan H
review_text:
This cosy café sits quietly next to the beach giving a peaceful and relaxing feel. The bright and airy space inside makes it a nice spot to enjoy a slow meal.

A slice of chocolate cake and a hearty sandwich on the table add the perfect finishing touch to a peaceful afternoon.

author: joanna tan
review_text: Awesome experience and awesome food. Can always trust PS cafe to serve up comforting fare. Many thanks to Eileen and the team for making our dinner an enjoyable experience! Her enthusiasm and passion is unrivaled!

author: J C
review_text:
This is the gem of East Coast Park, forget about the usual fast food and crowded places along the east coast park.

This place is so cozy and relax, the atmosphere and music they played will make you like to come back again. The foods were fantastic, most importantly the service was excellent. Kudos to Hannah, she was so attentive and friendly.

Will come back again!

author: Yeoh Yuxian
review_text: Had dinner at PS Café East Coast Park; ordered the PS Burger and Crispy Chicken. Loved the setting by the sea and the relaxed vibe. The burger was juicy, the chicken had a nice crunch. Big shoutout to Eileen and Joel ! They were attentive, friendly, and made the meal even better.

author: L Chan
review_text:
A convenient hawker centre right next to Bedok MRT, bus interchange, Bedok Mall & surrounding HDB shops

Wide variety of local favourites at reasonable prices, with popular stalls often drawing queues

author: Sam Goh SE
review_text: Have a host of many interesting and hugely popular local delights such chwee Kueh, fried carrot cakes soon Kueh, wanting noodles, Chinese dumplings, Cantonese roast meats, Hi char, Indian muslim prata, Chinese dessert, coffee stalls. Always something for everyone.

author: Bảo Hân Hồ
review_text:
Shop 1-21
My first meal in Singapore after a while
I order 1 pork leg and 1 rice: the pork so tender and well marinated, sauce is little bit thick and perfectly pair with rice
highly reccomend this shop

author: S.Y
review_text:
𝐑𝐨𝐣𝐚𝐤 so shiok! I love it when they give a lot of sauce that is also not watery and it is thick, the taste of the prawn paste, sugar, chili whatever they added in so yummy! Their You Tiao also not soggy and crispy. Inside got red apple, green apple. pineapple, radish, cucumber, taupok.

𝐏𝐨𝐩𝐢𝐚𝐡 is also not bad, spicy enough to make me wish I had gotten 2 roll instead.

Also had 𝐅𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐎𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐎𝐦𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐞 - taste is not bad but find it too starchy, should have ordered the one with egg instead and if it's crispy more good also loh.

𝐌𝐢𝐱𝐞𝐝 𝐑𝐢𝐜𝐞 with Broccoli, Cabbage, Fried Egg & Fried Prawn - If you don't know what to get just go picked whatever you want.

Ended our meal with a dessert of 𝐂𝐡𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐨𝐥 however it didn't taste very good and it came in a takeaway container which I find it hard to dig the ingredients that are at the bottom.

✨Rojak $5
✨Popiah $2.50
✨Katong Fried Oyster Omelette $5
✨Mixed Rice $6
✨Chendol $2.80

author: Moonlight
review_text:
Review of Katong Fried Oyster stall.
Taste good but don’t order 蚝煎. Too much flour and only 5 whole oysters for $6 portion. the 蚝蛋 might be more worth it.

update: weeks later, i went back and bought the egg version also $6 - take out. a lot more oysters but overall i prefer the flour version ONLY because i could further fry it up at home until its super crispy and the flavour with each crunch is so much more satisfying.

author: Chris Chee
review_text: Many good choices.. Weekends expect crowd.. Weekdays moderate crowd.. The pork trotter stall, sell out by, the evening.. This one can target..

author: mega
review_text:
There are a lot of food stalls here!
I tried the popiah, pie tee, and mixed carrot cake. The carrot cake was really good (mix black and white), definitely recommend it! 🥕✨
Popiah and pie tee weren’t really my fave, and they didn’t taste that fresh to me.

The place was honestly pretty hot, a bit noisy, and kinda dim (could use better lighting). Hopefully, they improve that in the future!

author: Din Neo
review_text: One of the best local coffee shop where you can find many authentic food. Highly recommended!!

author: Cass
review_text:
The curry noodles are really yummy! They’re Michelin listed… idk if they’re thatttt good, but they’re good.
There’s lots of options (prawn noodles, fish balls, ban mian, economic rice) and at 7pm on a Thursday, lots of space to sit.
The soy milk is good but apparently famous? And I don’t think it deserves fame but it’s good.

author: Joyful Explorer
review_text: Conveniently located beside Bedok Mrt Station. Big hawker centre with many food options. Some stalls have extremely long queues during lunch crowd. Love the dishes we had.

author: Franco Abrina
review_text:
Conveniently located near Bedok MRT station.

It has plenty of affordable food options, and finding a table wasnt difficult at all. Bought some egg fried rice and a huge bowl of chendol, partner had some delicious roasted pork 👍

author: Joanne PeaceMind
review_text: Giving 3 stars because no aircon quite hot to eat. Overall price is the cheapest of all.  Just located beside Bedok Mall so it is very convenient location.  Can use PayLah n PayNow. CDC vouchers too. Sheltered from Bedok mall to here. Nice. Please keep food this affordable, thank you.

author: Kaye Aboltivo-Yason
review_text: There's a lot of food and drink choices that are affordable! Located just a few steps from Bedok Mall and bus station. This Curry chicken bee hoon was so good. There was a short queue to get your order, but it's worth it. I paired it with iced milo to ease the spiciness

author: Ezzy Chan
review_text:
Great food, good ambience.

The tze char stall, sambal Kang Kong , steam fish, sweet and sour pork and rice x 04 cost 52 SGD

The oyster egg costs 8 SGD

The prawns and sotong cost 12 and 15 SGD respectively.

Even with the drinks, still less than 100 SGD for a family of 4. Awesome. 🙃

author: Lee Eric
review_text: Very disappointing with the maintenance of food market; the big fan has not been in service for more than half a year, and the recent closure for blending the good market during Christmas period also did not repair or put the fan as n in service!  What is the main purpose for closure gif service and was the big ceiling fan was included for the maintenances?  Food for thought 🐷🐷🐷

author: zzubsg
review_text: WARNING DO NOT BUY FROM THIS MIX RICE STALL BEING CHARGE $9.50 for this sad looking rice , they mention $7 for the braised intestine. TOTALLY A SCAM FOR SUCH STALL. Taste really average. GO AT YOUR RISK 😡😡🤬😡

author: Gabriel Ng
review_text:
Pretty sure this hawker centre has the most stores that sell affordable meal in the price starting from $3.50. The price and taste of the food are 5 stars but the atmosphere is 3 star because it can be a bit dark if u are dining at the inside of the hawker centre.

One advice I give is to avoid stores that always have no queue during lunch and dinner hours. There is a reason why they have no queue think about. I would not name stores but u will notice it yourself

author: Jackovan
review_text:
Food: The food expecially the Inspirasi or whatever stall it's called absolutely terrible. Taste felt off and what made my whole day went terrible wasn't the terrible and off taste. I found a PLASTIC in my food! That wasn't the worse part. Went for a drink at Kopi Meow and holy the people were so dirty I can't even describe. I don't want to even review any further as it's making me more frustrated.
Service: The service was okay, nothing special except a sense of unfriendlyness.
Atmosphere: I came here on a weekend and alot of the tables are dirty and crowded. It gives the local hawker vibes though!

Never go here. Never.

author: Stephant S (stephant_s)
review_text:
These is a huge hawker centre with Many delicious and famous food here! These hawkers have been running their stalls here for years!

This is one of the best place that you can get almost all the best tastes of Singapore food at the affordable price!

Look for those with long queues and let the patrons guide you to find the best!

My Recommendation:
Bedok Chwee Kueh
Nasi Lemak
Tiong Bahru Pau
Mee Goreng
Nasi Briyani Mutton
Mee Rebus
Stewed soup
Vegetarian
Satay Bee Hoon
Steamed Chicken Rice
Fish Soup Porridge
Fried Carrot Cake
Prawn Noodle
Fried Hokkien Mee
Desserts
Herbal Mutton Soup
Mala Hotpot
Spinach Soup
Satay
Sugarcane
Kway Chap
Fishball Noodle
Beancurd Desserts

Food variety ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Wallet friendly ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Cleanliness ⭐️⭐️⭐️

Few things to improve for this place that I can see are the hygiene issue and the birds…

author: Skye
review_text:
Had from 1 western food stall chicken chop at $7 and 1 fried hokkien prawn noodles at $5 by myself.  Gravy of the chicken chop so diluted and tasteless and small in size but the chicken quite tender. Comes with some unsalted fries that I didn't like it and a slice of japanese cucumber that I like.

The fried hokkien prawn noodles pretty wet and taste like corn flour. Not impressed at all. Won't order from these 2 stalls again.

I remember many years back bedok interchange that hawker center have nice food but totally disappointed. If happened to be at bedok interchange this hawker center, will try other stalls food.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Paul Ciprian
review_text: One of the oldest markets in Singapore. Now, very nicely renovated. It has two sections: one is the agri-food market, the other is a hawker center where you can eat cheaply and well.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Honglian Lee
review_text: Great place to be at to enjoy the vibe and energy of people going about their morning rounds to buy groceries, breakfast and so on. The food centre on the upper floor  is a glutton's heaven with unique food offerings such as Kacang Pool, Mee Siglap, Mee Johor and goodness whatever you wouldn't hear of normally in other parts of Sg. Come early from 8am to be able to find parking at the food centre and take your time to explore this gastronomical carnival!

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Mr Low (미카님)
review_text:
This place is where your nose, stomach and soul all say thank you.

Full of amazing Malay and Indian food like nasi lemak, curry puffs and all things goreng, it's a food coma waiting to happen.

Prices are friendly, portions are no joke and the vibes are old school chill.

Come hungry, leave rolling around (Because of food coma)

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Asyifa Rizki Aprilia Harahap
review_text: We came here for breakfast and we were surprised of how clean this place is. I heard they were recently renovated. They offer a lot of different cuisine also. The food area is available on the first storey & second storey.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: C L
review_text:
Plenty of Chinese market stallholders.
Cheaper seafood compared to mainstream markets.
You can get a fresh salmon head for $2 but from a hostile fishmonger.
Long queue at taxi stand even on weekdays.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: IUVA sg
review_text: Has been a favourite shopping site for the Malays and other races for fresh produces and on the 2nd floor, wide range of Malay Culinaries. All food are Halal. Prices are affordable. Try the Nasi Briyani or the Nasi Padang. There are many desserts too. All under 1 roof. It is accessible by bus or MRT.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Mohammed Isa Sidek
review_text: Ayam Penyet was really delicious and tasty  after i ordered the food I ask the staff to bring the food to the table where I was sitting and she bring the food to the table after that I paid for the $6.50

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Rai Syazwani
review_text: Big and clean market selling not only fresh produce but also clothes etc. The food court offers variety of halal food with cheap prices. There are two food courts one at the ground level, another upstairs. The appom and mee siam we had (upstairs) were so delicious. Must come in the morning, a lot of stalls upstairs start closing early afternoon. The ground level food court opens till evening.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Rupert Holm
review_text: Quite clean and tidy place. Alot of food options as well. Grateful to see Malay friends again. Definitely a good stomach refuelling place for tourists.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: M Astro
review_text: Mid size hawker center on the 2nd floor. 99% Muslim food. Food is great and the hawker center is airy and clean. Gets gery crowded on the weekends and at breakfast/lunch times.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Jorden Tan
review_text: Local wet market where you can find fresh fish and meat. Do note, it’s a Muslim market, so you won’t find pork related items there.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: genalyn Gocon
review_text:
Can be less crowded if you come early on weekends all the seafoods are cheaper compared to our neighborhood market but if you buy a fish they won't clean for you
The food court upstairs 2nd level are awesome specially the kambing soup and the mee rebus

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Cheong Loong
review_text: For malay food lovers,  this is the place where one can find the halal ingredients to prepare that muslim meal you have in mind. If lazy just adjorn upstairs to the food court where most of halal muslim stalls have the dish you want to eat. Only thing is which stall is good. It is just a preference of taste but will not go wrong if one sees a long queue infront of the stall. For the adventurous new to muslim food ,  just try . The rich spicy coconut cooked food will give you that kick and leave a good impression in one's mouth.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Azfar Maswan
review_text:
best place in the world! the variety of southeast asian ingredients here is amazing. and the meats from the butchers are the cheapest on the island.

Siti Flower Power has a complete Jamu (Nusantara traditional medicine) store where you can get ingredients to cure different ailments. best place for fresh coconut milk is Mr Khaled's shop.

after buying your groceries, head up to the hawker and enjoy classic Singaporean fares such as Laksa Siglap, Kacang Phool or even freshly made chapati. everything here is heaven!

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Hamzah Alsagoff
review_text:
Each year during Ramadan I make it a tradition to first bring the family and then my non-Muslim extended family of kakis to the festive bazaars. Bazaar...for Ramadan. Not a repurposed pasar malam. Where I grew up anticipating and looking forward to festive traditional offerings — especially soulfood that will break my resistance or restrain....for health reasons.....that I'll be damned over — and not the proliferation of supposedly creative fusion which often are the hipster young fascination with Western cuisines which they sadly not only butcher at times but rehash for localised taste. At times using cheaper pseudo ingredients and slathering with overly hot toppings to mask the mediocre passable copies. Anyway I hardly fancy those. What I want to lament is the glaring absence — if any it is scattered and few — of traditional Ramadan or Raya soulfood favourites that I don't see many talk or raise about. It can't just be me.

If I am blunt I'll say what used to be a great festive family affair at a beautiful bazaar, where we visit to soak in the vibe and sample the offerings, has been robbed and hijacked by 'vendors' who can afford the high rent who in turn sell high and expensive. Terrible. Where we no longer or hardly see committed makciks or pakciks lovingly peddle what they offer just for Ramadan and for some to do so to  sadaqah. What a sad state. The worst is this year's supposedly largest — not .....with plenty of empty spaces obviously untaken — Geylang Ramadan Bazaar. It is a pathetic disguised tourist-bait glorified pasar malam.

If you want classic traditional food that won't cost an arm and leg then for Geylang area head over to the food centre above the market. No hipster gimmick in sight. Just good ole familiar mouth-baiting classic Malay or nusantara food. And festive drinks that are traditional and not charged at inflated cafe prices.

One wonders if the ones who planned all these factor in consideration for heart and soul. For respect and love for our culture. Yes, I'm naive and hopeful. Profit is sadly evident in play.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Briam isari
review_text: Geylang Serai is one of Singapore’s key Malay cultural districts. Once an area filled with lemongrass (“serai”) plantations, it later became a hub for the Malay and Nusantara communities. Today, it’s known for the lively Geylang Serai Market, Wisma Geylang Serai community centre, and the vibrant annual Ramadan bazaar. The area remains an important symbol of Malay heritage and culture in Singapore.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Hoong Wai Wong
review_text:
Crowded but can get a seat eventually.

Friendly stall owners, plenty of great food choices here!

Mutton Briyani, Nasi Ayam, various nasi or mee gorengs, kambing (mutton) soup, mee rebus with satay, nasi padang, Bubur porridge. Every time come here lost for choice what to eat sia!

The Ching Teng dessert soup also nice and cooling contrast for the spicy dishes.

Recommended!

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Jeanne Herawati
review_text: Complete traditional market (for me), can find a lot variant of chilies, green tomato, which is not there in wet market near my house. So happy! And lot of halal food also in level 2.

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Yeoh Yuxian
review_text:
This is a must come for foodies! There’s the famous Geylang Briyani Stall, Iqbal Soup Kambing, the old school Hainan Kaya Toast (where you can get your kopi in a tin), and Oli Thosai!

Place is super packed and the queue is long too. But super worth it!

restaurant: Geylang Serai Market and Food Centre
author: Rajen Arasu
review_text: Iconic market in the East... has 2 levels comprising the market and sundry stalls on the Ground level  offering a myriad  of grocery and  market items,  and Hawker dining and retail stalls offering apparel and household items on the Second level. Very crowded especially on weekends. Time for a major renovation to the market area and hawker dining area as it's very congested. A few hawker stalls on the 2nd level are "Legacy Hawkers" having existed in the old Geylang Serai Market 50 years ago or more.

author: L.G. Wee
review_text:
Jan2026. This was probably one of the best bak chor mee i had for a long time.
In my opinion, it was even better than Taihwa bak chor mee.
I ordered a dry version, the minced pork and dumplings were served in a separate soup bowl from the noodle.
The soup absorbed the pork fragrance and the minced meat was fluffily easy on chewing. Even the dumplings had a unique taste which i liked.
The only thing to complain was it was oily albeit already ordered with no lard oil.

author: Clara Poh
review_text: Love the soupy mee pok version of this Famous Eunos Bak Chor Mee ($4.80). The minced pork and crispy pork lard pieces compliments the al dente Meepok very well and makes the broth very delicious. Three very good size huge chewy pork dumplings makes this simple meal a fulfilling one. Be prepared for the queue can be a 10-15 minutes wait depending on the time of the day Ordered a bowl of fishball soup to try ($5).
