The fish ball is big and bouncy but the soup is bland when compared to the minced pork soup. Definitely a must try for Bak Chor Mee lovers. Highly Recommended.

author: Carmen L
review_text:
This is my third time trying the BCM here and it never fails to disappoint. For $4.80, you get a pretty decent bowl. The soup is not too salty for my liking but still very flavourfully meaty in its own right. I feel another difference between this and other BCMs would be the minced meat; Famous Eunos is quite generous in this aspect but do expect the texture to be much softer than that of other stalls. Overall, the taste is very balanced and should be likeable by many.

My recommendation - get the soup version, not the dry one. This is even coming from me who prefers the dry version in our hot country; for some reason, the soup version slaps more. You can also top up for other ingredients such as solefish for $1.20.

author: SF Goh
review_text: So far is my favourite Bak Chor Mee noodle in this area. They're so comforting, and have an amazing flavor, slightly high salt level and springy noodles.Ever since I come to this area will think of this stall of lots of Pork Lark of noodle. The chilli in vinegar is a must to pair with the noodles if you can take spice. However dumplings so so, sometimes can be long queue, try to come off peak hour if you can

author: Jasper Teo
review_text: First time trying this outlet and I can see why the reviews are high. Ordered their main item, the soup BCM and was pleasantly impressed by the flavour. Slightly herby taste in the soup, with lots of bak chor and also fried pork skin. The wantons are pretty big too! And there were at least 3 in every bowl. The size of their wantons puts some wanton noodle stalls to shame. Would come back for more visits.

author: Jason Tan
review_text: We came here for breakfast. The queue is not too long, we order mee Kia soup. The soup is delicious and the noodle is not too soft type. The wanton is also good. After we order the queue became very long but move off quite quickly. My personal favorite is still the closed down bak chor mee stall at blk 58 new upper changi road hawker centre.

author: Ann Meow
review_text:
Super satisfying bowl of soupy BCM! Quite oily soup cos of the pork lards and minced pork that has fatty cuts. However i couldnt stop drinking the salty soup. It was addictive! Few moments later - i was so thirsty and kept drinking and drinking non stop. Watch out for the sodium.

My meekia was still quite raw, a bit al dente at the start. It started to soften the more i ate. Can consider asking them to cook the noodles longer if you mind hard noodles.

Would definitely be back!

author: Food lover
review_text:
The noodles is pretty good not too soggy, but I do find the price high in terms of ingredients.
A bowl almost $5 comes with 3 wantan and some minced pork and noodles.

I ordered the dry noodles but cook gave me soup noodles. Didn't want to disrupt the queue behind so accepted sadly...

A bowl of fish ball soup for $5 only came with 9 fish balls..

author: Jim Khoo
review_text:
🌟 Foodie Adventure 🌟
Tried Famous Eunos Bak Chor Mee after many years—nostalgia hit, but with so many stores now, that retro charm feels a bit lost. The noodles were decent, though the minced pork dumpling soup was a tad too salty for my taste (lesser salt would be perfect!). It’s a solid quick fix, so I’ll be back, but it’s not a monthly must for me. 🍜💧 #Foodie #BakChorMee #Eunos #SingaporeEats #NoodleLovers

author: Min Loo
review_text: Heard that they were good and thought was the same style as the bedok minced pork soup BCM. Nothing like it. Was pretty amateurish with room for improvement. My noodle was not cooked properly with some still tangled like a knot. Soup was bland.

author: Joshua Wong
review_text:
Nested in a local coffee shop, this stall sells minced pork noodle at an affordable price. Be prepared for queues at peak hours especially during the lunch crowds.

While the taste may not be comparable to a popular Michelin Bib Gourmand stall that sells similar food, this stall has its own unique taste that keeps me coming back for more.

If you are not a fan of lard, you can request for it to be excluded, else the crispy lard brings the flavour to another level. The dumpling that comes with it is big, but the skin is a little thick to my preference.

author: Kenny Yap
review_text:
Somewhat unnecessarily oily but it’s definitely a very delicious bowl. I added $1.20 for extra minced pork so total $6.

No queue at around 930 on a weekday morning.

author: Sing Lim
review_text: I used to come to this hawker when it was in the other location until I found it again recently. So, I decided to come and try it out.  I came early as it was reported that the queue can be very long. I was here at around 11 a.m., and there's already about 6 people in front of me. But the queue moved fast so I didn't have to wait for too long. I ordered the mee pok dry and a bowl of fish balls soup. The noodles come with a bowl of dumpling soup and minced pork. The noodles were cooked very well, and it went well with the soup. The fish balls were fresh and bouncy. Overall, I would have to say that i enjoyed it very much and I would probably come back again. But it is still not at the top of my favorite BCM.

author: Charlotte Teo
review_text: Had the soup version of the Bah Chor Mee. From food quality to service, all was great. The fried beancurd skin are crispy and comes with sauce at the bottom. I like the soup and bah chor because ingredients are fresh no stench at all. Great meal for rainy morning.

author: pk a
review_text: I ordered the number one minced meat with bee hoon soup. For those who like minced meat and meat dumplings this is good. However I prefer the teochew style with liver, dried mushroom and sliced pork, so I was rather disappointed. The soup tasted a tad too sweet for my liking. I also ordered the $5 fish ball soup and it came generously with 9 fishballs, it was not bad, but not the best I have tasted.

author: Stephen Ng
review_text:
$4.80 for the bak Chor mee. Taste was good. Very generous on the minced meat. The meat was made into a wanton which is quite special. No smell on the meat. 👍
Parking is small. Expect long wait time for parking during meal hours.

author: Garry Lew Your Estate Advisory Realtor
review_text:
Visited 4th July 2025 Friday morning. The following sharing are based on our unbiased and personal experience.

Wife wanted to give this stall a try and order herself a bowl of Bak Chor mee. Not much queue during this timing so she had her noodle pretty fast compared to the carrot cake stall

First bite the noodle wasn’t what I had expected. It’s a bit undercooked but the broth was pretty okay. Ingredients was also generous I would say but didn’t quite catch my taste bud.

A lot of missed rather than hit. A 3 ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ for this noodle

Follow us for a gastronomic experience and discover the world’s finest in its purest form.

author: Flo Yeow
review_text:
This bak chor mee soup stall shares its roots with the famous stalls at Bedok 85 and 58, tracing back to the same hawker in the 1920s.

While I found it to be a decent bowl of noodles, other stalls offer a more flavorful experience, though taste is subjective. This version is less crowded, which is a plus, and the soup-based bak chor mee is similar to what you'd find at the other locations. However, it could use a bit more umami.

Considering the price and the absence of a queue, it's a satisfying and convenient option.

author: ray toei
review_text:
You know this place is specially when 1/3 to half of the people are eating the noodles.

So so so reminds me of the Bedok south (morning)and the Bedok north (night) bcm. From the type QQ thin-broad noodles to the bakchor that surrounds the soup and the wanton. The soup is very slightly more salty than the Bedok north one.

4.80 sgd

author: William Tan
review_text:
This noodle place has been known for many years for the long Queues and waiting time.
I waited for 45mins with at least 15ppl in front on a PH afternoon. So be prepared to wait.

When the noodle is prepared, I must say it smells wonderful with the right amount of chilli and vinegar to complement the flavour. Springy and well seasoned and well greased! Yes…! It is filled with pork oil and lards (not for the faint hearted)

Eat mouthful is pack with flavour in my dried version. The soup filled with mince pork, garlic and meat dumpling is equally wonderful.

Had a bowl of fish ball soup and it tasted okay. Guess that is not their forte.

A wonderful bowl of “old school” (100yrs plus) heritage noodle as claimed. Will just hope the wait is shorter or at least used a numbering system to let us seat and wait…..

Parking is available but limited, so do have to wait for a while. Near the train station so that’s a plus. Spacious seating area and well ventilated!

Wheelchairs are accessible with slight ramp but mostly flat grounds.

Compare to the famous Bedok competitor… hands down a winner here!

P/s: maybe it’s just me but don’t down all the delicious soup as I had to flush down a lot of water after which. Hint hint…

author: CT liaw
review_text:
Spare ribs: Tender and easy to eat, ever encounter some rib not really not easy fall off the bone.
Soup not so favourable.

Pig's trotter: The sauce is thick and nice but meat is a bit tough.

author: Janchicsiken
review_text: I can see why my colleague recommended this spot - we got the pig trotters, pork ribs soup, salted veg and youtiao to share and the portions were perfect. The pork ribs were pretty generous, and of course the soup is free flow (for dine in). Very 老味道

author: Vee 祐宁 L
review_text:
I would think it’s quite nice as I love peppery soup. $7 BKT, $8 pork tail, $3- braised bean curbs ..dunno how much is salted vege & rice as we ordered separately.

Meat is tender and hard at the same time, came here for dinner as dropping girl for driving lesson. Hard as in I guess it’s freshly cooked and not long enough. Soft as in there are fats in the pork ribs, yummy…

Oh ya, I went to top up soup which they willingly gave..

Overall I think it’s good.. but quite costly for $7 BKT w/o rice..

The coffeeshop is very noisy though ..

author: Sleepy Snoopy
review_text: Value for money, the best was the pork trotter , deeply braised soak well in the sauce dark enough , peppery soup and tender pork ribs, peanuts was well cooked $10 pork ribs , $9 trotter , free refill soup

author: Charmaine
review_text:
Eat here if you want to experience the worst bak kut teh!
Soup was meh, just peppery and savoury without much depth of flavour
The worst crime was the you tiao which tastes like it has been kept for one year, it’s almost like a bun/bread texture instead of the crispy treat you expect.
Apparently this used to be good but I was SO disappointed

author: Hoong Wai Wong
review_text:
Had the $9 pig's trotter, added $2 said veggie and rice.

Pigs trotter not bad, the gravy is thick and sticky with the dissolved collagen, goes will with the rice. Meat portion is quite abit maybe cos I ordered the larger portion.

Salted veggie is expensive, small plate for $2 not worth it. Can skip.

Overall not that fantastic, can eat lah...

author: Richard Sng
review_text: I paid $7.80 for this BKT with rice. First impression is nothing spectacular. However I got a wow effect when I start eating. The soup is peppery with a hint of herbs favour. The pork ribs are super tender, literally melt in your mouth. The unassuming dark sauce is one of the main actor. It is spicy enough to kick off the overall Shiokness. I must say this is one of the best BKT around. Totally worth it.

author: Chan Yenny
review_text:
Taste is ok. But portion too little for the pork trotter with rice which cost $10 ish.

Ordered takeaway and seller gave me one pcs of big bone with like almost no meat at all... The portion is even lesser than my house area coffee shop which sells cheaper then him.

author: Tom Kang
review_text:
Way over priced for the portion. Nearly cannot finish my rice as there are too little meat given.

As per photo, $9.50, which is totally not worth it as it doesn't taste as good before.

The meat seems to be cooked over and over for many times. Tasted very "old".  Probably is the case since their standard dropped and customer traffic is lesser?

Verdict : thanks but no thanks

author: benson ang
review_text:
Kimly Coffee shop setting.
Meat is big bone with meat still ok.
But the side dishes portion are small and $2 up.

The same price can eat at those established BKT restaurants.

Not worth.

Try once will do.

author: zhen qin lee
review_text: Excellent food and uncle is so nice! Best braised pig trotter ever!

author: Han Sin Chia
review_text:
The bakuteh is not bad. The meat very tender n tasty. The soup is thick n peppery, the peppe is a little strong, but still OK.

Song Fa is better by a bit but double the price. For this price... Unbeatable 😂

author: Zhi Chiaw Lim
review_text: SCAMMER ALERT! Told me the BKT was $7 when I ordered, then collected $10 from me when served.

author: Susanna Pettigrew
review_text: Nice, very peppery broth, really tender, soft ribs and nice side dishes. We had the salted veg and braised beancurd. Friendly aunty and good value for money. I would recommend.

author: L Luo
review_text: Decided to get some food from here despite stopping for many years due to a bad experience. Unfortunately they have used up all the goodwill. There was hardly any meat on my pig trotter and the kiam chye tasted like there wasn't any effort to cook it at all. All these plus a rice for 9.50. And I'm already browsing my phone for other food

author: JASON
review_text: 9.5sgd definitely not worth the price, the soup is basicly tasteless and the YOUTIAO is HARDER than my life!! I usually dip youtiao in soup like few seconds but now i leave it there like fishball nia.

author: Rachel Low
review_text: Hawker owner was busybody and walked towards my group of friends when we were just checking out our friend’s crutches. He scolded us and said 你的老师没有教你这个东西不可以玩吗？ In a very rude voice. We didn’t even bother him and were minding our business then he came up to us and scolded us. After that all he did was glare at us from his stall non - stop, while we were minding our own business. This made us felt very very uncomfortable and felt that he invaded our privacy. Wasn’t a pleasant experience.

author: Chinsiong Lee
review_text: Food expensive and portion small. Asked for $12 bak kut teh was given only 4 pieces of pork rib. Didn't even asked if I wanted rib....which I didn't want. No going back again.

author: Terence Z W Lim
review_text: Wth...even jz a bowl of soup not asking for free...paying for it...also cannot...if not because I want to use cdc....I won't eat it...

author: Jim J
review_text: Pig trotters are really good. Bak Kut Teh is the white peppery type and was ok.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Xin Hao
review_text:
Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup is a solid go-to spot for late-night zi char, especially if you’re craving something hearty and comforting after hours. Located along Changi Road, it’s well known for staying open late, making it a popular supper destination for night owls and shift workers alike.

The food here leans towards classic, no-frills zi char done well. The chao ta bee hoon is a standout, with good wok hei and generous ingredients that make it satisfying without being overly greasy. This was my favorite of all. Starts from $10 for a small portion which can feed about 3pax. The herbal mee sua is another highlight — warm, soothing, and rich with herbal flavours, perfect for something lighter yet nourishing. Portions are generally generous, making it suitable for sharing among a small group. Herbal Chicken Soup was also a good standout for me.

That said, prices can be slightly on the higher side compared to typical hawker fare, and some dishes can be a little inconsistent. For instance, while the overall flavour is good, certain ingredients like pork liver may not always hit the mark texture-wise. The fried pork with fermented beancurd was also really average for me and not super unique. Still, most dishes are well executed and comforting, especially when enjoyed fresh and hot.

Overall, Seng Kee delivers reliable zi char with a strong supper appeal. It may not be the cheapest option around, but if you’re looking for a filling, late-night meal with familiar flavours and decent portions, it’s a dependable choice worth returning to.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: VHong Tan
review_text: Seng Kee’s pig liver mee sua truly lives up to its reputation — it’s really a case of “better tasted than heard.” We also tried the crispy bee hoon and hor fun, and they were all very delicious. 😋

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: I Love Fried Hokkien Mee
review_text: This plate of FHM is the wetter kind, with lots of broth. Pork bones were used as the base, but probably not simmered long enough to bring out deep flavour. The noodles taste raw and there’s no wok-hey, so it’s missing that smoky kick which we usually find in a Cze Char stall. The prawns and sotong were overcooked and a little tough. No pork belly, though there is some crispy pork lard to enjoy. The chili and lime help lift the dish, but overall the ingredients don’t quite come together.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Gavin Zheng (GavinEats)
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
The black vinegar trotter was super tasty — tender meat with just the right balance of sour and sweet! The soups were rich and comforting, perfect on a rainy day. Everything tasted really homemade and full of flavour. Definitely worth coming back for!

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Joanne Lee
review_text:
Bring a neck fan or portable fan. It’s horrendously warm.

Food standard has dropped. The dark soup pig organ’s mee sua still taste nice and rich but the white gravy mee sua tasted so bland, it’s like water. Not the same taste as we recall. Been having food from them once in a while over the past few years.

Ordered some takeaway too and needed to wait for quite a while before they are ready.

Hopefully the takeaway hor fun and fish maw soup maintains the standard.

Ordered a teh peng, which we were told will be made from 3-1 mix (???). Alright… not sure which is the brand being used but it’s like sugar syrup.

Overall, it’s a disappointing experience from the Seng Kee we used to love.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Mckayller Longsbow
review_text:
If you’re looking for authentic herbal soup in Singapore, Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup is a must-try! The black chicken soup is rich, flavorful, and really comforting — perfect if you want something nourishing and tasty. The herbs they use give it a great depth of flavor without being overpowering.

The place is simple and no-frills, but that just adds to the charm. It feels very traditional and homey, like a hidden gem. The staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole experience even better.

Perfect spot to warm up and recharge, especially if you enjoy traditional Asian herbal cuisine. I’d definitely come back!

Friend brought me here, great!

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Jayven Phang Jun Wei
review_text:
See Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup shop is located within waking distance from Kembagan MRT or if you drive there is parking along the nearby street.

Ate here multiple time with different groups and I highly recommend the beehoon, prawn balls and pork cutlet fried rice. Price point is decent and portions are generous for any group size!

Highly recommend for anyone looking for good food in the east, especially near an MRT station. To my understanding they only accept cash/paynow and no paywave so something to take note.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: The Chopsticks
review_text: When to have dinner here on Friday night around 7pm and there’s no queue.. so we ordered first and pay before getting seated. Came here from looking at tiktok.. i must say the star is really the herbal chicken soup.. it was really good and the soup is flavourful authentic.. i had the ginseng chicken. The steam fish and spicy sauce in my opinion second best but the fish that i had chosen was an old big fish i think not so great the texture.. despite that i still like the soup gravy. The crab bee hoon not too bad can be more crispy. The squid portion is alot for 2 person we didnt finish it.. overall is good, the place is pack with patron and constant queue. I would be back just to drink the herban chicken 😂👍.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Adrian Wong
review_text:
Black chicken was underwhelming for it's price. Tastes as decent as hawker ones, just overpriced.
Only special thing is the kidney mee sua, noodles are served thin & very chewable. An uncommon dish in SG, reasonable price.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Frankie Lim
review_text:
Infamous kidney mee sua soup and many other good dishes ( sesame chicken, dried fragrance fish head, vegetable...etc) from this long history authentic restaurant at changi.

There's another one at kaki bukit food center.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Marcuz Pae
review_text:
walking distance from kembangan MRT, excellent place to have tzechar if you are willing to wait since there’s lots of people on the weekend.

their signature is the black chicken herbal soup, the flavour of the soup is quite clear with a mild umani taste. the must order carbs will be the crispy bee hoon, with the mee sua. in addition, meat dishes you can order the pork belly, prawn paste chicken and the steamed pork, perfect for a family dinner near the MRT.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Velika Mustika
review_text:
Seng Kee is one of my go-to spots when I’m craving something satisfying and comforting especially at night or supper.

Their chili crab is an absolute highlight—packed with flavour and just the right level of spice. It’s messy in the best way and perfect for sharing!

Another must-try is the Herbal Pork Mee Sua with Intestine. The soup is rich and nourishing, with deep herbal notes, and the mix of tender pork and intestine adds great texture and taste. It’s comfort food at its finest.

I also love their Sesame Black Chicken—fragrant, juicy, and full of goodness. And don’t miss out on the Crispy Bee Hoon! It’s crispy on the outside yet soft inside, and goes so well with the rest of the dishes.

Basically, I love all the foods here. 😛 I’ll definitely be back for more!

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: ken goh
review_text: Liver in the soup had black spots . Meat was clumped like it was frozen. Kidney had a really strong smell. We are long time customers. Unfortunately standards seem to be dropping.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Adrick Loh
review_text:
Came many times for dinner here. Normally would order their pork mee sua and liver mee sua for wifey. This time ordered their white mee sua. More like soup but flavor and ingredients are to my liking. Their yellow wine lala is our favorite now. At $15 but worth it. Yellow wine is sweet and lala is the freshest I ever had in SG though small sized. We drink finish the yellow wine soup.
P.S if you dun like your liver more than 50% raw need to tell them u like them cooked. It will still come out 30% raw.
Tried their seafood white beehoon. Stock is good but overall taste no as good as Sembawang popular white beehoon. My gout was activated after 15 mins into eating it. Confirmed rich in ingredients. lol
Came on May 2025, their lala got strong fishy taste. The variety is different from the one I raved about the previous month.
Came on Jun 2025. Tried their fried mee Sua. Not bad, I like.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Tan Jie Kai
review_text:
Note to order before being seated, staff will assign seats depending on the dishes you ordered too incase the table is too small.

Ordered 6 dishes for 3 pax and surprised that it was just nice, few highlights included Sesame oil claypot chicken which was quite flavourful and the Mee sua with pork and seafood stir fry is must try. Would come back again to try out more of the dishes didn’t disappoint so far

Service wise you will have to walk to the counter for any add on, drinks too.

Atmosphere better to sit by a fan or air conditioned area as the assigned area we sat was quite warm with only 1 fan on oscillation.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Adrian Ng (Realtor Consultant)
review_text: Came with family for a late dinner. Ordered the usual mee sua, fried pork belly, steamed squid and fish hor fun. Food taste good except for the hor fun which is totally bland. Price is reasonable, serving sizes are good. However staff attitudes are bad and quite rude. So suggest just come, eat, go. Don't expect friendly service.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Claxton Ng
review_text: Recommended by my colleague. Came to try out the foods. Food is acceptable and variety of choices, price is very reasonable. No wonder the Q are so long. One things I don’t like is the payment type are limited and drinks is order separately from the stall, very inconvenient.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: My KING Seah
review_text: One of my favorite local zhi char restaurant to go to whenever we have a large group. Food is good and not pricey. Ingredients are fresh and don’t have any unpleasant surprises. Parking is difficult and will have to go early to avoid the queue.

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Albert Tan
review_text:
Been patronising Seng Kee for more than 10 years

Today am pleasantly served by Melvin , he is very professional, friendly and attentive to our needs and ensure our request are taken care of.

Can see he has great passion in his work.

Thank you Melvin

restaurant: Seng Kee Black Chicken Herbal Soup Pte Ltd
author: Caleb Tan
review_text: Affordable tze char in the east! Their signature beehoon is really good. Didn’t get to try their crabs cause it was sold out so we had the slipper lobsters instead. Very crowded so might need to queue if you don’t have a reservation. They have multiple seating areas spread across different units. Hard to find parking so need to park at a small open air carpark 5 mins walk away.

author: Bryan Tan
review_text:
Laksa for $6.50. Although slightly above the usual laksa prices, the cockles were given generously and size of it were relatively bigger. Soup is fragrant and had all the makings of what a laksa should have.

Some of the tofu puffs were slightly hard though. Felt as though they haven't been cooked in the laksa broth at the start😅. The rest were fine. Noodles portioned out fine too.

author: Yaz F A
review_text: Good food and friendly staff. Chicken porridge was delicious

author: Bien Claro Blanco
review_text:
I tried this and was REALLY DISAPPOINTED. DEFINITELY NOT RECOMMENDED. I waited for a while and the chicken rice was poorly served — for $5.30, I got a small, unappetizing portion with no soup, and not even any cucumber.

Local vendors still offer much better food quality and portion sizes.

author: josh li
review_text:
Roast chicken both meat n rice were dry, soup heavily laced with msg n still tasted terrible.
Chicken cutlet laska soup not hot enough with noodles undercooked.
Only cash or paynow accepted although multiple modes of payment stated.
Really regretted even trying out esp when Eng's hainanese chicken rice in e hawker centrenever disappoints. Must be fake google reviews!

author: Muhd
review_text: Too slow waited 30mins just for 1 packet takeaway. Please improve your manpower at this outlet. Still want take orders from walk in when others are still waiting for their food? Keep my $7 change.

author: Special K
review_text: Ordered through food delivery. Food is ok. Rice is fragrant enough. Portions could be a little more generous  though.

author: Albert Foodie
review_text:
The chicken texture is smooth and tasty
The laksa soup has rich coconut flavors. Not too impressed with their fried items. Overall very good chicken rice and laksa

author: Keng Fai
review_text:
Nothing fantastic. Humful Laksa only a name doesn't reflect on the amount of hum in the dish. Noodles also not cooked well. Clumped together and stick together. Wondering what was I eating.

For $6.50 can get much better laksa with more Hum at many other places.

author: Miss Billionaire
review_text:
Just a nice first try at this shop OK chicken rice.
The food was fresh and high quality. Like it so much !

author: Nicholas Ng
review_text: Tried the all in one laksa. Abit pricey but it includes a generous serving of chicken, 2 prawns, spoonful of hum and half a egg. Overall, a solid experience. Staff are very friendly as well.

author: Vik Su
review_text:
Humless bowl of laksa it was despite the name of the brand. Guess it's better to be harmless to those allergic to cockles.

Taste was alright, lacking some laksa leaves and real hum.

author: Nathanael Eng
review_text: Great atmosphere, amazing service!! Auntie here very cute very nice hehe, portion is a lor for an affordable price — would recommend because it’s quite underrated, their chicken rice is flavourful and their rostered chicken very tender and juicy!!

author: Derrick L
review_text: Average bowl of noodles, haven’t tried their chicken yet, will update again

author: Lee Lin
review_text:
Good food:)
The service here is very good and the staff are really friendly!their chicken rice is so good too!their steamed chicken rice is really very tender and juicy and their chicken rice is extremely affordable.is a must try

author: oscar w
review_text: noticed this brand for quite sometime as I'm a laksa and hum lover. today is the first time I had the chance to try. not sure if quality of food is different if I had chosen to dine in at the coffeeshop. takeaway laksa tastes quite bad. beehoon is not thoroughly cooked, still tough. cockles not fresh seem frozen or kept in the fridge for quite some time and overcooked. lacks laksa leaves. for $6.50 I would have expected better quality.

author: John King (King)
review_text: Tried their chicken rice. Must say that it is really good. Service is great too. Another great chicken rice place in Eunos Crescent

author: Anzac Chew
review_text: Nice Chicken Rice. I had the roast version & it taste great. But they are also very popular with it's humfull lasagne.

author: Nazmi Ridzuan
review_text: The food here is all delicious, staff are very friendly, and the prices are moderate. I personally buy dinner here every day.🫰🏻

author: Jeremy Lim
review_text:
The roast chicken rice was trying to play it crispy and cool, but sadly, it flew too close to the sun. The chicken, though roasted to a decent hue, was dry enough to make you reach for a second glass of water. The rice, fragrant but forgettable, couldn’t save the dish from its lackluster performance. A meal that aimed to roast the competition but ended up just winging it—barely clucking along.

That said, the service was impressively efficient, with a fast turnaround even during the bustling lunch peak, which deserves a nod.

author: Z Z
review_text:
Third time purchasing from them! Never disappoints! The portion size is always just right for me with deliciously tender chicken!

My only suggestion would be to offer plain cucumber as an alternative to the pickled ones, as not everyone might be a fan. It would be great to have the option for customers to choose their preference!

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Velika Mustika
review_text:
My first time here, and as a fish head lover, I had to try their famous fish head steamboat. We went with the grouper. It had a slight fishy smell, but asking for it to be fried beforehand helped a lot. (I’m pretty sensitive to fish smell, so this might not bother others.) The broth was flavorful and comforting, definitely the highlight of the meal.

We also tried the tofu prawn, which could use just a touch more salt, and the potato leaves, which were surprisingly good and a nice balance to the heavier dishes.

Note to self: next time I’ll go for the medium portion of potato leaves 😁

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Benny Tan
review_text: The fish head soup offers a delightful and flavorful experience. The Ha cheong gai is exceptionally well-prepared and succulent. The tofu prawn dish, complemented by a rich chili-crab-inspired gravy, is also highly recommended. Furthermore, the establishment provides convenient parking and ample seating within a comfortable, air-conditioned dining environment.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Shan Leong
review_text: Food was good, but not all dishes. Price is reasonable with that portion. Service was friendly and dish was serve fast after order. Even offer to top up soup, when they see getting low in the pot. Environment was ok, standard foodcourt with air-con. Will visit again.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: SH Y
review_text: Our first time here and we are pleasantly surprised by the quality of food served. All dishes are well executed and dish out so fast. Esp liked the cereal prawn and eggs. The soup were very nice too. As much as we are planning another visit this weekend!

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Crumpled Nomad
review_text:
Dropped by Tian Wai Tian at StarHub Green for dinner and it really hit the spot. Their traditional fish head steamboat cooked over charcoal gives the soup a depth of flavor you just can’t get with modern setups. The broth was rich, smoky, and comforting – perfect for sharing with family and friends.

We ordered a variety of dishes alongside the steamboat, and honestly, every dish was solid. Portions were generous, flavors were spot on, and the prices felt very reasonable for the quality and spread we had – definitely good value for money.

The ambience is no-frills and fuss-free, just like how a proper local zi char place should be. You come here for the food and leave satisfied – simple as that. Highly recommend if you’re craving old-school charcoal steamboat.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Jinchoon
review_text: It's a dish that is bold yet refined, rustic yet sophisticated, and offers a truly unique and memorable culinary adventure that is deeply rooted in the food culture of the region. It's not just good; it's an iconic experience.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Hui Ling Tan
review_text: Yummy food but the tofu prawn gravy not as flavourful as the one in harbourfront. Food court was aircon but smoky though. Smelt of steam boat after dinner. Service was prompt n efficient. Toilet was ok and provided with toilet paper and hand soap.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Yang Eu
review_text:
This branch is located in an air-conditioned food court. Most stalls are not open in the evening as its located in industrial area.
There are many large tables suitable for larger family or groups.
Price is the same as the original shop but there is a slight difference in taste. Nonetheless, the fish soup is still tasty and in a more comfortable setting.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: BABY GERM
review_text:
I visited Tian Wei Tian Fish Steamboat at Starhub Green Foodcourt on a Sunday afternoon, and it was surprisingly quiet. The air conditioning was strong and kept the place cool. I ordered a variety of dishes, including the 𝐟𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐚𝐦𝐛𝐨𝐚𝐭, 𝐡𝐚𝐫 𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐨𝐧𝐠 𝐠𝐚𝐢 (𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐰𝐧 𝐩𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐧), 𝐬𝐚𝐦𝐛𝐚𝐥 𝐩𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐨 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐬, 𝐲𝐚𝐦 𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐡 𝐛𝐞𝐚𝐧𝐬, 𝐬𝐞𝐚𝐟𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐭𝐨𝐟𝐮, 𝐭𝐨𝐟𝐮 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐰𝐧𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐝 𝐞𝐠𝐠 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐨𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫.⁣
⁣
The soup was refillable, which was a nice touch. The fried egg with oyster was a bit oily for my liking, but the har cheong gai was excellent. Overall, the meal was pretty decent, with each dish offering its own unique flavors.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: CHOW GENE
review_text: Food were heavily tasted and suitable for those who likes salty food .  Service lady with blonde hair just DROPPED !!!  our food on the other end of our table !! and we need to stretch and reach out for it !!! We paid for the food and we are not beggars !!!

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Samuel Ho
review_text:
Come specially for the fish head steamboat so decide to Order the Red Grouper fish steamboat. But when the food is served, the meat was actually Black Grouper. (those who are familiar with fish will know the price difference) Ask the staff twice, they'd till dare to say Red Grouper have black spots thus the skin were black. 😒

Besides, the fish is very fishy! (means it isn't fresh) as before I order, they still ask if the fish wants to be deep fried? (only poor quality fish then people will deep fry) Who the hell will deep fry Fresh fish meant for fish steamboat?

Really very bad experience and treating the customers like their dumb or idiots that don't know how to differentiate what they're eating.

The only saving grace is the tofu prawn, which is nice. Better off going to their main outlet in Serangoon Road or other places like in Beach Road for it! (Got scammed once and never again!)

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Cindy Kor
review_text: The food was absolutely excellent – every dish was fresh, flavorful, the quality exceeded expectations. Highly recommend for anyone looking for great food and a memorable meal!

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Rene Ang (Rene)
review_text:
Portion size great. Food not bad but not super amazing. Will rate the taste 7/10 overall.

We had 5 dishes shared amongst 6 people and it was just nice, had enough for everyone and did not struggle to finish. Came here on a weekend and there’s ample parking within the building. Relatively new eatery, clean and air conditioned (a plus!!!)

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Jonathan Goh
review_text:
Was here the week before Father’s Day on a weekend and it was so packed!
Amazingly this was an industrial location and apparently, everyone saw the Facebook posts to come to this outlet.
The place is a food court but it was filled mostly by patrons for this stall. Booking only gets you a place but you’ll need to queue to order.
Paynow or cash only.
Food took 1 hour before it started coming to our table and the fish head steamboat came last.
Most dishes were reasonably priced and taste good. The egg with oyster didn’t look like the photo at all but we didn’t bother to dispute cause it was so late and we were hungry.
Sweet and sour pork can give a miss.
Everything else is decent and worth a try.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Evonne Seah
review_text: We are there to celebrate dad birthday & we have a total of 13pax  . So glad that they have  海鲜长寿面 Seafood Longevity Noodle to pre order & when we ask if they have any other pre order dishes they recommended us big crab 🦀. We love the salted egg crab for those who don’t eat spicy food & black pepper for those who loved spicy food , really delicious & we will come back soon again

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: J T
review_text: Went on a weekday evening so it was not crowded. Finally had the pomfret steamboat that is always not available at the other outlet. The oyster omelette is quite unique, ease of ordering and payment.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Melissa Cheok
review_text: Came here for dinner on National Day with mt family of 30 people and everyone liked the food. Particularly the fish steamboat .. the kids loved it.. will definitely recommend this place for families... the location might need you to drive tho.. and the environment is a foodcourt environment... but price is fair and reasonable!

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Yvonne Yeoh
review_text:
Aircon food court. We used to go to this makan place at Moonstone Lane. However, the flavour of the food whilst good, Standard has dropped a bit.

Good part was we came for a late lunch Sunday and the food came very quickly and there was hardly any wait.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Martin Yeo
review_text:
Their garoupa fish steamboat was delicious and tasty. The soup has a thick flavour and is tasty with rice or just sipping it hot. The fish meat is fresh and mouthwatering with its chilli dip sauce. Their signature chilli prawns is another high recommendation. Serves hot with a thick gravy and soft tofu, and goes well with plain rice or just by itself.
Great fast service in a cool and clean dining environment.

restaurant: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (StarHub Green)
author: Jodie
review_text:
Fishhead steamboat tasteless and not thick enough as compared to the original outlet and even kovan branch.

Feels like the Har Cheong Gai uses a different batter / frying method. Not as crispy. No one near the original one

Oyster omelette and cuttlefish kangkong and tofu prawn is decent.

Wouldn't come back again for the fishsoup but if you want an affordable meal with the family it's great because there's aircon, lots of parking and the space is huge.

Long line of customers by 6.30 on a sunday but there's more than enough tables to go around.

author: Eric Lee
review_text:
I takeaway at least 2X per month from here coz nasi lemak is my favourite.

Service
The staff here is very efficient and fast so even if there’s a queue, it’ll clear pretty quickly (customers need to decide what they want earlier to facilitate this).  They’ll also accommodate any reasonable request (eg:separate pack the chicken wings).

Food
Love their rice (very fragrant and fluffy) and their chicken wings is insanely crispy (really shiok).  The Ngoh Hiang is also very good, but I don’t see much customers ordering this.

Conclusion
A little ex, but worth paying the premium coz it’s nice.  The must order stuff:
1) Chicken Wing - Mac shiokkk
2) Ngoh Hiang - bite into the chestnut and feel the crunch.
3) Egg - ask for runny and let the yolk seep into the rice.
4) Silver Fish - crispy and best combo with the rice & chilli.

author: CP
review_text: When it comes to Nasi Lemak, it isn't far-fetched to say that everyone in Singapore knows about Ponggol Nasi Lemak. They do a few things consistently well: the coconuty rice, the sambal, and the crunchy fried chicken wings. Among their outlets, the Serangoon and Tanjong Katong locations always attract snaking queues. It is a meal that feels both heartwarming and hearty every single time.

author: Howcan Eats
review_text:
A pretty standard nasi lemak - not outstanding but also nothing that we would complain about. Offers a good variety of ingredients, most of which tasted freshly cooked. The sambal had a good heat and paired well with the coconut rice. Do note that ikan bilis and peanuts are offered as separate ala carte ingredients and do not come with the rice by default.

The standout ingredient though is the chicken wing - freshly fried, crispy and wonderfully aromatic.

author: Chong Tee Lim
review_text:
Ponggol Nasi Lemak Centre sits tucked in the everyday hustle—unassuming frontage, open windows, and the comforting aroma of coconut rice, sambal, and fried goodies welcoming you in. Inside, it’s a blend of hawker energy and family rhythm: metal tables, plastic stools, lunch crowds, and the occasional diner asking in Malay for extra ikan bilis.

They do what they do with no frills but serious care. The nasi lemak arrives with fluffy, fragrant rice, each grain carrying creaminess but not sogginess. The sambal has a measured heat—not numbing or flat but soulful, slightly sweet with a hint of smokiness, picking up complexity at the edges. You’ll find crispy fried chicken with skin that snaps under your fork, ikan bilis that crunch, peanuts toasted, and custard egg just soft enough to ooze without chaos.

What stands out is how the flavours balance—nothing overpowers. The sambal, the rice, the sides—they hold their own but also support each other. It’s not gimmicky; it’s the kind of plate you taste room-by-room, noticing little things you’ll want again.

Service is hawker speed but with care. The workers are efficient without being robotic—tea top-ups come without asking, and they’ll clear tonight’s empty plates to make space for more. Prices stay kind, making this place as satisfying for daily habit as for those occasional cravings.

If you’re around Punggol or passing through and want a solid plate of nasi lemak that hits both heart and hunger, this is one you’ll keep coming back to.

author: Hulk
review_text: Extremely overrated $9.70 to be exact. Rice was not fragrant at all. Look at the soulless fried egg, it basically represents how my plate of nasi lemak tasted. Chili was it self made? … better off getting it from ntuc shelves. The chicken wings were a sure bet though!

author: lolli _k
review_text: A satisfying fix for nasi lemak cravings. The chicken wing is crispy and tasty. I personally prefer the usual ikan bilis over the tiny silverfish version (银鱼仔), but it’s still alright. The chili is flavourful with a nice kick. The rice is nice and fragrant, though not the best I’ve had. Overall, still a solid and enjoyable plate of nasi lemak.

author: Adeline Ng
review_text:
It’s like our fortnight event with Katong Punggol Nasi Lemak!
I wouldn’t say which dish is my favourite as in fact, every dish is top-notch and it’s always a challenge to pick what will be in my box. A good thing we always pack at least 8 to 12 person boxes so we can go home and “mix and match” kind of fun!
We will always pack extra cabbage curry and Achar for the next day lunch!

author: Avijeet Sen
review_text:
Have visited this outlet of Punggol Nasi Lemak as few times. I feel it’s like any standard 4 rating (out of 5) Nasi Lemak place. Nonetheless, it’s a decent place to quench your Nasi Lemak cravings. Dunno if they have a standard Nasi Lemak set which you can order because whenever I’ve visited, I’ve just chosen the various side dishes to go along with the rice and fried chicken.

Overall, a decent place to stop by for lunch for dinner if you’re in the area. But not sure if the place matches its hype.

author: Christopher Ho
review_text: Punggol Nasi Lemak is highly praised for its exceptional quality, featuring fragrant, coconut milk-infused rice, a balanced sweet-spicy sambal, and consistently fresh, piping hot side dishes like the famous crispy fried chicken wings. Be prepared for a long queue during dinner, with wait times often around half an hour, as this is a popular spot with a high demand for its delicious fare.

author: Clara Poh
review_text: Liked the fragrant coconut rice and crispy chicken wing. Takeaway box consists of coconut rice, a slice of cucumber, 2 small fish, 2 pcs of ngoh hiang and 5 pcs of brinjal that costs $9 +$0.40 (for the box), 4 chicken wings in a brown bag $8+$0.10cents (for the small paper bag). An additional spoon of ikan bills onto the rice box is $1+$0.30cents.( Why? The 30 cents) Total $28.20. Overpriced takeaway in expensive packaging.

author: Ryan
review_text:
One of the best Nasi lemak in SG. Power in Boon Lay is my other favourite.

Rice is fragrant consistently and chicken wings are to die for!! Pricey though, expect to spend ~$10. Expect to queue if you go at peak meal times

author: Leville
review_text: Clean place with consistent food. Eggs are all done properly. Overall a very good experience here.

author: darius
review_text:
Good plate of nasi lemak and an even better supper spot (till 2330). The rice was fresh and fragrant, with a good hint of coconut taste in it.

Egg and luncheon meat is what you expect from it.

The stars of the show are definitely the chicken wing and sambal. Firstly, the chicken wing was extremely crispy with a good layer of batter, followed by juicy chicken breast. The sambal was spicy and has a good kick to it. It complemented the rice extremely well.

My only regret was not getting the ikan bills with it. This plate costed $7.50, a little pricy

author: Shelley Goh
review_text: Food quality is good but not exceptional. It’s standard Nasi Lemak fare. Rice portion is abit too small. Also, there is no itemized breakdown of ordered items in the receipt. Hard to know if I’m being charged correctly. Just got to have faith in the cashier and pray they don’t make a mistake. It will be great if the business can work to improve on transparency in this area.

author: Justin Lim
review_text: The best Nasi Lemak in town! Even though it’s a bit pricey, I’m still happy to pay more for such a delicious dish. The dine-in environment is also impressive, the floor and tables are cleaned frequently, and the whole place feels very clean and bright

author: Melvin “Mel” Tang
review_text: The standard like drop liao leh.  Rice has nearly zero  lemak taste.. prawn taste like frozen kind. Saving grace is the chicken wing, otah and ah zhar.

author: Terrick W.
review_text: Finally had chance to revisit Punggol Nasi Lemak. Their queue is still consistently long but it moves pretty fast. We did both dine in and takeaway. Dishes wise their standard pretty comsistent. But sadly their food temperature is not right. Especially the rice, it was less than room temperature. Later we noticed new batch of rice and dishes came out hot. Perhaps just bad timing?

author: Teck Boon
review_text: Food standard at this location is always consistent. Service is prompt and efficient and tables are cleaned quickly to ensure that people will always be able to find a table soon. Slightly more expensive than other nasi lemak store but quality is good and that’s why there’s always a queue for food. It also means things are always fresh and hot.

author: Forest House
review_text: This is the best nasi lemak to my taste. Apart from the delicious food, the restaurant is always kept clean and bright.

author: Mr Fock
review_text: This Nasi Lemak is overpriced basic ikan bilis is charge instead of including it 3 dishes $6.30 ridiculous the taste also more or less the same as the ordinary Nasi Lemak 👎🏻

author: Mimi
review_text: This is a must-visit every time I’m in Singapore. The frog meat is always fresh, tender, and perfectly cooked, with no gamey taste at all. The sauce is rich and aromatic, pairing beautifully with the smooth, comforting porridge. I personally prefer this place over Eminent, the flavors here are more balanced and satisfying. Simple, local setting, but consistently great food. I never skip this spot when visiting Singapore.

author: EA TO
review_text:
Ordered the ginger onion frog legs (2 servings - $22) and porridge ($11) which was enough for 2 people. The frog legs are tasty and the muscle fibers are slightly shorter than chicken and have a flakiness like fish. Meat falls off the bones easily. I enjoyed it.

Prefer to eat the porridge and frog legs separately because the sauce of the frog legs will make the thick porridge more watery.

Fast service - ordered and paid soon after we were seated. Staff was helpful in her reccomendations which helped as it was my first time trying frog leg porridge.

Seated outside which was quite windy that night. Good vibes and breeze.

Crowded at 7 but still got a seat outside

author: Hai Phan (Francis)
review_text: This is where I often go to eat the famous Singapore frog porridge. I just came back and felt the taste of the dish is still great. The service is very fast, professional, reasonable price. The restaurant is clean and the staff is quite enthusiastic.

author: Benedict Chua
review_text:
Servers were readily available and took orders rapidly. The porridge smooth, had a claypot taste to it which was unique; higher end restaurants sometimes use milk to smooth out the texture.

The frog was really fresh, springy and chewy, with the cartilage still crunchy.

Bad part is for flavours wise, it is be-your-own-chef and add your own amounts of soy sauce and ginger. So you do not really get to know the chef’s skill.

author: Dalfin Chow
review_text: bowl was changed to plastic ! not environmentally friendly nor is it good for us diners to put hot porridge into plastic bowls.Micro plastic being consumed alongside our food for the convenience  and cost cutting measures of the owner .Will not patronise again until proper non toxic bowls and spoons are used.

author: Sharon Lee
review_text: Frog leg was good, staff all friendly and nice. Stingray was normal only but the price is considered okay for the amount of food we had.

author: Thanh Nguyên
review_text:
The must-go place when arrived in Singapore. Hot porridge and well marinated frog becomes the best combination.
Fried oyster with egg is should be tried also, but be careful if you dont like oily dishes.

In conclusion, it is the best choice for a supper.

author: Aloyscious Lee
review_text:
The frog legs are fresh, tender, yet with enough bite, paired with sauce that is flavourful (umami, a bit gingery / soy / sweet / spicy depending on version).

The congee is neutral enough to take on the flavours of the frog sauce.

For people who like spicy, the dried chili / gong bao style gives the kick. For me, I always go for the mild/ non-spicy, preserving more delicate flavours (ginger, spring onion, the frog’s natural taste).

author: Jason Cheong
review_text: We started eating the porridge here since early 2000. Over the years the quality is still maintained and not far away. Recent years this shop is getting more and more famous.  If you come at the peak time you will need to wait for 20-30mins.

author: KK
review_text: Best frog porridge in my life. I always go to this restaurant every time that I visited Singapore. Even though there are plenty of frog porridge restaurants including in youtube or influencers review or anything, I think the taste cannot beat this restaurant. Good to try and you will love it. Previously, I’m not the people who gonna eat frog.

author: Kevin M
review_text: Meaty frog logs and delicious spicy sauce. Enjoyed our meal here. A little on the expensive side...but worth it. Definitely try the spicy one. The tables are outdoor with fans. Service was fine. Will be back again.

author: Chris Ang
review_text: One of the best place for claypot froglegs cravings. Excellent service even when the crowds keeps coming. Service staffs were prompt and fast in any requests.  Well done!

author: Chui Mun
review_text:
When you’re in Geylang, trying frog porridge is a must — it seems to be the most recommended dish in the area. I arrived around 7pm expecting a queue, but luckily there were still a few seats available.

I had never tried frog porridge before and couldn’t quite imagine how it would taste, but it completely exceeded my expectations! The frog meat was incredibly tender and bouncy while the porridge was so smooth and soft. you could almost eat it without using teeth, haha!

We also ordered cockles and grilled fish, which were both fresh and full of flavor. The dishes came out quite fast too, so there was no long wait.

Overall the experience was satisfying from start to finish. 👍🏻

author: Takahiro Koyama
review_text:
Geylang Lor 9 Frog Porridge (芽笼九巷活田鸡) has been serving up its famous frog dishes since 1995, and it’s won tons of awards like The GreenBook Best Food Awards and Singapore Brands Awards. Open daily from 11:00 AM to 4:00 AM, it’s super convenient—just a heads up, it gets really busy at night and into the late hours.

The menu has all kinds of frog dishes like frog porridge, claypot frog, and fried frog, plus seafood, chicken, and veggie options too. You can choose portions for 1, 2, or 3 people for the porridge and claypot frog, so it’s fun to order different spice levels and share with friends.

Dry Chili Frog (宮保田鸡)
This one’s spicy! It’s frog cooked in a sweet soy-based sauce packed with dried chilies. If you’re not big on heat, go for the Ginger Spring Onion version instead. The frog meat includes legs, shoulders, and more—tastes kind of like a cross between cod and chicken. The thighs are especially juicy and flavorful!

Ginger Fried Frog (蒜片炸田鸡)
This dish has chopped frog pieces lightly battered and fried until crispy. Each bite is crunchy on the outside and tender inside, with a simple salt seasoning. Don’t forget to dip it in chili sauce—so good!

Plain Porridge (白粥・小)
Lime Juice with Sour Plum
Ice Jelly (愛玉冰)

author: lee chaiyin
review_text: The porridge frog was very tasty I ben eat almost more than 10 years the taste still same and the sauce very delicious , price oso cheap n environment was very clean

author: Shem
review_text: The frog dish cooked in ginger and spring onion was indeed very flavorful, stingray just as good. The gong gong (shellfish) was a disappointment. They are not fresh, overcooked and when you are able to pull any flesh out of the shell, they are slimy which means they are probably rotten.

author: Bryan (SMAD)
review_text:
We had a fantastic dining experience at Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Porridge (芽笼九巷活田鸡)! The frog porridge here is absolutely delicious and lived up to all the great reviews we've heard. The frog meat was tender and flavorful, cooked to perfection. The white porridge was very well done, smooth and comforting with just the right consistency.

We also recommend the homemade fried prawns—the chilli sauce had a perfect balance of spicy and sour. The stingray was also very well done, adding to the variety of tasty dishes. It's a pity the cockles were not available during our visit, but we still had an amazing meal.

However, the staff could improve their professionalism. They announced the overall bill amount out front, which felt a bit rude. It would be better if they asked how we would like to make payment and guided us downstairs to settle the bill before eating. Despite this, the restaurant has a lively atmosphere, and the food quality makes it a true gem for food lovers. If you're in the Geylang area and looking for a unique and tasty meal, we highly recommend trying this place!

author: Quittance
review_text: One of my favourite food in Singapore, I absolutely adore the gong bao flavour. 1 frog per person is enough for a tasting, 2 frogs are enough to feel fulfilled.

author: Phat Nguyen
review_text:
A very popular place for frog porridge, noticed this place is highly recommended on all the websites and with all the awards shown on the store front.
We ordered frog porridge, which is ordered based on how any frogs you would like, and a clay of porridge. The spicy level can be adjusted. It was quite good, the frog was tender and the sauce was well flavoured.
We also ordered fried oysters but the dish was just okay, nothing special. The stir fried veggies was the same as well, overall this was an okay meal, nothing too special.

author: LW Chua
review_text: Their frog porridge is the perfect late-night treat. The porridge is silky and savory, and the tender frog meat with fresh herbs makes it both comforting and flavorful.

author: Cao Nguyen
review_text: Food is nice, unique and very tasty, especially their signature "white pepper crab" dish. I personally think it is a bit over price but it is fine, we paid for what we wanted 😀😃. Our group is 9pax, eat and drink beer, total bill S$588, happy ending, haha.

author: Tan Yung Yung
review_text:
06 JANUARI 2026
J.B. San Lou Bee Hoon (S) Very yummy , smoky , flavourfull, never let us down

Cod Steak (S) this time a little bit rough , not as soft as we ate before , but over all still yummy

Longan Pineapple Sweet & Sour Pork yummy but to sour for me

Rice,  a bowl full that so satisfying

Barley with ice , nice not too sweet

author: Abby Y
review_text:
Chanced upon this place which was fairly booked but had space for walk-in. Large indoor dining area comprising of 2 shop spaces, with air-conditioning and looks clean.
Qr code given to make orders, which allowed customisation eg less salt, no msg etc.
San lou beehoon was great! Well seasoned with slignt char and wok hey. Sambal kangkong- cant fault that. Deep fried pork belly was crunchy with good ratio of fat and meat.

author: Dai Wen Sim
review_text:
Kinda disappointed with their sanlou mi fen. I was expecting a more crunchy texture and wok hei taste but it turned out to be really average.

Shoutout to their white pepper crab though! One of the best I’ve had. Really fragrant

author: Cheryl T.
review_text:
This place is practically an institution in Geylang. Everyone knows JB Ah Meng. I’ve heard of them for years but never came because we’ve heard of the long queues. But we just came here on a Friday evening at 7pm and guess what - no queue. Not only was there zero queue, there were even many empty tables. Did we get lucky or have people moved on from this place?

We ordered a bunch of dishes for 2pax and spent $183. The crab goes for about $10/100g. To be honest, the white pepper crab is not my favourite style of having crab but I can see why some might like it. I have to say we got a good crab though, as the flesh was firm and not mushy. The chaotah beehoon is also renowned but I’ve had better elsewhere. They should make it crispier and add pieces of pork lard or belly instead of using lean pork.

Overall we left feeling stuffed and satisfied with leftovers to spare. We wouldn’t mind coming back again but would definitely not queue for anything more than 5mins for a table, as this has turned out to be a pretty run-of-the-mill tzechar spot. Not bad, but not mindblowing.

author: yc zhong
review_text:
White pepper crab is very good !! All the dishes are super fresh and tasty.

We called to reserve. Restaurant is quite popular.  And asked the restaurant to reserve a nice crab for us.  Supper good !!!

author: Hanh Hoang
review_text:
I visited the restaurant a bit after 10 PM. It was still quite busy but luckily no wait for a table. The crowd was a mix of tourists and locals. The interior is decorated with numerous photos of the owner/head chef posing with customers, giving the place a personal touch.

I tried two of their bestsellers – the white pepper crab and the meehoon. The crab was flavorful, though the seasoning was too strong for my taste. The meehoon, on the other hand, was delicious.

In terms of price, it’s on the higher side – around $10 per 100 grams, comparable to Jumbo Seafood, though the ambience here isn’t quite as upscale.

author: nads
review_text:
food is alright, expensive for what it is but alright in general and enjoyable.

the fried beehoon is the star of the show that my table ended up ordering 2 more portions, the pork is good too and the salted egg sotong was alright only

minus one star for their yam paste / orh ni , the yam had a hard inner layer that was not edible like it has been prepared and left for very long, then reheated and served to us. there were quite a fair bit of corn as well so it mostly taste like corn instead of yam

wont recommend the yam paste.

author: Leia H
review_text:
The JB San Lou Bee Hoon is a disappointment, soggy and not nicely pan fried at all. It was not authentic, (if you tried it in JB you would know)The sambal that accompanied was extremely salty.

Other than that their sweet sour pork, stir fried vegetables, boiled prawns are delicious.

author: Amos Lau 立辉
review_text:
Food was really yummy 😋 worth the time and waiting for food 👍🏻

A bit warm despite the night meal out with friend group, one of more senior lady didn't seem as trained, she had trouble taking our landscape, vertical photos and brought us a wrong dish....the seating was cramp especially if you sit at the edge of the round table, hence I recommend 3-4ppl or else, get 2 tables.
Besides that, I had a good time with my friend group

author: Supapat W
review_text: Their bee hoon is a must that it has crispy edges, packed with wok hei. Loved the fried pork and the silky eggplant. The salted egg shrimp was rich, creamy, and addictive. Always crowded, but worth the wait. Classic late-night zi char spot in SG!!

author: jessica bizzoni
review_text: Came for their signature white pepper crab but sadly it was sold out. Luckily, their signature bee hoon and clams did not disappoint — both were delicious! The crayfish was decent, though not as memorable. Be sure to pre-order the crab if you’re planning to go!

author: Chewielicious T
review_text: Came here as 2 people and just ordered the large bee hoon and salted egg prawn ball. Portions were good and both dishes hit the spot — tummy is happy!

author: Yoana Kurnadi
review_text: Went there for the fried beehoon, very crispy and nicely done. Unfortunately the cereal prawn is not great, though it looks nice and smell nice. The creal got nice crunch but prawns got no taste.

author: Hana
review_text: We ordered the famous san lou mee hon, deep fried pork belly, and of course, white pepper crab. All for 2 people T_T lol our total bill was 111sgd but every penny was worth it. Thanks to Gordon Ramsay for such a fine recommendation. We went here around 6pm, there are still a few tables available outside. You can call them to reserve a table inside. Staff are friendly. They have clean restroom, too. Restaurant's very accessible. There's bus stop nearby. Can't wait to go back here and order their pork belly and bee hon again (crab's expensive lol)

author: Bee Sun Ng
review_text:
The signature white pepper crab was wholesomely good; meaty and filled with crab roe! This came as a surprise as we ordered the smaller crab for 2 pax.
The other dishes were also delicious, flavourful!
The staff were very helpful and friendly, ready to meet our needs so that we can enjoy our dinner.

author: Taiji Master
review_text: Used to love the San Lou beehoon here – still decent, but the flavour is noticeably less rich now. The lala remains as fresh and tasty as ever. Unfortunately, the kang kong was a letdown – extremely dry and lacking in sauce. Overheard staff mention it was done this way to make it look better for photos, but honestly, taste should come first.

author: Merryheart
review_text:
Tucked away in two modest shop houses along the ever-buzzing Geylang stretch, JB Ah Meng doesn't look like much from the outside-but come evening, it's packed to the brim with hungry diners who know exactly what they're here for. This zi char joint has built a loyal following, thanks to its menu of over 30 classic Johor Bahru-style dishes.
If you're familiar with Malaysian style zi char, you'll likely spot your favourites right away. And while some dishes hit the mark more than others, there are a few standouts worth mentioning.
The famed JB San Lou Beehoon came out as expected-pressed flat and crisped up on both sides, delivering that signature wok hei. Though satisfying, it didn't quite match up to the authentic JB version. The sambal kang kong, however, was a solid hit-spicy, crunchy, and perfectly balanced.
Prawn rolls were decent but unmemorable. A surprising highlight was the fried spicy lala, which packed a punch and had us reaching for more.

In short, JB Ah Meng makes a strong case for those craving a zi char fix without making the trip across the Causeway. It's not quite a JB clone, but for a night out in Singapore with friends over comforting, wok-kissed dishes-it's a worthy contender.

author: Alvin Choo
review_text:
I was recommended to try this place years ago during covid, and recently, someone recommended the place to me again. I decided to make a reservation for Sunday to go down. Please take note that if you want to call in to make a reservation, you would either have to call before they start business at 5pm or call at 11+pm like I did.

We got quite a few dishes, their signature bee hoon, white pepper crab, dragon chives, fermented pork belly, salted egg prawn balls and stir fried clams.

I came with rather higher expectations but most of the dishes were quite normal and nothing delightful. I liked the sauce from the white pepper crab but there was too little to enjoy it.

author: Shiela Kim
review_text:
If you’re looking for a no-frills, authentic Singaporean zi char experience, JB Ah Meng is a must-visit. Tucked away in the heart of Geylang, this casual eatery is beloved by locals, foodies, and even Michelin-star chefs — and for good reason.

The White Pepper Crab is the star of the show. Unlike the more commonly found black pepper or chili versions, this dish stands out for its intense aroma, fiery white pepper kick, and juicy, perfectly cooked crab. It’s spicy but addictive — a dish you’ll crave long after the meal ends. But I highly suggest booking an appointment to avoid waiting time.

author: hels
review_text: 10/10 an authentic, humble Filipino food place that reminded me of home:) food was impeccable (and under $30!?). Ordered the chicken sisig and inasal which both came with rice. The portions were very generous and perfect for sharing. Came in the evening and most of the karinderia food was gone, unfortunately, but a good excuse to come back for more. The 10/10 Milo, gulaman was good too. Food came out extremely fast, overall very good vibes, literally wanted to go back the next day.

author: Fiyah Faith
review_text:
My first time trying authentic halal filipino food with colleagues. We bought the boodlefight set 2 and everything was so yummy. Their egg had onion and eggplant which was a surprising mix. The chicken was barbecued with the sweet sauce. We also had a side of liang which was a yam paste. The staff were friendly and while the indoor space was small, we were seated more spaciously at the sheltered outdoors. The location had a mushollah/prayer room which was a nice addition.

The only feedback I would give is, there is a reasonable waiting time for the food preparation so if you are in a hurry, you should eat elsewhere.

author: C T
review_text:
It’s rare to find halal Filipino food in Singapore, so this place is a gem!
I loved the Chicken Sisig—definitely a must-try. The Chicken Inasal and Oxtail Soup were also really good. I appreciated the localized Halo-Halo—it’s less sweet than the traditional Filipino version, which suits my taste better. The Turon (fried banana) was another favorite!

The only downside is the ambience—it can get quite warm as there’s no air-conditioning.

author: pokemon phua
review_text:
Food is average at best
but the appalling thing is definitely the price. Nested in ubi, you would have never thought that prices here would be steep. For reference, chicken rice here cost $3.50, while a plate of sambal fried rice cost $5. However, being the only nasi padang stall here has allowed them to monopolize the market and become very complacent with the prices. I bought 1 meat, one sambal goreng and one begedil only to be charged $7.35! Totally unacceptable as this is similar to CBD pricing. Been to many neighbourhood nasi padang stalls and i dare say this is BY FAR the MOST EXPENSIVE nasi padang. Go at your very own risk but you are sure to break the bank. 💸💸💸(Maybe thats why they are right beside the ATM haha)

Portion size: FRIGGIN LITTLE they expect to feed an adult with this is shocking like the rice and the sambal goreng is so pathetic

Quality: CHICKEN IS NOT COOKED. Please see the attached picture. ITS STILL RAW!!! Had to air fry it again myself….

author: KhaiDougie Tomlinson
review_text:
Absolutely unforgettable! From the moment we walked into the restaurant we knew we were in for a treat. The ambiance was so inviting, the staff and owner were incredibly attentive, and top notch service and the food was simply divine.

Despite Fasting month, and they have to attend orders, they still prioritise the people who are fasting.👍👍
This place is a gem and good service.
The female owner deserve credits!
Power la.

author: emz
review_text: As a filipino... the food here is really mid... ESPECIALLY for what they're priced at... the halohalo wasn't sweet enough and the ice had already melted the moment it arrived? area is really humid unless u're fortunate enough to sit next to the fan... the condiments aren't refilled... but the staff were very nice!! just not good food...

author: nyaw kyungji
review_text: A lovely and friendly couple serving authentic Philippine halal food. Generous portions and a hearty meal — a great way to start your day!

author: Mark Justine Segovia
review_text: My Filipino food cravings were truly satisfied! The food here is excellent, and the staff are very friendly and accommodating. I thoroughly enjoyed their authentic Filipino dishes. I highly recommend Nanay’s Kitchen if you’re craving delicious Filipino food 💯💯

author: Patrick Adrian Trinidad
review_text:
I've have come from Philippines to work in a foreign country, and I can say I missed the local dishes, my friends, and the culture. Longing for something from Home, I looked in Google and stumbled upon this kitchen, it's a mix of Philippine/Malay Food, I felt welcomed. I've been eating here since Last July 2024, and I have never missed a month. I make sure to visit once a month and I am delighted to eat every time the same thing, my favorite food is Sizzling Sisig, previously I only preferred to eat without Chili Peppers since I couldn't take spicy food, however as time passes by I have started to like them, I plan to try to bring my colleagues however its very far from my office its 15-20 minutes' walk. I'm very happy for making friends with the people here since I can preorder my meal since it has to be newly cooked and when I arrive its already prepared! I'm very happy and will be back for more Sizzling Sisig with 2 Rice each time! don't worry there is a cheaper option since the meals differ from each other!

Sizzling Sisig is 11 SGD with 1 Rice
Add 1 more Rice 1 SGD
(Drink 1-2SGD)

Total 12 SGD.

author: Timothy Teo
review_text: Rare Filipino Halal place. They also serve local Malay dishes like Mee Goreng and Nasi Lemak. Definite must try dessert is the Halo-halo, similar to local Ice Chang but sweeter and more ingredients like leche flan.

author: Angelica Ferrer
review_text: If you are looking for Authentic Filipino Food, Nanay’s Kitchen is definitely something that could satisfy your cravings and a go to place when youre thinking of something nice to eat at very affordable budget.

author: jayden
review_text:
Superb Phillipine and Malay cuisine in the neighbourhood, very much accessible via ubi downtown line.
The oxtail bulalo is delicious and has the strong bony taste of oxtail, the soup is not over flavourful or overpowering kind, it's just the right taste which will warms up your stomach especially on a cold day. It's pretty good to go with rice especially if you add some lime into it and their special homemade sambal which is good too(note that their sambal has this unique taste of which is not spicy however still has the sambal taste to it). They do also have chilli padi and lime condiments which you can add as you wish.
The nasi lemak rice is fragrance and soft, the chicken is crispy however the nasi lemak chilli is not those of sambal or spicy, it's sweet thus might not be the kind of chilli which we locally love on the traditional nasi lemak. However just ask for the homemade sambal instead and you are good to go! The curry vegetable is also nice even though it's lukewarm which usually I would dislike or feel turn off, however it's still pretty awesome and this is one of the few lukewarm currys which I still will give it a thumbs up.
However the place has many mosquitoes, me and my friend was being bitten a few times there, the outside seats tables are also not that clean and prone to crows which are eating the leftovers from diners which have left, might be good if the staff could clear the plates or set a rule for diners to clear the plates to avoid crows hovering over the leftover food which is quite unhygienic for the rest of the diners still eating near the tables.

author: Regiena M
review_text: This is my second time having Boodle Fight in less than a week and the food experience was superb. The star dishes are sizzling chicken sisig, grilled sotong, fried milkfish, chicken bbq and chicken skin. The food is well seasoned,  delicious and appetizing! My family and friends enjoyed the food experience and has positive feedback as well. Come and try the authentic Filipino halal dishes. Next time I visit Nanay’s Kitchen I will try their nasi padang dishes.

author: Rochelle (OchieBon)
review_text: So accessible via Ubi MRT, if you are craving for Halal Filipino Malay food, this place is for u! Nanay's Kitchen means Mother's Kitchen in English and you can really expect homecooked filipino dishes that is sprinkle with mother's love no wonder why the food here is soo delicious plus with great quality & yet very affordable!!! Even the drinks, a lot to choose from even teh-c and the kopi-c plus the bandung and limau C my gosh i live this kind of drink while enjoying my Pinoy Food! Make sure to try their bbq!!! the best! from the beef hotdog, beef skewers (so soft!!!), chicken feet, and the boodle fight (eating on a long table with bare hands) was the ultimate feast! the milkfish, tilapia, pansit super wow, grilled chicken etc on top of the rice was really a show stopper!! Dont worry the food is not salty at all plus the desserts not too sweet thats why i enjoyed everything! must try mais con yelo with yema goodness in evey bite! Oh they have karaoke!! Bulalo and tocino was a hit too! Worth visiting this place i promise u! check them out at Outram too!

author: shiela lim de leon
review_text: Food that is close to home! the dishes are savory and delectable. Dessert is refreshing and sweet!

author: aisyah
review_text: Second time dining here, it's a wonderful place to dine in, they sell a wide variety so there's something for everyone. Their food is excellent, drinks and desserts are also delicious. The staff here are extremely friendly, good vibes all around. The person in charge is very welcoming and makes the experience wholesome.There's a musollah here too, definitely a plus. Will definitely be returning here again!

author: Kenna
review_text: Very nice food and ambience. Authentic filipino food! I would definitely go back here. Me and my friends really enjoy the feast!

author: SH
review_text: Delicious food served! Must try their fried banana roll! Kept dreaming about it. Their rice portions were big for us, can consider sharing if small eaters. Do take note the hotplate comes with a serving of rice as well. Felt like mum's homecooked food.

author: Jeremy Teng
review_text:
Went after watching the feature on TSL. Really doesn't disappoint, very affordable and good selection.

Had the lamb and it wasn't too gamy, and the eggplant egg is good! The fish that I ordered was yummyyyyy. Make sure to order halo halo as well!! Sinful and good

author: Maryann Alvarado
review_text:
Halal filipino food just stone throw from ubi mrt.
I got the sagot gulaman, but it's very sweet, one sip, and I feel I'll have diabetes.
The sisig with rice is just okay. The chicken sisig has a lot of onion compared to the meat.
