Partner likes it, though, but I hope the meat will be more than onion. I'll come back, though, to try other food.

author: Boon Leong
review_text:
Located in the industrial area accessible by car 🚗
Went on Sat evening &with a few tables occupied
The ingredients are stored in the refrigerator with a fixed price based on the color plates.
Chose the plates & paid at the cashier.
The clayport of lala are placed on the charcoal stove.
The place is stuffy after a while enjoying.
For 3paxs it cost ard $80
Prob find the prices on the higher side.

author: Escilpe
review_text: We came on a Sunday evening and didn’t get a crowd. Food is great and the lala claypot soup taste delicious. You order the soup and the hotpot adds on ( beef, fish slice , luncheon meat and vegetables etc) Kids love the food. Family of 5 and costing below a $100.

author: Sammy Soong
review_text: Ubi Claypot Lala – Generous Portions, but Hygiene Needs Improvement - At Ubi Claypot Lala serves their dishes over a charcoal stove with a generous portion of lala (clams), giving it a nice, smoky aroma. However, food hygiene seems to need better attention — the fridge doesn’t feel sufficiently cold, and the vegetables weren’t very fresh during my visit. While the concept and portion are good, proper food storage and freshness should be improved to match the quality of the dish.

author: Currie Pok
review_text: Lovely find in the area. Best food on a rainy day. Owner was attentive and filled up soup for us. He said he selected the lala himself daily. We didn’t opt to add any steamboat sides into the soup as we wanted the original taste.

author: samlivestoeat
review_text:
Comforting and satisfying meal! We can choose from a wide variety of fresh ingredients to complement the flavourful lala soup! My personal favourites are tiger prawn, shabu shabu beef, scallop, fish slice, chicken slice, burst ball and shiitake.

📣Check out my IG/Lemon8/Tiktok @samlivestoeat for more detailed foodie reviews! 🥰

author: Damian Koh
review_text: I can imagine this to be amazing if it was a cool rainy evening. It's pretty much self service here. First you notify the staff of your table number, then pick out the ingredients you want in the fridge and pay for it at the counter. Then you wait for them to bring the claypot to you. Soup was rich with a reasonable amount of garlic, which I love. It does get quite heavy after boiling for some time so you can get free soup refills. Ingredients are fresh and go well with the soup.

author: Jack
review_text: Saw on TikTok and decided to pay a visit. The lala broth is pretty good but feels like the clams are rather small and the shells took up a lot of space in the small pot. The ingredients are fairly fresh and also fairly priced. Beef slices are fatty perfect for hotpot. The prawn paste was also very fresh. Broth is refillable self service so it's good. The environment can be rather stuffy with the hot fire and smoke sometimes get in your face. Maybe sitting in the open will be better. We paid $75 for 2 adults and 1 kid which is alright I think.

author: Wing Chan
review_text:
Heard about this Lala hot pot and tried it for dinner. Ordered the large hotpot and portion is reasonable.  Lala hotpot is delicious and it's a fusion of Lala and steamboat. Service from kevin is excellent,  he came over to check on the food and dinning experience from time to time and ensure everything is good. I like the idea of the fusion and the food is good.
Parking could be a problem,  be sure to be there early.

author: Victoria
review_text: The lala soup is super nice and affordable. The lala clay pot is selling at $13.80. Then you can choose all the fresh ingredients inside the fridge. Come on weekdays not so crowded. Weekend will be packed and sold out fast. I can just come here for the soup. Super hearty for a rainy day or any day. Haha

author: Sook Mei Cheong
review_text:
Love their fresh lala and umami broth. Sincere, hardworking folks serving great food. You can take your pick of ingredients to add on. I went with family on Friday evening for dinner.

Non air cond and very local environment.

There's a western food stall "Hot potato" that serves delicious fare. Gave us some French fries to try for free. Nice boss!

author: Marcus Chan
review_text:
Very good supper place for a Saturday night, the crowd was not overwhelm. Quite a lot of empty parking space by the road.

The lala soup was good & clams were fresh, ingredients such as the Shabu pork, prawn paste & beef were good & decently priced. The soup base & huadiao jiu is refillable and no msg I think, as we didn’t feel thirsty thereafter or even next day.

Only downside is the overall cleanliness of the coffeeshop can see quite a few small roaches here and there, not the stall, the stall is clean.

Will still visit there again hope the overall coffeeshop management do something about it

author: Chua Yixun
review_text: Warning this place is a no go, hdl prices for lesser portions. Base price of 21.8, with coloured plate pricing, some stuff are priced at ridiculous price, like in the picture, green plates at 6.9 is crazy

author: DS Gno
review_text: Came here cause of the reviews..Ordered lala hotpot here… 10min become like BCM and taste bad. The shabu shabu taste 50% like chewing gum, 50% like rotten meat.

author: Andrea Chua
review_text: Soup is very sweet and fragrant after all the lala are cooked. We dig in immediately the lala is cook. We did not even managed to take any pics only at a later part for this review. I definitely will come again.

author: King
review_text:
So many bad reviews, and so many good reviews, therefore I come to take a look.
Order time and service time is that that long, it is reasonable. Unlike many bad reviews that wait long time and no food left.
The lala pot is reasonable price, but the fish dumplings definitely is at the high price that 5 pcs for $6.9. If I want to standardize for $6.9, it can be 6 pcs or 8 pcs , because every pcs is quite small .
The soup added too much MSG, because I can easily tell when my heart beats go too high.
Overall, can try la.

author: Esther Khoo
review_text: The clay pot la la is very fresh, very delicious. the soup base was also really nice. soup refill and sauces and cooking wine all self service and provided. there's a variety of other ingredients to choose from ranging from different kinds of meats, dumplings, meat balls to vegetables. it is also possible to add more lala was $5.80 for 250g. the clay pot is over charcoal which cooks lala perfectly. only downside that we experienced was that the food too quite awhile to come. other than that, went around 5.30pm so no queue really and food was really good.

author: Irene Chung
review_text: 1st time visiting this place, the place is just next to the Ubi Driving school.  Arrived around  6.30pm, less crowded. Lala soup based is tasty, not to forget to add the 花雕酒 to enhanced the flavor and more tasty and its refillable! Price is reasonable too. Recommend to be seated outdoor and it’s quite hot seated inside.

author: classical9034
review_text:
I order a small pot but surprisingly the serving of the lala is quite a lot. The soup is very rich and tasty.

I am impressed with the prawn size which is quite big and fresh.

The sauce selection is limited but good enough for a simple hot pot.

The place I sit has some housefly with no fan. It becomes very hot and humid as we are eating. The overall environment could be better for a more enjoyable dining experience.

author: Agnes “ManKiller” Sem
review_text: First time here to try out this lala pot. I would prefer if their fried garlic is freshly made instead, that will level up the soup though. If they fried the lapa on the spot will be great but i heard from one coffeeshop lala pot boss told me in sg not allow to stir fry on the spot in public, i am unsure abt the rules .

author: Darren Loo
review_text:
Went on a weekend early evening before 6PM, not much queue, so it is recommended to visit during this period as it will get relatively packed, and the time your pot gets ready is long after 8PM. It's very stuffy if you are sitting indoors, so do find a seat outdoors.

Food quality was fairly decent, but the additional ingredients were pricey around $6.90 or $9.90 each, depending on the color. The lala soup base is more on the milky side compared to the other known lala stores. It is strongly recommended to order the large pot as even for two individuals, the amount of lala felt rather little. Price is reasonable for the large at $22.90.

author: Thomas Saw
review_text:
This neighborhood has good mix of old & new HDB estate and MRT entrance is nearby 10 min walking distance.

The Mee Siam ($4)from Hup Hup stall is good as recommended & the soup not sour like muslin type but alittle sweetness toward Nonya. The mee hoon is well cooked with evenly mee siam powder color & the tao por is cut edible piece size, unlike other stalls cut small pieces.

In the same roll stalls at corner has fried carrot cake stall 333. They sell white, black or mix ($4.5) carrots cake and may take awhile to cook. The white carrot cake taste like old school style and has little egg in it, but the black carrot cake taste better.

author: L Chan
review_text: Nice, clean & airy place. Ground floor has provision shops & wet market. Upstairs food centre serves a good mix of familiar hawker dishes. 2 passenger lifts makes it easy to get around.

author: Jason Ng
review_text:
[MATTAR, SINGAPORE] Don't remember the Circuit Road Hawker Centre being so crowded at night, but there were so many dishes I wanted to try 😍 among all of them we had 3 that caught our eye:

The Fried Prawn Mee from Tian Seng was like a roller coaster ride; I was shocked & disappointed at the start when I saw that the bigger $5 portion was so small... But once I tried it I fell in love 😍 the umami prawn & garlic flavour was so intense, and the noodles were cooked just right! Although the wok hei might be slightly lacking, but such intense prawn flavour is really hard to find. This might be one of my top 5!

I've had oyster omelette ($5) from Ghim Guan quite a few times, and the standard remains high. This rendition is wetter than others, but rich in flavours. I love how eggy this whole dish tastes and that the oysters were plump and juicy!

Lastly, the Claypot Chicken Rice ($7) from Nanxing was just decent, felt like there was nothing much to say about the rice. The chicken was very tender and fresh though!

Such a nice place for dinner, with quite a huge variety of stalls to choose from! I think this is a lesser known hawker which you should try visiting 😍

author: Everhart
review_text:
Stopped by here for a quick Kopi C. It was pretty spacious, with the first level as a market and the second level as the food centre. There was plentiful of seats, which can accommodate various group sizes.

There is a plethora of food options for you, as well as drinks. A good place for uou and your family or friends to drop by here for lunch!

author: Yi Ling
review_text:
I honestly love this hawker centre so much, and it hits my old soul in the most nostalgic punch.

Though there aren't many food options in the 2nd level, this place is bustling with elderly and 1st and 2nd gen hawkers. You really don't get to see this very often anymore.

Most of the patrons here are the elderly and prices are pretty much catered to them as well with smaller portions and price point.

Facilities wise, there are:
✅️ Great ventilation with multiple ceiling fans and big head room space
✅️ Clean toilets with soap
✅️ Wet market at level 1

author: Terence Ho
review_text: Was there for lunch with a customer and many of the stalls were not open. Tried the fried prawn noodle. Its ok just that the prawn and ingredients were only added onto the noodles after the noodles are cooked. So the ingredients are actually cold. Would be better if they cook the ingredients together with the noodles

author: Samuel1992 California
review_text: Everywhere the place are still in old fashioned and the toilet, locations and corridor have a small gap, MP in charge please wake up your idea. Got money and never closed down the coffeeshop for 1 month and replace the toilet from squat to seat toilet. What the heck and the people needs to have their mindset fixed. At least the carpark got the under shelter and other places like traffic light needs a high shelter. Please get LTA to investigate the location to replace the toilet

author: Rachel
review_text: Hup Hup Mee Siam (#02-14) is a must-try! The laksa and orh nee are both fantastic. The orh nee is so authentic (I steamed at home), and their laksa is even featured on Malaysia Airlines. Really delicious!

author: Lockheart
review_text: Most stalls close by late afternoon so go in the morning if youre looking for variety. Sugar cane juice was refreshing for hot weather.

author: Yoke Lan Sun
review_text:
All these good food for just SGD33!
Gem of a find in this day and age!

author: Jenny Sin
review_text: The hawker is at the 2nd floor, thanks that no flying birds inside and it is clean. It is a morning open hawker, start at 5am+, one of the stall laksa end at 10am so early. Surprisingly still can find $2.50 food at this hawker, happy. The food is nice, handmade and cheap, worth to try :) I first time bought so big chau siew bao x2, and price is cheap!

author: Ken Loy
review_text:
This is a very old hawker centre.
Been there for more than 50 years but recently renovated with a new parking scheme in place.

Only some of the original stalls have remained. These ones have been there for the longest time. One example will be the prawn 🦐 noodle stall operated by the 2 sisters. Must try...

Overall food quality is pretty standard. No standouts.

author: Tan Junyu
review_text: This food centre is known for vegeterian food and quite quiet but when you walk over to 79A food centre, you can spot this long snaking queuing for Yong Lai Fa Ji Shu Shi fish soup. Queue move quite fast. Batang Fish is silky soft, fish skin is removed. Fried fish is tasty, deep fried using batang fish and not the usual dory fish. Broth is clear and light flavour. Chilli with douchi is complement with the fish soup well. Pig organ soup from heng heng was equally good as well. Liver, pig stomach, sliced pork were tender. Broth is slight peppery with some salted veg. 😋😋😋

author: Cat P
review_text:
One of the oldest hawker centres in the East offering a plethora of local fares.

Opens early in the morning to provide the office dwellers with breakfast and last all the way past midnight with amazing supper choices.

Conveniently located next to Mattar mrt and serviced by over 10 different buses from all corners of Singapore.

author: J Seng
review_text: Small hawker center on second floor. Notable stalls are fried carrot cake, nasi lemak, bak chor mee, kopi etc. Look for stalls with long queue for popular food items.

author: Papa Lim
review_text:
Good food like intestine soup & chicken wings.

Crispy skin bbq wings

But majority of e food stalls (9 stalls) sell vegetarian. So if u are big fan, this is a must go place.

author: Chew LìYǎ
review_text:
Too bad 02-10 Minced pork noodle 🍜 is Off today, Tue, 02 January 2024.
So try besides Niang Tofu. Average on scale.

Majority operate in the morning and Close by around noon

author: Brandon Yap
review_text: Very good food, when I used to live there my mom used to mostly go there to buy stuff to eat. Very nice food.

author: K C
review_text: Great place for nice food. Especially Gan's Yong Tou Foo which I always support. Of course there's also other great food to try out too.

author: TCH
review_text:
This morning I came to try this stall after a strong recommendation from a friend.

Very old school taste of fried Bee Hoon Mee.  Added Chicken Wing and Taukua.  The chicken wing was well marinated tasted awesomely delicious.

Worth the queue and I am told usually by 9am they are done and close for the day!

author: Hatsune Miku
review_text: MacPherson Market & Food centre offers food that start off at lower prices that seems to cater more to the eldery. Lower prices here also translate to smaller portions. Food served here is slightly below average and you won't find anything stellar here. The only stall worth mentioning here is the vegetarian stall that serves vegetarian food at affordable prices. You will be hard-pressed to find vegetarian bee hoon at $3.50. Portions of vegetarian bee hoon are also generous, and this is one of the stalls I frequent often. Another stall worth mentioning is the yong tau foo stall that also sells laksa and char kway teow. Personally, I rather enjoyed their laksa yong tau foo and I feel that this is a hidden gem.  Whatever the case, the food here will not blow you away. There are a few stalls here, but there is still a good variety of food options. This place is good if you want to spend a little less on your meals.

author: MC Teh
review_text:
This is an old hawker center.
There is a lot of hidden gems of good and cheap foods. However not all foods store are open every days.

author: don Toh
review_text: Very small hawker center next to a wet market. Opening till afternoon, hence mainly morning crowd.

author: Zenobia Loh
review_text: Can remember the individual stalls but the food here generally quite yummy one. Will come back again to try the other stuff. Best is if you can come in a group so can try more items. Lots of parking spaces and a lot of seats. But most of the seats quite dirty so i guess thats the only bad thing. Also if you walk pass the toilet its DAMN SMELLY so i suggest you empty your bladder first before coming.

author: susan chow
review_text: Had lunch at No :01-95 Laksa Yong Tau Foo & Char Kway Teow. Food is deliciously good and lots of crispy pork crackers ontop wok hei char kway teow. Indeed a worthwile meal.

author: Pak Soon Lau
review_text: Nice small market and food centre serving the local residents adequately. There's a stall selling very reasonably priced Yong tau foo (uncooked) here. Most of the stall holders are elderly and quite a few stalls are left vacant. Hopefully this estate will see some rejuvenation and more young families.

author: L Chan
review_text: It’s very much a morning place. Many of the hawker stalls cater to the breakfast & early lunch crowd & it tends to quiet down significantly by mid-afternoon. By evening, the whole place winds down & feels almost deserted.

author: Kim Kimora
review_text: The chicken rice is marvelous. Must give it a try. But must come before 2pm. They close around 2 pm and we were lucky to get two more places before they close.

author: Hikigaya Hachiman
review_text:
Nested and Hidden away from those who aren't local to MacPherson. After walking around Circuit Road I managed to find this hawker centre.

I came the following week in the morning (as it closes early afternoon) I had the Black Carrot Cake (Facing the Provision shops), Porridge and Soya Bean. I had spent a total of 7 dollar for this. Hawker prices kept low , this is really a rare find in sg with everything getting more expensive.

My favourite is the Black Carrot Cake being a 8/10, good amount of egg, nice texture with the garlic and Radish along with the sweet and just enough sweet sauce.

The porridge was a little of a miss, 6/10 , on the mild side , I imagine their audience being older folks who wouldn't want too salty. They have porridges around 2.80 and you can add on Ingredients found in like economical BEEHOON stalls.

The 1 dollar Soya Bean was amazing for me , so cheap! Definitely give them a try when you are here. Nothing beats morning with coffee or Soya Bean.

I hope to come here in the future , as it seems popular with their Prawn Noodles , Wanton Mee and Laksa.

author: Elvina Heng
review_text: A lot of shop changes . So long . Recommend a white and roasted chicken rice . I order no 2 . $3.50 .

author: Eric Tan
review_text: Comforting local favourites in the heart of Circuit Road. Wantan mee was delicious.

author: Steven Chiu
review_text: Really a hidden gem with seniors getting up at early as 330am to be there. It was already crowded at 5am!

author: Elynn -
review_text: thick and rich coconut gravy topped with tau pok, slices of fish cake and cockles. comfort food.

author: C.S
review_text: Most stalls are not open even during lunch time. Variety is limited too. Avg small hawker.

author: Yong Hee Chan
review_text: A place that offers food of my liking, be it laksa, prawn mee, carrot cake, roti prata. I mostly patronised the carrot cake and prawn mee, the carrot cake, at $3.50/packet is not only cheap but very well cooked. Prawn mee, a very popular stall where ingredients vanished is one goes after 9.30am, is another generous stall, with the food very much in my favour. There are many other stalls, making choices difficult. Highly recommended place, cheap and delicious food!!!!

author: Dennis Cheong
review_text: Have not visited since COVID. Market was renovated and feels better. It is main5a breakfast/lunch market/hawker centre

author: neo l c
review_text:
Authentic Laksa and New Char kua too stall are available.. Reasonably cheap
Worth trying only available morning till noon

author: Yeo Heng Choon
review_text: Just find back old time feeling eating at the market. Really nice and economic prawn noodles.

author: Sung Long
review_text: The newly renovated MacPherson Market & Food Centre is very much cleaner with new floorings, fittings and seatings. The price and quality of foods are reasonable and good. All these give patrons and a more pleasant and delightful experience.

author: Otoko Otoko
review_text: Long queue for this chicken rice stall. Just $3 for a decent sized plate of Hainanese Chicken Rice

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Eileen
review_text: I went with a group of colleagues as our plan was lunch at old Airport road end up market was closed for washing. I feel disgusting after I finish my meal and I witness this myself. 1st soup was diluted, meat not so tasty, the salted vegetables taste horrible too and totally tasted different and not as good as previous stall we have at Jalan Besar. After our meal, I'm shocked to see the stall helper digging his nose and worst is after doing that he didn't wash his hand! Less then 5min, he went to smoke 🚬 at the walk way and came back to the stall didn't wash the hand and proceed back to cook for the customer who ordered. Omg! Never in my life, I will go back again! This is super disgusting and horrible unhygienic! Hopefully, SFA can visit and access the stall! I seldom give such review and would said this is the 1st time I see such thing! Regret having meal there!

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Mr Wang Wang
review_text: Despite the vendor's notably brusque demeanor, this stall earns its reputation through impeccably cleaned pig organ soup. The offal—whether liver, intestine, or stomach—arrives without a trace of that gamey aftertaste that plagues lesser versions, a testament to rigorous washing that borders on artisanal. Where they falter is portion control: servings lean modest, making the automatic inclusion of meatballs and three-layered pork feel like filler rather than value. Truthfully, I’d prefer an organs-only option to savor their star ingredient undiluted. Come prepared for old-school transaction rules—cash is king here, with digital payments firmly off the menu.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Jayon See
review_text:
One of the famous Pork Organ Soup in the area.
Ingredients were fresh, the portion is pretty big for its price as well.
However, the soup has a bit of porky smell, and their Kiam Chai (Pickled Veggies) is not tasty.
To me it’s just average, plus the uncle is pretty sarcastic toward his other customers, not really friendly.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: MrJayquak
review_text:
Nice portion for SGD 5.50
Add 50c for a bowl of rice
Chill sauce is spot on, suitable for most taste buds. The salted vege is strong, so its suitable for those prefer their soup on the salty side of things.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Wei L
review_text: Went at night and everything was bad. Pork, pig liver, pig stomach, etc were all v hard. Soup was bland, sauce was bland and so was Chilli. Only good thing was the store owners' ' good attitude.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Rayne
review_text:
Decent big bowl of pig's organ soup.
I like the braised intestine but the soup is not as flavourful as compared to the one at Foch road.
We went at night for dinner so not much crowd.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: John Tango
review_text:
Decent service. Good price value. Taste overal for the mix pork soup with white rice is 7.5/10. Tau kwa (soya bean curd) too salty 6/10. Tau pok (spongy soya bean) 7/10.

The pork ball & pig’s stomach are tasty. Pork slices a little tough.

A repeat? Yes.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Mike Ang
review_text: They are good for the pig mix soup, but maybe can consider give up selling this pork leg ? It will bring up the review instead.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Tan Lai Heng
review_text: The soup was savoury and nice. But a little on the salty side. Best to drink when it is on its hottest. The meat is a bit hard. Seating is aplenty here but if you are driving here, parking space is limited and you sometimes have to eait for spaces.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Connie Lim
review_text: Went here today to give a try, food was okay. But the service of a short, black hair uncle was super unfriendly. Understand that being a hawker is not an easy job, honestly, which job is easy? We’re not your scolding bag, as I couldn’t find the chili plate, the uncle could have say nicely instead of replying you cannot see? Walk over there and see yourself. I mean I am okay to walk over; but the tone seems like i own him a thousand bucks. Improve your service. Nobody’s job is easy. If I could rate the service, it will be ZERO!

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Goh Kheng Leng
review_text: The soup base is nice except the lean meat a bit tough to chew. The braised pork is nice not too salty.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Phylicia Lim
review_text: One of my favourite place for 猪杂汤. Price maybe on the pricier side for hawker but lots of ingredients. Recommended to try the 猪脚饭 too, very flavourful and meat is tender. Overall very tasty food. Service needs to be better though, ordered takeaway and doesn’t want to give extra chilli, ask me go refill with that small container myself, cannot just give me one more packet?!

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Chelsia Chan
review_text: Generous mixed organ soup! Value for money. Really a lot of ingredients, very generous. The salted veg is very tasty, adds on a tinge of sourness to cut through the meatiness porky taste.yummy

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Maverick Ng
review_text:
Horrible and arrogant attitude! The soup was also so bland and not nice at all.

A China National helper gave my mother a dirty dollar coin change, then my mother asked to change to a cleaner one, but he gave a even more dirtier one! Then a aged 60 plus big size uncle from the stall said my mother that you think my food are dirty, and my mother told him that I did not say your food was dirty. After that, he told my mother don't ever come and eat again! "Your soup was so bland and not nice at all!" My mother retorted.

FYI, they are already famous for being lousy and arrogant service attitude too!

* Never ever gonna patronise this stall! Even if you were to offer for free, I would not waste it but I would give it to a street dog or cat to eat.

If there is a 0 rating, you deserve it, I am very sure!

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Joe Goh
review_text: Nice old school pig's organ soup. Price slightly on the higher end at $6 for hawker prices.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Ezekiel Dixon Lim
review_text: Had a late lunch there so there wasn't any queue. Top notch no nonsense in-ya-face flavour. Can't go wrong if craving for some salty goodness!

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Shawn Tan
review_text: Standards have dropped. Braised dishes are ok. But the soup is not as flavourful, and has an unpleasant ‘pig’ taste. Would prefer to go to the other outlets.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Steven Neo
review_text: Not bad for Local Fovourite Pig Organs Soup. Kinda expensive though, 1 bowl of soup with all the various organs with rice, salted vegetables and Tofu at $6.

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: HeLiX Truong
review_text: Good taste, cheap price, but the seat have a little hot. You must take your seat first, remember the table number and then talk to cashier when you order

restaurant: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
author: Ryan
review_text: Standard bowl of pig organ soup, Ordered taukee on the side and wasnt given much. Chilli sauce that they give is not spicy. Overall just an average pig organ soup nothing special.

author: jimmy quek
review_text: Go for the food and old school atmosphere.... Lots of nice food.... Can't go wrong lah...

author: L Chan
review_text: Not a morning place - many stalls were still closed. The space feels stuffy, likely due to low ceilings & inactive exhausts, with fans just circulating the hot air from above.

author: Botak
review_text:
One of the older hawker centres, that serves reasonably priced food as this is an estate for senior citizens who probably are staying alone or are no longer working.

I found it interesting to be able to discover a TUTU kueh stall selling just that and muah chee,  which u don't see often since rent these days are high and such food are only found at night markets. There is even a char kway teow stall that serves the dish with a sunny side up egg on top. You can't miss the stall's name : 'dancing char kway teow'.

If u enjoy having your meals outside, there are options as seats can also be found outdoors for u to people-watch as well.

It is a nice place to reminisce and watch the world go by

author: Jay Tham
review_text:
Circuit Road Hawker Centre is a hidden gem with that old-school neighbourly vibe I absolutely love. We grabbed a seat outside, where the breeze was cool and uncles next to us were deep in beer, tea, and stories. It felt like stepping into a childhood memory.

But the food? Pure magic.

First up, the claypot rice — every grain smoky and fragrant, with lap cheong and salted fish adding bursts of savoury sweetness. That crispy rice at the bottom? Heavenly.

Then came a surprise: the fried egg with oyster, or orh luak — not your usual. The eggs were extra crispy, the oysters plump and fresh, and that rich gravy poured on top was next-level. A slight char in the flavour made it insanely addictive.

I accidentally ordered the dry bee hoon with fish, lala, and Napa cabbage, expecting soup — but what a win. The seafood was fresh and generous, and the sauce clung to every strand of vermicelli, bursting with ocean flavour. The Batang fish was thick, juicy, and rich.

And the fried Hokkien prawn mee? Absolutely divine. That deep prawn broth flavour, the perfect wok hei, and nostalgic taste hit all the right spots. It’s been ages since I had Hokkien mee this good.

Around us, the sound of clinking beer bottles and chatter made the food even better. Circuit Road isn’t just a hawker centre — it’s a flavour-packed escape.

author: C Y
review_text:
This hawker centre is loaded with a large variety of stalls selling different delicious cuisines at reasonable prices.

Sambal stingray, chicken chop, bbq chicken wings, nasi lemak, oyster omelette,  soya beancurd, satay, mixed veg rice, pig organ soup, duck rice, chendol, zichar, and many more! The only prominent food missing is roti prata.

author: J Seng
review_text: This hawker center offers an array of Singapore's local delights. From the comforting warmth of Claypot Rice to the vibrant variety of Zi Char dishes, each bite promises a burst of flavor. Savor the smoky char of Satays and BBQ Chicken Wings, or indulge in the rich, spicy Curry Rice. The Steamed Fish and Fish Soup are a testament to the freshness of local seafood, while Briyani and Thai Beef Noodle provide a hearty, aromatic experience. Not to be missed are the Pig Organs Soup and Char Kway Teow, each offering a unique taste of tradition. For those with a sweet tooth, the Traditional Desserts will surely satisfy. Every dish is a celebration of Singapore's culinary heritage.

author: Jace Lee
review_text: Good place for vegetarian food , local noodle stall , malay satay , western food , fried Hokkien mee , economical rice , local dessert store , steamed fish. All the stalls operate at different timing and start from 630am - 1130pm.

author: Zoe
review_text:
Western food beside fish soup stall located at the back after the toilet was bad and expensive , gave wrong order, ordered chicken chop, gave me chicken cutlet and the chicken cutlet was all bones and not much meat, I don’t recommend that western food stall.

The western food stall at the front is much better.

Overall hawker food at other stalls were good, I have visited the hawker almost everyday, that 1 star is for that western food stall

author: Randiano Tamelan
review_text: Circuit Road Hawker Center is the real deal for a chill food adventure. It's got the vibe, comfy seats, and a crazy mix of eats. From classic Hainanese chicken rice to fresh seafood, it's a flavor fiesta. The place stays clean, and the crew is on top of it. If you're into diverse, tasty bites without breaking the bank, this spot nails it. A lowkey gem for sure—Singapore street food at its finest! 🍜✨

author: Truth Fairy
review_text: Good vibes with funny standee. Claypot rice is the best here. Typical hawker vibes with relatively better and cheaper food. Duck rice is just 3 stars. Fried yong Tau foo not bad, smells very aromatic when it was cooked. May be jelat if you are eating one plate alone so suggest you share. Come around 1230pm but still have seats. Shops here open and close when ever they feel like it. But whether the food here is worth traveling for I don’t think so. But good to go if you are nearby.

author: Gerrich Behrendt
review_text: Best Hawker Center for vegetarians I have found so far! No idea why , but it has a high density of vegetarian stalls and they are great! Also get an iced kopi at the coffee and drinks stall , it's amazing!

author: Richard Soon Chai Lim
review_text: It's located in an old estate, and now that the downtown line Mattar MRT station is situated behind the Hawker Centre, which brings convenience for hawker food connoisseurs. There is a mix of stalls that caters to the breakfast and lunch crowds and those who cater for the dinner and supper crowd. It's a must for an experience to those who love Hawker Centre foods.

author: Daniel Ling
review_text: Food was great! Price was very reasonable. Steamed fish for $10 and sotong for $12. Will come again for more.

author: Daniel
review_text:
Laid back old school hawker centre with some good original hawker stalls.

Highly recommended for dinner. Lunch time, half of the stalls are closed.

author: clara lau
review_text: This hawker centre has 2 sections. Lots of  vegetarian food stalls here. Tried the vinegar pork leg. Nice ! There's also a big stall selling pig organ soup.

author: Jonathon Chua
review_text:
One of the few places with reasonable price but awesome food.

Highly recommended Hakka Yong Tou Fu which operates in early morning 530am to 9am. Handmade YTF each at $0.80 without minimum order. Add pork into your dry noodle.

Dancing Char Kway Teow, as the name goes. The chef stir fry your dish, he shake, rattle and roll. His own chilli recipe only at $4.50 with an egg.

Fish Ball Noodle. Good decent serving with newspaper interviews. One of my favourite too.

Dessert - end your lunch or dinner with dessert from here. Not too sweet, average price $1.80 - $2.00. Tau Suan my favourite.

author: R T
review_text:
I come here for my ban Mian fix.
So far I find the Hokkien mee and ban Mian nice. The rest is very average. So many vegetarian stalls. Chicken wings and satay right at the end (right side from the bridge).

Qiu xiang ban Mian is left side from bridge all the way to the end near the hardware shop at hdb. His mee Hoon kueh is damn yums!

Nearby Qiu xiang even has truffle fishball! Laksa from fishball noodle shop is not bad, fishball bouncy and no fishy smell!

author: Daniella Louise Santiago
review_text: Had a pretty good cheese paratha, and an even better mango aloe dessert while I waited for a bus back to my hotel. It’s conveniently on a busy bus stop.

author: CAi Zhenken
review_text:
The Fish soup sells one of the cheapest fish.

I ordered the seabass at $9.90/fish  and to my surprise it was the whole fish served. They drizzle some Hongkong style style sauce with coriander leafs and fried garlic and alas it was a very fulfilling dish.

Vegetables can be bought here at $6-$8/fish.

They have red chilli and lemon lime sauce for you to dip the fish in.

came ard 5.30pm on a weekday n hence waited jus 8 mins to tuck in.

portion is very big ,ard 4-500g/fish,recommend 2 pax to share 1 portion haha

author: Peter Lin
review_text: Kway Chap. Kway Chap stalls without a name always draws me to buy from them. This one near my hood is not super shiok compared to my previous hood but definitely passes well as a kway chap place.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Ding Heng Lee (harryldh)
review_text: The prawn broth is way too sweet with MSG taste. After eating can clearly feel my inner lips tearing. For prawns, regardless of small prawn or big prawns there were overcooked. Pork ribs are also filled with gaminess. Had the dry noodle with beehoon as recommended, no fragrance. Pork lard was gamy, fried shallots cannot be tasted without actually biting into it. Overall the noodles were badly seasoned. I’m really questioning how was the Michelin Bib Gourmand given on this. Ngiong hong however was decent, pass standard but definitely can’t compare with good ones in Penang.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Fatdieme
review_text:
Hands down one of the best prawn broth. It has everything you want: umami, prawn flavour, sweetness, savoury and pork lard+shallots. The colour of the soup is just 🔥🙏👌✨.

For the price, is really expensive but I can recommend the normal prawn noodles ($15), Jumbo prawns and other seafood isn't that special ($26-$30). Personally, I like it better when prawns are not cut in half for the qq texture.

The dry noodle portion is MASSIVE, thank goodness we can dabao the leftovers.

The hokkien mee is ok. If we never add the lime, easily I can forget how it taste like. Lime is ALWAYS good, must add. Even thou it looks saucey but the noodles absorbs fast and it becomes sticky. Still ok thou, will eat it.

Waiting time expect 30mins average.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Evon Tan
review_text:
🍜 Zhup Zhup hits the spot

Tried both the Jumbo and Supreme prawn noodles (dry and spicy). The noodles portions are generous and the soup is refillable. The prawns are sweet, broth is comforting, and everything feels nicely balanced.

Personally, I would go for the Supreme at $20 per bowl - more than good enough for me and great value. Comfort food cravings satisfied 😊

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Sheen Cher
review_text: Tried Zhup Zhup and totally get why it’s a Michelin Bib Gourmand favourite. The flavours are rich and comforting, and the GAOGAO broth is seriously addictive. We had the Jumbo Prawn Hokkien Mee and Jumbo Prawn Paofan — the tiger prawns were huge, sweet, and super satisfying. Also loved the har cheong gai and their refreshing drinks like the yuzu soda and ice lemon tea. Definitely worth a visit if you’re a prawn noodle fan!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Vivian Chu
review_text: Second time here. Prawn noodle tastes delicious and prawn biscuit is very fresh and crisp. Definitely we will come again.  First time, there was a staff, Indonesia woman, her service attitude was really bad , my friends said they wont come back. Second time,  served by two chinese women (one was cashier , another one helped us to order food) that service was good. 👍

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Joanne Lee
review_text:
Overhyped. Underwhelming.

Broth - failed. It looks thick but on taste, it’s the sugar type of sweetness which was building to a puke towards the end of the bowl. I go for umami meat sweetness taste but the broth here is simply sugar sweet and it feels like a thick concoction of prawn head juice with sugar. Overly pungent like 腥 and not 鲜.

At $18 before GST and service charge for the pao fan, the prawns seems to be the small, regular size, quick freeze type, together with the lala clams.

Hubby ordered the dried version of prawn noodles. Dried noodles was average, like any coffeeshop standard but wait… this is afterall a coffeeshop setting too. No aircon and really, it’s a coffeeshop.

Overall, it’s not worth it. Simply overhyped. Will do better in terms of taste and prawn size with similar concept one at Killiney Road plus… there’s ac there!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Mike Tse
review_text:
This place is legit. People who say it’s “too sweet” doesn’t understand seafood umami. This so called “sweetness” is the natural flavor of shrimp heads and pork bones. This is natural sweetness not sugar!

Sorry but there is a difference. This is really good. I recommend getting it spicy and getting it with thick noodles. The supreme with larger prawns is really good.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Another Big Bite
review_text:
5 Fortune Jumbo Prawn with lovely seasoned yellow noodle mixed Kway Teow in dry version. The 5 fortune comprises jumbo prawns, seafood ball, sliced thick & collar bone pork slices & clams in rich broth is delicious. More Jumbo Prawn in our Paofan (Rice)- very flavorful with the umami seafood rich broth all soaked up by the rice. Crispy batter yet rich marinated juicy tender Har Cheong Gai - prawn paste chicken wings is finger licking good!
Kinda expensive refreshing drinks we ordered but it’s a must to quench our heat -  CALAMANSI Sour Plum & Sour Plum Prune Soda. A must to experience this popular many hours prep prawn rich broth. Dress lightly!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Lin Zhanquan
review_text:
I ordered the Supreme Prawn Noodles and chose the non-spicy prawn broth with dry yellow noodles. The dish came in a piping hot claypot of prawn broth with noodles on the side. The noodles were springy and chewy and very well seasoned with the base. Then came the highlight of the dish - the prawn broth, which comes with 3 prawns, 3 prawn balls, and 2 pork ribs!

With the claypot style, it elevates the flavour and keeps the broth and the food warm throughout the meal! The broth was very savoury and very addictive overall!  Even though the prawns weren't the biggest, they were all very fresh and easy to deshell! The prawn balls were also very chewy with a few chunks of prawns in it and the pork ribs were very tender and flavourful as well. The portion size was definitely more than enough for 1 pax as even though i am considered a big eater, I was stuffed and slightly overwhelmed by the sheer portion.

I also ordered the sotong youtiao which was very crispy on the outside but soft and chewy on the inside, and such complementing dichotomy made the dish very enjoyable to eat.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: oXRYSTALo Ong
review_text:
Donkey and I are obsessed with prawns, so we'd been wanting to try Zhup Zhup by One Prawn & Co for ages, especially since it has a Michelin Bib Gourmand! We finally got a chance to go when we were on our way to the Garmin service center. I had Zhup Zhup by One Prawn & Co saved on our Google Map for a long time. When we got there, we saw they had a pretty big menu, and a lot of people were ordering the clay pot dishes. It's in a coffee shop, but they had a good variety of food, as you can see in the photos Donkey uploaded.

The liver roll was amazing! It was super savory and used pork liver instead of the usual stuff. The owner said we'd like it if we liked pork liver. I don't normally like liver, but even I tried it and thought it was good! There was no weird smell at all, and I actually enjoyed it. The crispy prawn crackers didn't have that oily taste, either. They were clean and tasted great.

For our main dish, we got the claypot prawn noodles, which seemed to be really popular. They had both dry and wet versions, and we went with the wet one. I was surprised that they put the clams, pork ribs, and prawns in their own claypot instead of cooking everything together. The claypot definitely added to the flavor of the whole dish. If we had known that, we would have order the dry version instead.

The Hokkien Mee also came in a claypot, and it tasted so unique. I can't really describe it, but it was different from any Hokkien Mee I've had before.

The owner recommended the Hibiscus Orange drink, and it came in a teapot with two glasses. But it was only lukewarm, and by the time we were halfway through our meal, it was practically cold. That's definitely something they could improve.

Overall, Zhup Zhup by One Prawn & Co is a great place to eat if you like the dishes we talked about. It's definitely worth a visit.

• Food Quality: 4.5/5 - Standout dishes include the liver roll, crispy prawn crackers, claypot prawn noodles, and Hokkien Mee. Unique flavors and fresh ingredients.

• Ambiance: 3.5/5 - Coffee shop setting with a decent variety of dishes.

• Service: 4/5 - Friendly owner with good recommendations.

• Drinks: 2/5 - Hibiscus Orange beverage was served lukewarm and became cold quickly.

• Overall: 4/5 - Recommended for those who enjoy prawn dishes and unique flavors.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Chan Veronica
review_text:
The broth really surprised me. I went in with normal expectations, but the moment I took the first sip, I could taste how naturally rich it was.

The sweetness doesn’t feel artificial, It’s the kind that comes from real prawn flavour, slowly cooked until the depth really comes through. It has that comforting warmth that makes you pause for a second and go, “Wah… this is good.”

What I like most is that it’s not overly salty or heavy. Even after finishing the whole bowl, it doesn’t leave that jelak feeling. Instead, the broth is clean yet full-bodied, with enough richness to feel satisfying. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Fong Zhi Yen
review_text: Broth was thick with aroma and overall portion size is huge, worth what you’re paying for! The pork rib meat is soft and tender and the seafood was sweet and well-cooked! Other than just the food, will recommend you to try their home made drinks. Was refreshing and didn’t taste too sweet at all!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Aw Yao Feng
review_text:
This has got to be an undisputed winner for prawn noodles. The soup is just like a good “Tonkatsu” equivalent to ramen - but in this case, it’s a thick creamy prawn broth simmering in a hot clay pot with really adds to the flavour of the overall dish.

The portion was worth the price tag, with 3 big fresh prawns and 2 meaty/lean pork ribs, can’t get any better with proper and fresh ingredients!

Highly recommend if you are craving any prawn noodles and you definitely won’t be disappointed with making a stop here! 💪🏼

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Victoria Ho
review_text:
Had a really good meal at Zhup Zhup — no wonder they’re a Michelin Bib Gourmand awardee! The flavours were bold yet comforting, and you can really taste the effort that goes into their rich, umami-packed broth.

Here’s what we tried:
🍜 Dry Five Fortune Jumbo Prawn Mee / Kway Teow Mix – packed with wok hei and generous tiger prawns
🍲 Jumbo Prawn Paofan – warm, comforting, and full of seafood flavour
🍗 Har Cheong Gai – super crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside
🥤 Calamansi Sour Plum Soda – bright and refreshing
🥤 Sour Plum Prune Soda – a great balance of sweet, salty, and tangy

Service was quick and friendly, and the food came out piping hot. Highly recommend Zhup Zhup if you love prawn noodles, hearty broths, and comforting local flavours done right! 🦐✨

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Raymond Yee
review_text:
Michelin Bib-Gourmand Zhup Zhup — Local Comfort, Levelled Up

Where prawn broth turns into poetry, and “zhup zhup” becomes the sound of satisfaction.

📍 Zhup Zhup (formerly One Prawn & Co) is all about tradition meeting innovation — think soul-warming broths, luxurious seafood, and the kind of local flavours that make you smile after every slurp.

🔥 What we tried (and loved):
🍜 JFive Fortune Jumbo Prawn ($30++) — packed with lala, shabu pork, tobiko prawn ball, and pork ribs in that GAOGAO prawn broth. It’s rich, savoury, and full of depth — every sip screams umami.
🦞 Jumbo Lobster Paofan ($88++) — an indulgent bowl with a whole wild-caught spiny lobster, egg floss, and clams poached in their signature broth. Fresh, meaty, and a total must-try for lobster lovers.
🍗 Har Cheong Gai (5pcs, $11) — crispy, juicy, and seasoned just right.
🥢 Tasting Platter ($9) — perfect for sharing and sampling.

🥤 Don’t miss the drinks:
🌿 Pandan Lemongrass ($5++) – refreshing, earthy, and soothing.
🌾 Barley ($4++) – simple and cooling (a bit diluted).

💭 My take: If you love rich prawn broths and hearty local flavours, Zhup Zhup will hit you right in the feels.

⭐ Rating: 4/5 – A comforting, flavour-packed meal worth gathering your makan kakis for.

#ZhupZhupSG #SingaporeFoodie #BibGourmandSG #PrawnNoodlesSG #LobsterPaofan #SeafoodLoversSG #SingaporeEats #FoodieSingapore #SGFoodies #SingaporeRestaurants #ComfortFoodSG #ZhupZhup

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: johnnykuochung
review_text:
So I saw these zhup zhup prawn noodles blowing up on TikTok... and I had to try them! Here’s what happened. 🍲
I ordered the SUPREME PRAWN NOODLES three plump prawns, two tender pork ribs, lala (clams), and a generous portion of pork meat, plus an ice lemon tea to wash it all down.
🔸 The Noodles: I’m a bee hoon fan, so I went for that. The texture was perfect slightly chewy, and it soaked up the broth like a sponge. And the broth... oh man, it had that zhup zhup vibe. Thick, hearty, and packed with deep flavor salty, slightly sweet, and oh-so-satisfying. It wasn’t greasy either, just a touch of oil to make it rich.
🔸 The Prawns: Fresh and juicy! But honestly, I was hoping for a little more tenderness. They were solid but didn’t wow me.
🔸 The Tea: 🍋 Complete letdown. Watered-down tea with a sad lemon slice. No refreshing kick just bland. I’d rather grab a Pokka or Ant Band ice lemon tea.
💸 For nearly $30, I felt okay about it. The broth was definitely the highlight, but the prawns and the tea didn’t really justify the price.
Would I recommend it? 🤔 If you’re a fan of rich broths and don’t mind splurging a little, it’s worth a try. But if you’re looking for a more balanced, satisfying meal there are better options out there.

"If you're into food reviews like this, make sure to follow me on Instagram @Johnnykuochung for more delicious food adventures!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: aindrila karmakar
review_text: Tried the new Jumbo Menu at Michelin Bib-Gourmand Zhup Zhup and it was amazing! The Five Fortune Jumbo Prawn Noodles came loaded with tiger prawns, lala, pork ribs, shabu pork, and their signature prawn ball in rich broth – super flavourful and satisfying. The Jumbo Prawn Paofan was comforting with clams, egg floss, and plump prawns. We also had the Har Cheong Gai wings which were crispy and juicy. Drinks like Calamansi Sourplum and Yuzu Soda were refreshing and paired well with the food. Great portions, quality ingredients, and a must-try for seafood lovers in Singapore.

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Zheng Yan Tan
review_text:
The new branding Zhup Zhup is very apt. The soup literally tastes as good as a rich prawn zhup! So full of flavour and umami. The dry prawn mee is tossed in a fragrant chilli paste with just the right kick. The prawns are fresh and plump, the noodles have a nice springy bite, and the portion is generous. From the noodles and pork slices to the lard bits, everything comes together so well.

I also ordered a sharing ngo hiang plate for fun, and it really surprised me. The tofu, prawn cracker all done nicely, tasty and super crispy as if they are specialise in ngo hiangs!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: Wan Qing Leck
review_text: Perfect meal to have on a cool evening! Thoroughly enjoyed both the orders. The classic prawn noodles soup had a thick tasty broth and the kwayteow was soft yet chewy. Shout out to the classic prawn soup with pork ribs - it had a sweet lingering taste on top of the already delicious broth. The prawns were also fresh and the ribs were tender. The coffee shop space is also newly renovated making it comfortable and clean to dine at. Will recommend!

restaurant: Zhup Zhup | Prawn noodle | Hokkien Mee | Pao Fan
author: TheSeanEdit
review_text:
Tried their prawn noodles and hokkien mee. Prawn noodles’ broth was very sweet due to the prawns, bones and other secret ingredients. I love how they separated the noodles in a bowl from its soup of goodness. Will go back just for that.

Hokkien mee was generous in prawn serving. It doesn’t come with lime for that tangy complete taste. Can tell good broth was used but felt a little flat and too mushy.

Overall, I will swing by again to try it again.
